question: An inverted wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskite solar cell shows a weaker light-induced photoluminescence redshift than the corresponding bare film, yet the complete device develops increasing current-voltage hysteresis and an AgI signature at the silver electrode during prolonged illumination. Explain how these observations can coexist. Build a mechanistic argument that links carrier extraction, halide redistribution, the metal contact, and the limits of photoluminescence as a stability metric. Conclude with one decisive experiment that would test your explanation.

A qualification team proposes replacing a repeated 12 h light/12 h dark stress test for a wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskite top cell with a single continuous-illumination exposure of equal total light dose. Critique this substitution and design the smallest defensible experiment that can determine whether the material undergoes cycle-dependent structural fatigue rather than only reversible halide demixing. Specify the controls, the cycle-resolved observables, the pass/fail logic, and two material or device interventions that would directly target the diagnosed failure modes.

A technoeconomic model for an integrated tandem photoelectrode predicts a low manufacturing cost per square meter, but hydrogen cost remains unacceptable unless operational lifetime increases from hundreds of hours to roughly multi-year service. Propose a design-transfer and qualification plan that prioritizes the protection layer, catalyst support, and current-collection bond without damaging the buried tandem. Your plan must include coupled-stress testing, diagnostic metrics that separate catalytic from photovoltaic degradation, and a quantitative decision rule for whether a design change is economically meaningful.

A recovery process based on short thermal delamination, polar-aprotic solvent cleaning, ultrasonication, and top-cell redeposition works for a silicon-heterojunction bottom cell. Determine whether the same process should be transferred to TOPCon or PERC bottom cells. Formulate a go/no-go framework that covers architecture-specific chemical and thermal compatibility, cleanliness and functional-performance gates, repeated-recycling behavior, and environmental/process-scale consequences.

A treatment increases the open-circuit voltage and fill factor of a wide-bandgap Sn-perovskite top cell without measurably changing its bandgap. Explain the conditions under which those gains will translate into higher power conversion efficiency in a monolithic Sn-perovskite/CIGS tandem, and the conditions under which they will be lost. Then design a subcell-resolved aging experiment that separates top-cell chemical degradation from recombination-layer, optical-current-matching, and CIGS-bottom-cell limitations.

After a buried electron-contact treatment in an n-i-p CsPbI3 solar cell, the transient photocurrent decay becomes substantially faster, whereas the time-resolved photoluminescence lifetime becomes longer. At the same time, the absorber bandgap and short-circuit current remain essentially unchanged, while open-circuit voltage and fill factor increase. Explain why the two transient observations are not contradictory, infer the dominant device improvement, and identify one measurement artifact or alternative explanation that must be controlled before accepting that inference.

A dual-interface strategy combines improved molecular coverage at the buried hole contact with a bulky-ammonium-derived, vacuum-annealed 2D/3D top interface. It performs well in small cells during 55 °C maximum-power-point tracking in nitrogen. Design a factorial validation program for transfer to a 100 cm² module operated at 85 °C under illumination and humid air. The program must determine separately whether degradation originates from buried-contact coverage, thermochemical instability or ion migration in the top treatment, or scale-induced coating nonuniformity. Specify controls, stress conditions, spatial or operando diagnostics, and one defensible go/no-go rule.

A new buried interlayer inserted between a SAM/oxide hole contact and a perovskite changes the water contact angle from approximately 90° to 40°, shifts the contact work function by about 0.2 eV, lengthens the apparent bulk carrier lifetime, raises QFLS, and improves both open-circuit voltage and fill factor. The authors claim that one interfacial dipole explains every improvement. Critique that claim and design an orthogonal control set that can deconvolve four possible contributions: wetting/nucleation, chemical defect passivation, electrostatic energy alignment, and reduced effective contact area. State the outcome pattern needed to assign causality to each contribution.

A three-cell lead-free antimony-based minimodule shows an open-circuit voltage close to three times that of one cell and retains 90% of its initial efficiency for more than 1600 h in unencapsulated dark ambient storage. A company concludes that the technology is ready for outdoor deployment. Evaluate this conclusion and design the minimum qualification sequence needed to separate successful series interconnection, shelf stability, operational stability, and manufacturability. Include laser-scribe diagnostics, module-area accounting, accelerated stresses, and rules for interpreting failure.

An all-inorganic CsPbI3-xBrx film is modified with a thermally reconfigurable low-dimensional framework. Calculations indicate that aggregated iodide vacancies destabilize the black perovskite phase far more strongly than the small lattice distortion introduced by the framework. Design a falsification-oriented diagnostic strategy, using at least three orthogonal measurements, to establish whether the improved phase stability is caused primarily by suppression of vacancy accumulation rather than by static strain stabilization.

You want to transfer the concept of a thermally reconfigurable defect-buffering framework to a wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskite used as a tandem top cell. Define a go/no-go screening workflow that distinguishes a useful dynamic defect buffer from a merely insulating low-dimensional overlayer. What properties and stress tests must a candidate pass before scale-up?

A porous carbon-electrode perovskite cell shows high apparent PCE at a very fast J-V scan, much lower PCE near steady state, and a nonmonotonic current bump at an intermediate scan rate. Its capacitance rises sharply under illumination and relaxes in the dark. Construct a kinetic explanation with at least two coupled state variables, and specify experiments that would distinguish interfacial ion accumulation from a simple RC or instrument artifact.

A molecular treatment lowers the perovskite surface work function and quenches photoluminescence only after the hole-transport layer is deposited, while neat-film PLQY-derived quasi-Fermi-level splitting and TRPL remain nearly unchanged. Explain why the PL quenching is non-diagnostic, and specify a measurement chain that would prove improved hole selectivity from corrected band bending rather than the creation of new traps.

An organic hole-transport material gives stronger steady-state PL quenching and a shorter perovskite TRPL lifetime than two molecular analogues, while also exhibiting lower energetic disorder and higher film conductivity. Explain why the optical observations alone do not prove lower interfacial recombination. Build a measurement logic that separates (i) faster hole transfer, (ii) reduced transport loss inside the hole-transport layer, and (iii) lower nonradiative recombination at the perovskite/HTM interface. Predict the result pattern for a genuinely superior HTM.

On glass, a molecular modifier causes higher perovskite PL intensity and a longer TRPL lifetime; on SnO2, the same modifier causes lower PL intensity and a shorter lifetime. XPS indicates coordination to undercoordinated Sn sites, and UPS indicates a smaller energetic offset at the electron-selective contact. Explain why the substrate-dependent PL trends can be mutually consistent rather than contradictory. What minimum controls are required to distinguish improved electron extraction from newly introduced interfacial quenching?

A planar perovskite device uses both a buried SnO2 modifier and an independent top-surface passivation layer. Design a factorial experiment that can assign gains in open-circuit voltage, hysteresis, and aging resistance to the buried treatment rather than to the top treatment or their interaction. Specify the device groups, primary mechanistic readouts, and how you would test whether reduced metal/halide migration is causal rather than merely correlated with slower degradation.

You are selecting a polymeric additive for a Sn-Pb absorber intended for a monolithic tandem module. Define a materials-selection and qualification framework that preserves the mechanical benefits of grain-boundary localization without sacrificing charge transport, crystallization, or Sn2+ chemical stability. Include at least one concentration-dependent failure mode and a coupled-stress protocol more realistic than dark thermal cycling alone.

Introducing a wide-bandgap low-dimensional additive into an n approximately 5 quasi-2D perovskite improves vertical orientation, reduces trap density, and raises open-circuit voltage and fill factor. Design a causal experiment to determine whether the dominant benefit is (a) templated crystallization/orientation, (b) redistribution of n-phase populations, or (c) grain-boundary electronic passivation. Use perturbations and predicted readouts that distinguish the three mechanisms rather than merely listing characterization methods.

An inverted perovskite solar cell uses ALD-NiOx as the hole-selective contact. After inserting an anchored molecular interlayer, the hole-only contact resistance and valence-band extraction barrier both decrease, while the perovskite-side-excited TRPL lifetime of an incomplete NiOx/interlayer/perovskite stack becomes longer. Trap-density measurements also decrease and KPFM shows a narrower contact-potential distribution. Explain why the longer lifetime is not inconsistent with faster hole extraction. Assign the observations to defect-passivation and energetic/transport mechanisms, and specify one measurement geometry or control that is essential for separating these effects.

A phosphonic-acid molecular bridge gives excellent small-area inverted perovskite cells on ALD-NiOx, but it must now be transferred to slot-die-coated modules. At large area, both incomplete molecular coverage and multilayer aggregation can produce local shunts, energetic disorder, or nonuniform crystallization. Define a process-window strategy and a minimum validation package that would demonstrate that the layer still functions as an anchored molecular bridge rather than merely as a wetting additive. Your answer must include controls, spatially resolved diagnostics, and a stability test that is relevant to operation.

A coordinating additive improves a tin-perovskite device, but the available durability evidence consists only of nitrogen-glovebox storage and a short maximum-power-point test. Design an accelerated validation matrix that can distinguish three possible origins of the apparent stability gain: suppression of Sn2+ oxidation and self-doping, improved contact energetics, and a one-time crystallization/morphology benefit. Specify the control structure, stress conditions, time-resolved readouts, and the pattern of results that would support each mechanism.

Two approximately 20-micrometer-thick single-crystal perovskite absorbers are tested in the same inverted device stack. The methylammonium-free crystal has a slightly smaller bandgap, a red-shifted EQE edge, stronger PL, a longer TRPL lifetime, a lower light-intensity ideality factor, and both higher Jsc and higher Voc. Explain how the photocurrent and voltage gains should be partitioned. In particular, why is a higher Voc not paradoxical for the smaller-bandgap absorber, and which normalized quantities would you compare to prove the origin of the voltage gain?

A residual-solvent-management strategy works in spin-coated cells and must be transferred to a 100 cm2 flexible slot-die-coated module, where coating speed, web temperature, air flow, and edge-to-center evaporation gradients differ strongly from small substrates. Propose a manufacturing control strategy and quantitative acceptance criteria that would demonstrate uniform solvent removal without sacrificing the beneficial wet-film intermediate. Include spatial metrology, module-level electrical validation, and a durability protocol appropriate to the lower thermal budget of a flexible substrate.

You must transfer fast coevaporation of a micrometer-thick hybrid perovskite from a small laboratory chamber to a meter-scale in-line tool. The inorganic precursor flux is comparatively stable, but the organic precursor flux depends nonlinearly on source temperature, source depletion, precursor batch, chamber pressure, and substrate position. Design a closed-loop control and qualification strategy that can preserve composition and thickness at four-times or higher throughput. The answer must address spatial nonuniformity, sensor drift, source transients, and the criteria for deciding that a faster rate is manufacturable rather than merely achievable for one champion device.

During high-temperature spin coating of an FA-rich perovskite, a strongly coordinating Lewis-base additive produces a persistent intermediate-phase signal, delays the PL and absorption transition to the bulk perovskite, and yields fewer cracks. The proposed explanation is not only slower nucleation, but that spatially distributed intermediate adducts act as physical barriers that prevent nuclei collision and solute-depletion cracking. Explain why time-delayed PL, absorption, or XRD alone cannot distinguish these two mechanisms. Design a falsifiable experiment and state the observations that would specifically support the physical-barrier mechanism over a simple uniform slowing of crystallization.

You must choose between two stabilization strategies for a mixed-halide tandem top cell: (A) increase effective A-site steric bulk, which may perturb phase stability and bandgap, or (B) introduce a low-concentration molecule that mainly passivates halide vacancies but has uncertain bulk incorporation. Design a go/no-go screening workflow for prolonged simultaneous light-and-heat operation. Explain which kinetic, optical, structural, and device metrics must agree before assigning success to slower ion migration, and how you would reject a formulation that only masks segregation transiently.

After a low-dimensional precursor solution is coated onto 3D FAPbI3, a distinct excitonic PL peak appears and cross-sectional microscopy shows a top layer. These observations alone cannot distinguish deterministic bilayer deposition from partial dissolution-reprecipitation or in situ cation exchange. Construct an evidence hierarchy that would discriminate the three mechanisms, and explain how low-dimensional orientation and vacuum-level bending should be linked to opposite extraction requirements in n-i-p and p-i-n devices.

A binary orthogonal solvent forms an optimal quasi-2D/3D interface by spin coating, but scale-up requires blade coating and laser-scribed modules. Design a process-window study that jointly optimizes solvent orthogonality, wetting and drying, low-dimensional phase number and thickness, and architecture-specific energetics. Which module-level tests would prove that improved stability comes from ion blocking or interfacial crosslinking rather than simply better encapsulation?

An additive-treated perovskite film and an untreated control have the same grain size, similar Williamson-Hall microstrain, and indistinguishable initial buried-interface toughness. Only the treated devices retain efficiency after thermal cycling. The treated film has near-zero macroscopic biaxial residual stress, whereas the control is tensile; after cycling, the control shows cracking, delamination, lower interface toughness, and loss of diffraction intensity. Explain why this pattern supports residual-stress-mediated fatigue rather than initial adhesion, grain-size, microstrain, or phase-change explanations, and identify one important measurement limitation that must be addressed.

A completed n-i-p perovskite device receives a low-temperature ALD exposure after the metal electrode has been deposited. The treatment raises VOC by about 65 mV and electroluminescence quantum yield by roughly one order of magnitude, while JSC changes little. One hypothesis is that the metal-organic precursor penetrates a porous doped hole-transport layer and creates a thin PbI2-rich passivating region at the buried perovskite/HTL interface; competing hypotheses are thermal/vacuum conditioning and a top-surface oxide barrier. Design a falsification matrix that can distinguish these mechanisms.

A post-assembly infiltrative passivation process developed for porous, doped spiro-OMeTAD must be transferred to a large-area module that uses a dense dopant-free polymer HTL and a more corrosion-sensitive electrode. Define a process-window and go/no-go qualification that decides whether to retain post-assembly infiltration, move the reactive chemistry before HTL deposition, or abandon the approach.

You plan to transfer DC-poling-induced ferroelastic restructuring from MAPbI3 to a 1.7-1.8 eV mixed I/Br perovskite tandem top cell. The same field that moves twin boundaries may also drive halide segregation and ionic accumulation. Define a safe poling window and a go/no-go test that demonstrates a persistent ferroelastic benefit without creating a metastable compositional artifact.

A batch perovskite/Pt film produces hydrogen from methanol vapor, but its rate collapses after roughly 10 h and can be partly recovered by renewed Pt deposition. Design a continuous-flow development and qualification protocol that distinguishes Pt detachment/contact evolution, perovskite decomposition, product poisoning, and vapor-transport artifacts before any scalable-stability claim is made.

A Pb-Sn perovskite/C60 interface is treated with EDA plus a series of carboxylic acids that share the same headgroup but have progressively longer alkyl chains. Predict a nonmonotonic relationship among interfacial PLQY, VOC, JSC, and FF, and design a diagnostic set that separates metal coordination, surface doping, physical separation from C60, and electron-tunneling resistance.

A large-area all-perovskite tandem retains the high VOC of an EDA/long-chain-ligand-treated Pb-Sn subcell, but shows a wide spatial spread in FF and early maximum-power decay. Construct a failure-analysis and scale-up gate that distinguishes nonuniform ligand coverage, excessive interfacial resistance, renewed Sn oxidation, and tandem optical/current-matching effects.

An industrial team wants to scale a humidity-assisted hybrid perovskite conversion process from square-centimeter coupons to full textured silicon wafers. Across the wafer, relative humidity, temperature, pyramid height, and absorber thickness are not perfectly uniform. Propose a process-control and qualification strategy that preserves moisture-assisted buried conversion without increasing humidity-driven decomposition. Identify the control variables, an endpoint or trigger for switching process stages, and the minimum film and device diagnostics required before the recipe is transferred to manufacturing.

A 500 nm halide-perovskite film is measured at sufficiently low injection that bimolecular and Auger recombination are negligible. Its TRPL shows three features: (i) a faster early decay under 405-470 nm excitation than under 640 nm excitation, (ii) a much smaller wavelength dependence after surface passivation, and (iii) a lower stretched-exponential beta when the detection region of interest is enlarged. Construct a mechanistic interpretation that separates vertical from lateral heterogeneity, and state how the data should be modeled without assigning arbitrary physical meaning to biexponential components.

An iodide-rich treatment slows humidity-driven phase conversion in a CsPbI3 model film, but it must now be integrated into a complete solar cell. Propose a transfer protocol that determines whether the treatment improves operational stability rather than merely delaying a dark, open-circuit film transition. Include chemical and electronic controls, operando stress conditions, and explicit criteria that would disqualify the treatment.

A solution-processed small-molecule HTM gives a much higher Pe-QLED EQE than two analogues. Relative to the controls, it survives the nonpolar quantum-dot ink solvent, forms a smoother film, has a shallower HOMO and higher hole mobility, and its QD/HTM bilayer shows fewer traps and a longer photoluminescence lifetime. Design orthogonal experiments that determine how much of the EQE gain comes from (i) solvent-orthogonal film integrity, (ii) hole injection and transport, and (iii) interfacial defect passivation. For each proposed perturbation, state the result that would support or falsify the assigned mechanism.

A methoxy-functionalized small-molecule HTM performs well in a green Pe-QLED, but a first blue-device demonstration has lower EQE and the green devices survive only minutes under an ambient operational test. Define the molecular-design, interface-engineering, and reliability evidence required before claiming that the HTM platform is transferable to blue high-brightness displays. Explain why simply increasing hole mobility or making the HOMO shallower may worsen the blue device.

A molecular donor is applied after deposition to a p-type Sn-Pb perovskite. XRD is unchanged, surface-sensitive Sn core levels shift while Pb core levels do not, the oxidized fraction of the donor increases, Hall analysis reports an almost order-of-magnitude drop in hole density, conductivity falls strongly with only a modest mobility change, and a p-i-n device gains voltage and current. Design a depth- and geometry-resolved experiment set that decides whether the dominant effect is bulk molecular doping, surface/grain-boundary compensation, trap passivation, or modification of the electron-contact interface. State the scaling behavior expected for each case.

A post-deposition compensating molecular dopant improves a Sn-rich p-i-n perovskite at moderate dose, but further dose reduction of the hole density is accompanied by surface build-up, fill-factor loss, mobility degradation, and greater air sensitivity. Construct a dose-process-stress optimization framework for transferring this treatment to a micrometer-thick absorber and then to a large-area module. Define the stopping criteria that prevent useful compensation from becoming an insulating or unstable interlayer.

A mixed Br/I quasi-2D perovskite develops a new red-shifted photoluminescence band during illumination and partially recovers in the dark. Build a diagnostic decision tree that distinguishes (a) reversible photoinduced halide segregation, (b) intrinsic compositional immiscibility or site preference already present before illumination, and (c) irreversible redox-coupled halide expulsion. Include controls that prevent X-ray or ion-beam characterization from creating the phenomenon being measured.

A carbonyl-containing additive binds PbI2 more strongly than DMSO and lowers the final trap density. At moderate loading it produces fewer nuclei, faster conversion during annealing, and larger grains; at higher loading it instead delays conversion, leaves residual intermediate or PbI2, and produces smaller grains. Explain why coordination stronger than the solvent can be necessary but still not sufficient for useful growth regulation. Design an experiment set that locates the beneficial coordination window and separates crystallization control from post-growth defect passivation.

A molecular additive selected for a DMF/DMSO spin-coated two-step perovskite process must be transferred to large-area blade coating that uses NMP or another slower-evaporating coordinating solvent. Develop a recalibration strategy for molecular selection and process conditions. Your answer should explain why an absolute additive-PbI2 binding energy is not a portable design rule and should define the measurements needed to prevent drying gradients, residual adducts, or passivation loss across the coated area.

Epitaxial strain converts a nitride perovskite from an indirect to a direct 1.70 eV bandgap. The strained phase nevertheless retains a nonbonding N-2p valence-band maximum, a transition-metal-d conduction-band minimum with negligible spin-orbit splitting, hole effective masses above 1 m0, a weak near-edge optical transition matrix element, and a low-formation-energy nitrogen vacancy with a deep donor level. Is direct-gap conversion sufficient to make this material a lead-halide-like photovoltaic absorber? Build a causal diagnosis that separately addresses photon absorption, carrier transport, and non-radiative recombination.

A submicrometer MAPbI3 monocrystal film has much weaker steady-state photoluminescence than a polycrystalline control, yet it also shows longer TRPL components, lower SCLC trap density, faster transient photocurrent extraction, slower transient-photovoltage recombination, and a higher device fill factor. A student concludes that the monocrystal must have more non-radiative recombination because it is dimmer. Diagnose the error, interpret the complete measurement set, and name at least two controls required before assigning the PL-intensity difference to intrinsic material quality.

A monolithic, fully textured perovskite/silicon tandem uses a wide-bandgap perovskite top cell that performs well on planar witness substrates. After integration, the tandem retains nearly the same open-circuit voltage but loses both short-circuit current and fill factor. Subcell EQE shows current mismatch, electroluminescence imaging reveals localized dark regions, and cross-sectional microscopy shows a thinner perovskite layer at silicon-pyramid valleys. Construct a ranked diagnosis and specify measurements or process perturbations that would distinguish optical mismatch, nonconformal coating/interface recombination, and a resistive or optically lossy interconnecting layer.

An industrial team must choose an interconnecting layer for a perovskite/silicon tandem. Candidate A has lower initial sheet resistance but requires sputtering that can damage the perovskite; Candidate B is solution-processed and gentle but absorbs more near-infrared light and softens during thermal cycling. Define a decision and qualification framework that can select between them for commercialization, and explain why the lowest initial series resistance is not a sufficient criterion.

An additive reduces conventional JV hysteresis to nearly zero, but under stabilized maximum-power-point operation the photocurrent still drifts downward over several seconds while synchronized photoluminescence rises. Should the additive be considered to have solved mobile-ion-induced losses? Define acceptance criteria and propose material or device changes that target the actual loss mechanism rather than the appearance of a fast JV scan.

Increasing the dose of a fluorinated phenethylammonium-iodide treatment makes an inverted perovskite film brighter and lengthens its TRPL lifetime, but the complete device loses both fill factor and short-circuit current. GIWAXS shows a stronger low-q perovskite-quantum-well peak with a broad azimuthal distribution, while XRD shows increasing n=1 phase content. Diagnose the most likely failure and explain how to distinguish useful defect passivation from formation of an electrically blocking, misoriented low-n quantum-well layer.

Design a scale-up and durability qualification plan for a fluorinated-spacer PQW/3D surface treatment intended for large-area inverted perovskite modules. The plan must preserve both surface and grain-boundary passivation without sacrificing vertical charge transport, and it must distinguish true durability from normalized-PCE retention in small unencapsulated cells.

An acidic fluoride treatment is applied to an oxide electron-transport layer before perovskite deposition. The treated devices show nearly unchanged absorption and short-circuit current, but higher open-circuit voltage and fill factor, much lower J-V hysteresis, stronger interfacial photoluminescence, a lower oxide hydroxyl signal, a new fluoride signal, and a modest work-function shift. These observations are consistent with at least three coupled effects: proton-assisted removal of oxide hydroxyls, fluoride-induced passivation/energetic tuning of the oxide, and fluoride-mediated passivation of undercoordinated Pb or organic-cation vacancies at the perovskite bottom surface. Design the smallest convincing control-and-measurement matrix that can separate these three contributions. State the predicted signature of each mechanism and specify what result would falsify an explanation based on bulk fluoride alloying of the absorber.

A manufacturer wants to transfer an oxide/perovskite fluoride-passivation concept from a laboratory mesoporous TiO2 cell to a low-temperature planar SnO2 process on flexible substrates. Direct hydrofluoric-acid soaking is rejected for safety and equipment-compatibility reasons. A benign fluoride-containing primer gives an initial Voc gain, but after light-bias aging the cell develops an S-shaped J-V curve and fluoride becomes detectable away from the buried interface. Formulate a redesign and validation plan that preserves the useful interfacial chemistry while preventing transport barriers and mobile-ion instability. Include molecular/process design rules, architecture-specific controls, accelerated stresses, and a defensible rejection criterion.

An ultrathin modifier is inserted at a SnO2/perovskite buried interface. The device gains 45 mV in open-circuit voltage and shows higher glass-side PLQY, but Jsc and fill factor fall; top-view SEM and the absorber optical gap are unchanged. Four explanations remain plausible: reduced buried-interface recombination accompanied by a new extraction barrier, altered bottom-side crystallization/wetting, increased series resistance from an insulating interlayer, or strain-induced transport degradation. Build a falsifiable diagnostic decision tree for this inaccessible interface. Specify the complementary measurements required, the signature expected for each explanation, and the evidence needed before claiming that a buried-interface dipole or band offset is the dominant cause. What observation would most strongly falsify that energetic-barrier claim?

You must select a buried-interface modifier for the perovskite top cell of a flexible tandem mini-module. Four candidate concepts have similar small-area PCE: (A) a hygroscopic alkali-halide salt with strong trap passivation, (B) a polymer that improves wetting and adhesion but has low vertical conductivity, (C) a conductive fullerene or 2D-material interlayer that can aggregate, and (D) a self-formed perovskite-related coherent layer whose formation is sensitive to precursor stoichiometry. Construct a multi-stage selection funnel that does not rank candidates by champion PCE. The funnel must cover electronic, chemical, crystallization, mechanical, optical and scale-up criteria, and must specify how a candidate advances from coupon cells to a flexible tandem mini-module under combined stress.

A polar-solvent-compatible fullerene is introduced into a normal-structure perovskite cell by three routes at matched total loading: homogeneous precursor mixing, coating it on the electron-transport layer immediately before perovskite deposition, and coating it on the electron-transport layer followed by a short waiting period with the wet precursor. Homogeneous mixing mainly increases Voc, whereas the waiting route mainly increases fill factor and electron mobility. Design a falsifiable evidence chain showing that a bottom-enriched vertical fullerene gradient, rather than total fullerene amount, gross morphology or a uniform bulk additive effect, causes the waiting-route improvement. Include depth-distribution controls, spatially selective electronic measurements and a perturbation that should reverse or erase the effect.

The bottom-gradient fullerene strategy must be adapted to high-throughput slot-die coating, where a one-minute waiting step is impractical. The chosen fullerene has good polar-solvent miscibility but a glass-transition temperature near 50 °C, while the module may operate at 70-85 °C. Propose a molecular and process redesign that creates the required bottom enrichment during continuous coating and locks it against thermal or bias-driven redistribution. Explain how you would balance miscibility, energy levels, anchoring, diffusion and conductivity, and define the scale-up and stability experiments needed to prove that the gradient remains functional.

A multifunctional precursor additive produces 23%-class small cells by ambient blade coating, but transfer to a 100 cm² mini-module gives a large fill-factor loss and edge-first degradation when relative humidity fluctuates. Propose an integrated molecular, coating and module-validation strategy that preserves useful precursor interactions while separating additive chemistry from large-area hydrodynamic and interconnection losses. The plan must address additive dose/interaction strength, spatial drying control, electrical loss mapping, moisture and thermal degradation pathways, and the evidence required before attributing module stability to defect passivation.

A 1.75-1.80 eV mixed-halide perovskite deposited on flexible PEN/ITO shows a high quasi-Fermi-level splitting in a contact-free reference stack, yet complete devices have a substantially lower and highly variable open-circuit voltage. Comparison stacks containing the buried hole-selective contact show spatial luminescence dark patches that are absent from the reference; adding a fullerene electron-transport layer produces further nonuniform photoluminescence loss, while the optical bandgap and external quantum efficiency remain essentially unchanged. A mild bulky-ammonium chloride surface treatment then increases photoluminescence lifetime and open-circuit voltage with little change in short-circuit current. Diagnose the dominant loss channels and specify the minimum evidence needed to distinguish incomplete buried-contact coverage, top-interface energetic or recombination loss, and light-induced bulk halide phase segregation.

A molecular interlayer improves shelf retention, humidity tolerance, maximum-power-point retention, and bending endurance in unencapsulated inverted cells. However, treated and control devices were not tracked for the same MPPT duration, and water contact angle is the principal moisture-related descriptor. Design a validation matrix that can establish whether the interlayer separately suppresses chemical decomposition, interfacial delamination, and bias-driven ion or electrode degradation. Define the evidence required before the result can be transferred to large-area flexible devices.

An ultrathin polymer/ITO electrode becomes more foldable because reducing substrate thickness lowers the outer-fiber strain at a fixed bending radius, but sputter-induced residual stress curls the free laminate so severely that device fabrication is impossible. A stiff oxide layer deposited on the back side makes the laminate flat. Explain why anti-curling and crack resistance are not the same design problem. Using qualitative laminate mechanics, predict how polymer thickness, back-oxide thickness and modulus, and neutral-axis position affect initial curvature and cyclic ITO strain, and state the measurements that distinguish true stress compensation from merely forcing the sheet flat on a carrier.

An embedded metal-mesh/ultrathin-ITO electrode is being scaled from laboratory cells to a laser-scribed foldable perovskite module. Propose a co-optimization strategy for mesh geometry, oxide thickness, planarization, neutral-plane protection, and P1/P2/P3 interconnects. Identify four coupled trade-offs and the module-level tests needed to prevent a transparent-conductor coupon that performs well initially but fails after folding.

Fluorinating a bulky spacer for a nominal n = 4 quasi-2D perovskite increases its molecular dipole and the apparent size of precursor aggregates. The processed film then shows larger grains, stronger preferred orientation, longer photoluminescence lifetime, higher local conductivity, and a device gain dominated by fill factor. Explain why these correlations do not prove a single causal sequence from dipole to aggregation to orientation to transport. Design a discriminating experiment set that separates solution aggregation and nucleation control, direct defect-passivation or electronic effects, and phase-distribution or orientation effects.

A fluorinated quasi-2D spacer produces a more hydrophobic surface and better thermal and illumination retention than a 3D perovskite control, yet under humidity aging its device retention is slightly worse than that of the nonfluorinated quasi-2D analogue. Give a mechanistic explanation for this apparent contradiction and design a spacer-screening protocol that avoids selecting candidates by water contact angle alone.

After selectively passivating the contacts of a perovskite p-i-n solar cell, open-circuit voltage and low-intensity photoluminescence quantum yield increase, but high-fluence transient-absorption decays and the extracted bimolecular recombination coefficient remain nearly unchanged. Using R(n) = k1 n + k2 n^2 + k3 n^3, explain why these observations are mutually consistent. Predict how the differential-lifetime curve, the steady-state carrier density at one-sun open circuit, and the light-intensity dependence of open-circuit voltage should change if the treatment mainly lowers first-order interfacial recombination.

A PAN-containing carbon-electrode mesoscopic cell shows little efficiency loss during a few hundred hours of ambient storage. Before transferring the chemistry to printable modules, design a durability program that determines whether the benefit is genuine suppression of moisture-induced δ-FAPbI3 rather than an artifact of the carbon scaffold, unequal initial efficiency, or simply slower water ingress. Include controls, stresses, spatial diagnostics, and a criterion for successful transfer.

A proposed triple-functional passivator contains a pyridine nitrogen, a carboxylic-acid group, and a fluorine substituent. It is claimed to address undercoordinated Pb2+, FA-related defects, and halide-vacancy-related sites. Design the smallest informative molecular-control library and a measurement logic that can assign each function, while ruling out lattice incorporation and a simple work-function-shift explanation.

A passivator improves Voc and fill factor of a roughly 1.68 eV wide-bandgap perovskite top cell on textured silicon with little change in Jsc. You want to transfer it to a more Br-rich 1.75–1.80 eV top cell. Design a staged experiment that determines whether the defect chemistry and stability truly transfer without corrupting tandem current matching. Define controls, normalization, operando phase-segregation tests, and tandem-level success criteria.

Two carbazole-phosphonic-acid hole-selective layers have nearly the same mean work function and produce perovskites with the same bandgap. One layer forms large solution micelles and a patchy monolayer with about 25 mV nanoscale contact-potential variation; a co-assembled layer forms much smaller aggregates and only about 5 mV variation. The co-assembled layer yields lower perovskite microstrain, less light-induced iodide-rich emission, and higher Voc and fill factor. Explain why the mean work function is an inadequate descriptor, build a causal link from nanoscale HSL heterogeneity to phase segregation, and propose an experiment that changes aggregation while holding molecular composition fixed.

A mixed hole-selective layer suppresses phase segregation in a wide-bandgap perovskite top cell and increases the voltage of a perovskite/organic tandem. The tandem also contains an organic rear subcell and a recombination/interconnection stack, either of which can dominate aging. Design an operational-stability experiment that determines whether the mixed HSL extends tandem lifetime specifically by stabilizing the wide-bandgap perovskite. Include matched devices, operating conditions, operando diagnostics, and a rule for attributing failure.

A wide-bandgap perovskite is examined under identical excitation in three configurations: a pristine bare film, a mildly solvent-reconstructed bare film, and a reconstructed film carrying a fluorinated ionic interlayer. The final bare film shows higher steady-state photoluminescence and a longer decay lifetime than the pristine film, yet depositing C60 on it produces stronger photoluminescence quenching and a faster interfacial decay than the untreated perovskite/C60 stack. At device level, the trap-filled-limit voltage decreases, electron mobility increases, and the light-intensity dependence of Voc approaches an ideality factor of one. Reconcile these observations using competing carrier-rate pathways. State what photoluminescence alone can and cannot establish, and give a minimal control set that distinguishes passivation plus faster extraction from newly introduced nonradiative quenching.

An ultrathin phenethylammonium-halide layer raises Voc in spacer configurations where thin dielectric layers prevent its direct chemical contact with either the perovskite or the hole-transport layer. UPS and Kelvin-probe measurements show a vacuum-level shift, while photoluminescence lifetime increases and the trap-filled-limit voltage decreases. Construct a diagnostic argument that distinguishes an oriented interfacial dipole from direct defect passivation, charge-transfer doping, and generic dielectric-field screening. Which perturbations and signatures would be decisive rather than merely consistent?

A phenethylammonium-derived dipole that improves hole extraction in an n-i-p perovskite device would point in the unfavorable direction at the perovskite/C60 contact of a p-i-n device. Design a transferable interlayer strategy for the inverted architecture. Specify the molecular-orientation logic, processing sequence, and validation tests needed to obtain favorable electron extraction without creating a thick insulating 2D phase or an unstable solvent-dependent dipole.

A wide-bandgap perovskite treated with a mixed methylammonium-thiocyanate and phenethylammonium-iodide solution develops much larger grains and fewer horizontal grain boundaries. After annealing, a weak diffraction feature consistent with an n = 2 layered perovskite remains, but sulfur is no longer detectable. Construct a mechanistic model that distinguishes transient thiocyanate-mediated dissolution/regrowth from permanent thiocyanate passivation or simple phenethylammonium surface capping. Propose time-resolved and control experiments, including the expected outcomes that would support the transient-regrowth model.

A reactive grain-regrowth and bifacial-passivation treatment improves small-area opaque wide-bandgap perovskite cells. It must now be scaled to a large-area semitransparent tandem top cell containing a self-assembled hole contact, C60/SnO2 electron contacts, and a sputtered transparent electrode. Identify the dominant scale-up and stability risks, and design a process-and-diagnostic plan proving that the voltage gain survives area increase without optical, transport, or durability penalties.

At a SnO2/perovskite buried interface, a mixed dipole-plus-passivator interlayer produces the strongest steady-state photoluminescence quenching and the shortest time-resolved photoluminescence lifetime. Those observations could indicate either fast electron extraction or additional nonradiative recombination. Construct a hierarchy of evidence that would discriminate the two explanations using work-function mapping, conductive-AFM, trap-filled-limit measurements, XPS defect chemistry, transient reverse-current behavior, and morphology controls. Which evidence is necessary, and which is only supportive?

An unbiased all-perovskite water-splitting assembly uses a stabilized perovskite photoanode, but system degradation shifts to the photocathode, where electrons travel from SnO2 through a transparent conductor before reaching Pt and accumulate at an internal interface. Redesign the photocathode architecture and propose a component-resolved diagnostic plan that verifies whether the bottleneck has actually moved or been removed. Include electrical, electrochemical, and materials-level acceptance criteria.

Two fullerene electron-transport layers have indistinguishable frontier energy levels and nominal chemical composition, but one is enantiomerically pure and the other racemic. The enantiopure film shows discrete GIWAXS spots, higher electron mobility in an electron-only device, much faster photoluminescence decay when deposited on the perovskite, and higher device Voc and fill factor. Explain why the faster PL decay cannot by itself be labeled improved electron extraction. Construct a mechanism that links molecular packing to device performance, then design the minimum measurements needed to distinguish among higher ETL bulk mobility, faster interfacial transfer, and increased interfacial nonradiative recombination. State the contrasting signatures expected for each case.

A tin-perovskite device containing an acetate-based ionic liquid retains efficiency during unsealed storage and heating in nitrogen, but it must now be transferred to an encapsulated Sn-Pb tandem operating in realistic air. Design a qualification program that can establish true oxidative and operational stability rather than merely hydrophobic surface behavior or delayed crystallization. Your plan must separate oxygen, moisture, light, heat, and electrical bias; track Sn oxidation and mobile-ion redistribution; test compatibility with adjacent transport layers and the tandem interconnect; and end with quantitative acceptance or rejection criteria.

In a laminated perovskite pseudo-module, adding more encapsulant-filled scribes raises double-cantilever-beam fracture energy, and scribes perpendicular to the crack path outperform parallel scribes at a similar area fraction. A silane-grafted polyolefin infiltrates the scribes, while fracture energy increases further after thermal cycling. Develop a mechanistic explanation that separates covalent oxide bonding, crack deflection or bridging, polymer pull-out and viscoelastic dissipation, and post-lamination chemical or morphological evolution. Then propose a control matrix and rate-, temperature-, and orientation-dependent fracture tests that could falsify each proposed contribution rather than merely correlate scribe count with toughness.

A module engineer wants to use silane-bonded, encapsulant-filled P3-like scribes as mechanical anchors in a commercial monolithic perovskite module. Narrower pitch and more transverse anchors may improve crack resistance, but they reduce geometric fill factor, can perturb electrical isolation, may create moisture pathways, and must tolerate scribe-width and registration errors. Formulate a coupled optimization and qualification strategy for scribe width, pitch, orientation, and silane-encapsulant chemistry. Include fracture statistics, electrical and optical penalties, thermal-humidity and mechanical stresses, manufacturing tolerances, and explicit acceptance criteria for commercialization.

You must use a heterogeneous literature database to select a 1.75-1.90 eV perovskite top-cell architecture for a tandem program. Device records differ in composition, transport layers, area, year, scan protocol, and reporting quality, and only a small minority contain stability data. Design a data-analysis and prospective-validation pipeline that avoids selecting the architecture with the highest raw median PCE simply because of publication bias or confounding. Include normalization, stratification or causal adjustment, missing-data treatment, uncertainty and sensitivity analysis, standardized stability evidence, and a final decision rule for advancing a stack to fabrication.

Two grain-boundary additives produce mixed-halide perovskite films with indistinguishable grain size, crystallinity, Urbach energy, trap density, and Pb-defect passivation. Additive A is an asymmetric Lewis base; additive B is a size-matched macrocycle with two negatively polarized portals separated by a positively polarized cavity. Under illumination and electrical bias, only additive B strongly suppresses I/Br demixing. Explain the most plausible additional mechanism and design a decisive experiment set that distinguishes it from residual strain, morphology, or ordinary chemical passivation.

A macrocyclic grain-boundary additive that suppresses halide migration in spin-coated CsPbI2Br cells must be transferred to a slot-die-coated wide-bandgap top cell for a perovskite/silicon tandem. Define the molecular, process, and qualification gates needed to preserve the ion-caging benefit without creating a transport barrier or mistaking moisture protection for intrinsic photostability.

An inverted 2D/3D perovskite solar cell treated with a new ammonium ligand shows higher PLQY and VOC but lower FF. Three explanations are proposed: excessive low-n phase coverage, unfavorable 2D crystallite orientation, and an energetically misaligned but chemically well-passivated interface. Explain how each mechanism can produce this metric combination and design a diagnostic sequence that distinguishes them.

Design a ligand-selection and qualification framework for a blade-coated, inverted wide-bandgap 2D/3D perovskite mini-module that must survive both damp heat and 85 °C maximum-power operation. The framework must balance defect passivation, ion-migration suppression, moisture resistance, vertical transport, and scalable phase control.

A fluorinated low-dimensional perovskite treatment improves the voltage and ambient moisture retention of an FA-rich printable carbon cell, but the device loses performance rapidly at 85 °C because the perovskite/carbon contact mechanically degrades. Propose an interface and scaffold redesign that preserves selective band alignment while mitigating thermomechanical mismatch, and define the experiments required to validate it.

A hot-cast quasi-2D perovskite recipe produces well-oriented quantum wells on a 1 cm2 substrate but fails on a 100 cm2 coated area because temperature, solvent evaporation, and wet-film residence time vary across the web. Design a scale-up strategy that matches the crystallization trajectory rather than copying the nominal hot-casting temperature. Specify the controllable parameters, inline observables, and acceptance criteria for both photovoltaic performance and stability.

A Lewis-base additive coordinates Sn2+ and hydrogen-bonds iodide in a 2D/3D tin perovskite. It improves storage and MPP stability in dry nitrogen, but excessive loading produces pinholes and roughness. Design the minimum real-world stress matrix needed to determine whether the additive truly suppresses intrinsic tin oxidation and defect generation, rather than merely improving morphology under inert conditions. Specify controls, stressors, chemical and electrical readouts, and a go/no-go rule.

A chemically reacted ionic-liquid capping layer improves both small cells and a laser-scribed perovskite module. Identify the scale-up failure modes created by spatial variation in surface PbI2, capping-layer thickness, rough surface crystallites, and P1-P2-P3 scribe regions. Propose an acceptance map that would show the module improvement is a genuine area-wide interface effect rather than the average of a few well-passivated subcells.

A Bayesian optimizer trained on small spin-coated perovskite films uses mean PL intensity and PL uniformity as its targets. It must now be transferred to blade-coated 100 cm2 mini-modules on a pilot line whose humidity and airflow vary between runs. Design a defensible closed-loop transfer strategy that does not simply copy spin speed, antisolvent timing, or nozzle height. Define (i) physically transferable process variables, (ii) a multiobjective response function, (iii) robustness and full-device validation, and (iv) explicit failure criteria for scale-up and stability claims.

Two nominal n = 3 Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite films have similar conventional absorption spectra and comparable surface coverage, yet one gives much lower Jsc and fill factor. The possible causes are: an unfavorable vertical sequence of n-phases, predominantly in-plane quantum wells, or trap-rich lower-n inclusions distributed through the bulk. Construct a diagnostic workflow that can distinguish these cases. Explain what depth-resolved spectroscopy, orientation measurements, and carrier-kinetic/device measurements would each establish, and state what result would falsify a claim of a beneficial energy-funneling phase gradient.

A top-down route that dissolves a target Ruddlesden-Popper single crystal in a weakly coordinating solvent system works for one spacer cation and n = 3. You want to transfer it to a chemically different spacer, target n = 4, and deposit the absorber by slot-die coating. Develop go/no-go rules for this transfer. Explain why reusing the same cosolvent and acid fraction is not sufficient, and specify the precursor-state, film-state, device, and stability evidence required before claiming that the single-crystal template mechanism has transferred.

A phosphonic-acid SAM that performs well when spin-coated on small UV-ozone-treated FTO substrates must be transferred to textured, large-area FTO and blade-coated perovskite mini-modules. Propose a process-control and reliability qualification plan. Your answer must address incomplete coverage, excessive coverage or unbound molecules, spatial work-function variation, perovskite-ink wetting, interfacial adhesion, and the difference between a short unencapsulated MPP test and a credible module-stability claim.

Several hydrophobic dopant-free polymer HTMs require an anilinium iodide surface treatment before a two-step FASnI3 deposition. After treatment, one structural isomer gives the best precursor wetting, highest perovskite crystallinity, shortest PL decay, and largest recombination resistance. Design a factorial causal study that determines how much of this advantage is intrinsic to the polymer backbone and substitution pattern, how much comes from the anilinium treatment, and how much is mediated indirectly through altered perovskite growth. Include the controls and measurements needed to avoid assigning every improvement to faster hole extraction.

A conformationally locked, sulfur-containing dopant-free polythiophene is optimized as the buried hole contact for an all-tin FASnI3 cell. A team proposes transferring it unchanged to a wide-bandgap mixed Sn-Pb p-i-n cell. Develop a go/no-go framework for this transfer. Identify which apparent advantages may be transferable, which may reverse, and the experiments required to evaluate energy alignment, wetting/crystallization, Lewis-base coordination, Sn oxidation, ion migration or light-induced phase segregation, and operational stability.

Two p-type dopants are evaluated for a semicrystalline P3HT hole-transport layer. Both move the P3HT Fermi level toward its HOMO in UPS. Dopant A strongly increases in-plane film conductivity, but GIWAXS still shows predominantly edge-on packing; a perovskite/P3HT bilayer exhibits only modest PL quenching, and complete devices retain a low fill factor. Dopant B gives face-on-enriched packing, stronger PL quenching with a shorter PL lifetime, lower charge-transport resistance, higher recombination resistance, and a much higher fill factor. Diagnose why the UPS shift and conductivity increase are insufficient to establish that Dopant A is an effective device HTL. Assign the measurements to the distinct roles of carrier density/energy alignment, out-of-plane transport, interfacial extraction, and recombination. Also identify one ambiguity in interpreting PL quenching and state how it should be resolved.

In a textured silicon TOPCon contact, increasing the oxidation severity of an ultrathin SiOx interlayer improves implied open-circuit voltage, but contact resistivity rises by orders of magnitude and the contact becomes nonlinear. Reducing oxidation severity restores an ohmic contact, yet carrier lifetime collapses after high-temperature annealing. Cross-sectional microscopy shows that the oxide is thinner on pyramid sidewalls and locally absent in valleys. Explain how a spatially nonuniform ultrathin oxide can produce this apparent passivation-transport paradox. Your answer should include tunneling or pinhole-assisted transport, dopant in-diffusion, local recombination, and current crowding. Then identify spatially resolved measurements that could falsify a model based only on the average SiOx thickness.

A tin-halide perovskite device improves during several days of storage in an oxygen-free glovebox: Voc and photoluminescence lifetime increase, dark hole density decreases, a surface-trap signal weakens, and the bulk absorption edge and bulk XRD pattern remain essentially unchanged. Diagnose the most plausible origin of the improvement. Explain why these observations do not support 'beneficial Sn2+ oxidation' or a major bulk phase reconstruction, and propose a measurement set that can distinguish slow surface passivation/additive redistribution from strain relaxation or contact modification.

Design a staged development and qualification roadmap for a fully lead-free ASnX3 solar module intended for a service life measured in decades. The roadmap must separate precursor/redox control, bulk crystallization and vacancy control, surface/contact passivation, and package-level protection. For each stage, state a diagnostic or acceptance criterion and a stress test that could expose failure. Explain why either (i) a high-efficiency Sn-Pb low-bandgap device or (ii) good retention during short inert-atmosphere storage cannot by itself satisfy the stated objective.

An external luminescent coating on the illumination-side glass of a perovskite solar cell increases Jsc and EQE mainly in the 400-500 nm region, while Voc and fill factor remain nearly unchanged. A nonemissive polymer control has similar UV absorbance but gives no current gain. The same luminophore gives high solid-film PL quantum yield when spray-deposited and very low PL quantum yield when spin-coated, although both films contain similar molecular loading. Build a diagnostic case that the current gain is caused by photon downshifting rather than simple UV filtering, antireflection, or an electronic change inside the cell. Explain the role of aggregation and specify the minimum optical/device measurements needed for a convincing causal claim.

A multifunctional small molecule is introduced at three locations in an inverted perovskite device: beneath the absorber, inside the precursor, and on the top surface. The full three-location treatment gives the best performance. Design the minimum causal experiment needed to determine whether the benefit is additive, synergistic, or merely caused by a larger total molecular dose. For each location, identify a distinct mechanistic signature that should be measured. Explain how interaction terms and dose-matched controls would change the interpretation of a superior three-location device.

A three-location passivation scheme improves an inverted perovskite cell, but each added coating or dosing step increases manufacturing complexity and defect risk. Develop a mechanistically informed down-selection protocol to decide whether the bottom, bulk, and top placements should all be retained for large-area manufacturing. Identify failure modes that make a placement non-redundant, process risks that can reverse its benefit, the large-area measurements required, and the operational-stability criteria for selecting the smallest acceptable treatment set. The protocol must not assume in advance that the full three-location scheme is necessary.

An all-perovskite tandem is analyzed with a loss ladder rather than with its two-terminal J-V curve alone. For the high-gap absorber, absolute PL on the isolated film gives a large quasi-Fermi-level splitting (QFLS), but adding the selective contacts lowers the PL-derived QFLS. In the completed device, the subcell-selective EL-derived pseudo-JV curve yields still less voltage than the PL-derived pseudo-JV curve; the same PL-EL gap is already present in an otherwise matched high-gap single-junction cell. The sum of the two subcell EL-derived pseudo-open-circuit voltages is close to the measured tandem VOC, yet the measured tandem fill factor remains substantially below the pseudo-fill factor. Attribute each gap in this measurement ladder to the most likely physical loss class. Explain why the interconnect should not be assigned the dominant voltage loss in this case, and specify one conditioning control needed before trusting the EL diagnosis.

A high-gap perovskite subcell shows excellent VOC and PLQY as a small-area single junction after interface optimization, but a large-area monolithic tandem made from the same subcell develops spatially nonuniform VOC, unstable subcell EL, and a lower fill factor after the oxide interconnect and low-gap subcell are deposited. Design a stepwise qualification protocol that can distinguish (i) damage to the high-gap absorber or its contacts during subsequent processing, (ii) recombination or leakage in the interconnect, and (iii) large-area transport/current-matching losses. State the minimum controls, spatially resolved measurements, and steady-state stability checks required before transferring the interface strategy to manufacturing.

Three covalent-organic-framework additives all suppress the PbI2 diffraction peak and shift Pb 4f binding energies, but only one additive strongly delays crystallization, removes a photoinactive intermediate from the in situ phase pathway, and improves final film uniformity. Propose a causal molecular-ablation experiment that can determine whether this additive truly coordinates Pb-containing species, halide anions, and organic A-site cations simultaneously rather than acting only as a Lewis-base Pb2+ retardant or as a hydrophobic surface passivator. Specify the matched molecular controls, the decisive solution/film measurements, and the result pattern that would constitute evidence for a synergistic all-component mechanism.

A multifunctional COF additive that works in antisolvent-assisted spin coating is transferred to slot-die coating without an antisolvent. The wet film now dries more slowly, the additive occasionally forms aggregates, and some modules show excellent PL but poor electron extraction. Explain which kinetic and spatial design principles must be preserved during scale-up. Propose a process-development matrix and acceptance criteria that prevent both under-regulated crystallization and over-retardation/insulating COF accumulation, while demonstrating stability benefits rather than merely a high initial module efficiency.

A molecular salt inserted between a wide-bandgap perovskite and C60 increases VOC and fill factor while JSC is nearly unchanged. The molecule can create an interfacial dipole, coordinate undercoordinated Pb, and physically separate the first C60 layer from the perovskite. Design a matched-molecule and thickness-series experiment that separates the contributions of (a) electrostatic dipole/energy alignment, (b) chemical defect passivation, and (c) tunneling-barrier or C60-displacement effects. For each mechanism, state the diagnostic signature expected in spectroscopy, recombination measurements, and device transport.

A dipolar ammonium-salt interlayer gives a high VOC on a small planar perovskite cell, but after transfer to a large-area perovskite/silicon tandem on a textured substrate the VOC gain is retained while fill factor falls and electroluminescence becomes spatially nonuniform; JSC remains essentially unchanged. Diagnose the most likely scale-up failure modes and propose a deposition/qualification strategy that preserves dipole orientation and passivation without forming an insulating salt-rich phase. Include measurements that distinguish contact resistance from recombination and a durability protocol appropriate for the tandem.

A protected halide-perovskite photoanode initially drives oxygen evolution in aqueous electrolyte, but its photocurrent and product Faradaic efficiency decay during operation. Construct an operando diagnostic decision tree that distinguishes four failure classes: absorber decomposition, pinhole or delamination failure of the protection layer, catalyst deactivation/side reactions, and increasing charge-transfer or recombination loss at a still-intact interface. For each class, identify a mutually reinforcing set of electrical, optical, chemical, and product-analysis signatures.

A team must build a neutral-aqueous CO2-to-CO system that operates for at least 1000 h, permits independent replacement of the electrocatalyst, and has a near-zero tolerance for lead release. The light absorber may be a high-efficiency lead-halide perovskite. Choose among a directly suspended photocatalyst, a protected perovskite photoelectrode, and an electrically isolated perovskite PV-electrolyzer architecture. Defend the preferred architecture, define the voltage/current-matching strategy, and specify the system-level metrics and accelerated tests needed to establish genuine solar-to-fuel performance and containment.

A fluoroarene-hydrazine post-treatment leaves the perovskite absorption edge essentially unchanged, causes only a small photoluminescence peak shift, lengthens bare-film photoluminescence decay, lowers the light-intensity ideality factor, shifts the surface work function, and produces a fluorine signal confined to the upper few nanometres. A low-angle quasi-2D diffraction peak appears only at high treatment dose, where device Voc and fill factor begin to fall. Build a causal diagnosis that separates defect passivation, interfacial electrostatic or band-alignment effects, and formation of a transport-blocking low-dimensional phase. Which controls would make the attribution mechanistic rather than correlative?

Two diammonium post-treatments give similar first-order recombination lifetimes in transient absorption. Process A forms a surface-enriched low-n phase, whereas process B forms higher-n phases earlier and leaves a more uniform mixed-n distribution through the reconstructed surface region. Process B nevertheless gives faster energy transfer, a longer electron diffusion length, and a higher fill factor. Explain why the similar recombination lifetime does not refute a phase-distribution mechanism. Design an orthogonal measurement set that distinguishes transport continuity and energy funneling from simple trap passivation.

After thermal aging, a fully contacted perovskite cell develops a slower low-fluence transient-photoluminescence tail even though Voc, electroluminescence efficiency, and maximum-power output all decline. Design a stack-resolved protocol to determine whether aging truly reduced recombination or instead increased capacitive charging, ion-induced band bending, or carrier re-injection. State the sample ladder, excitation and bias variables, electrical-optical cross-checks, and decision criteria.

A ferrocene interlayer optimized beneath conventionally LiTFSI/tBP-doped spiro-OMeTAD must be transferred to a low-Li or Li-free hole-transport formulation and to large-area coating. Propose a factorial design and acceptance criteria that reveal which ferrocene functions remain useful while preventing an incomplete or overly thick interlayer from becoming a recombination site or transport barrier. Include compositional factors, spatial diagnostics, and stress tests.

Two photovoltaic mini-modules have the same standard-test-condition efficiency and the same backsheet. Module A is planar and lets much of the sub-bandgap near-infrared light escape. Module B uses strong light trapping that raises photocurrent but also increases absorption in the transparent conductor and encapsulant. Under low wind B operates hotter, whereas at high wind the temperature difference nearly disappears. Construct an energy and heat-transfer diagnosis, and specify measurements that separate optical parasitic heating, recombination or resistive heating, and differences in thermal boundary conditions.

Five repeated batch photocatalysis cycles with retained powder XRD are reported for a ligand-regulated halide double perovskite. Design an accelerated stability study that can distinguish four failure modes: ligand desorption, renewed Ag/Bi disorder or antisite formation, halide loss/chemical corrosion, and organic-reaction-product poisoning. State the stress protocol, the time-resolved measurements, and the recovery tests that would assign causality rather than merely document activity loss.

A bulky-ammonium-containing perovskite film exhibits a lower slope-derived ideality factor than the 3D control, yet its absolute open-circuit voltage and efficiency are much worse. Spectroscopy detects low-dimensional phases, and depth profiling places the bulky organic component near the buried electron-contact interface. Explain why the lower ideality factor is not evidence that recombination has been reduced overall. Give a diagnostic hierarchy that can determine whether the dominant loss is bulk recombination, an interfacial energetic barrier, defective low-dimensional material, or impaired carrier extraction.

A new pyrazine analog has a more negative calculated adsorption energy and produces a longer film TRPL lifetime than the current passivator, but complete devices show a lower fill factor and worse thermal stability. Explain why ranking candidates by adsorption energy or TRPL lifetime alone fails. Construct a go/no-go test matrix for deciding whether the analog should be optimized, rejected, or reformulated for large-area perovskite modules.

In a two-step perovskite deposition process, non-perovskite delta-phase CsPbI3/RbPbI3 particles are added to the first-step PbI2 precursor. The final film contains Cs and Rb, has less residual PbI2, and shows larger grains. Design a control set that can distinguish true seed-assisted heterogeneous nucleation from three alternatives: simple alkali-cation compositional doping, a generic ionic-strength/solvent effect, and nonspecific particulate templating. State the observations that would be required to claim a seed-specific mechanism.

A delta-seed-assisted two-step perovskite recipe developed by spin coating must be transferred to continuous slot-die coating. Copying the laboratory concentrations and annealing temperatures gives nonuniform conversion and large roll-to-roll variations. Identify the process variables that must be preserved by mechanistic equivalence rather than by copying their numerical values. Propose inline or rapid at-line indicators for each critical stage and define a process-control strategy that protects both device performance and operational stability.

A 1.75 eV mixed-I/Br perovskite develops a new red-shifted PL peak during one-sun illumination and its device VOC falls, but conventional XRD shows no obvious peak splitting. Construct a diagnostic decision tree that distinguishes true light-induced halide phase segregation from carrier funneling into pre-existing low-gap defects or tails, sample heating, and contact-induced interfacial recombination. Explain why the absence of a conventional XRD signature is not decisive.

Design a phase-stable approximately 1.75 eV perovskite top cell for long-term maximum-power-point operation. Organize the design into thermodynamic, kinetic, mechanical, and interfacial controls. For each category, give at least one intervention, its intended mechanism, and a likely trade-off. Then define the operational evidence needed to show that the design is genuinely stable rather than merely slow to segregate during a short PL test.

Two chemically dissimilar ultrathin interlayers produce nearly the same QFLS recovery when inserted between a wide-bandgap perovskite and C60, while neither improves the neat-film QFLS. Design a discriminating experiment set to decide whether the shared benefit arises mainly from chemical passivation, physical contact displacement or spatial separation, an interface dipole/band-alignment change, or protection against C60-deposition damage. For each candidate mechanism, state a prediction that would support or falsify it.

An ultrathin perovskite/C60 interlayer must be transferred from a flat small-area cell to a textured, large-area tandem top cell. Design a process-control and qualification framework that balances recombination suppression, conformal coverage, charge extraction, and operational durability. What spatially resolved measurements and ageing signatures determine whether the interlayer has a robust manufacturing window rather than a narrow champion-device optimum?

A passivation treatment lowers the apparent deep-trap density but creates a larger population of shallow traps. The treated film has higher one-sun PLQY, yet its low-light performance depends strongly on illumination history and its device VOC drifts during bias-light ageing. Build a decision workflow for accepting or rejecting this passivant. The workflow must separate trap concentration, trap depth, capture coefficients, photodoping, and ion-migration-induced evolution across relevant operating conditions.

You want to test whether Pb2+/Pb0 and I-/polyiodide redox chemistry is a causal driver of light-induced segregation in an all-inorganic mixed-I/Br perovskite rather than a late byproduct. Design a charge-selective perturbation experiment using otherwise identical films with preferential electron extraction, preferential hole extraction, and inert control contacts. State the predicted effects on grain-boundary I-rich phase nucleation and on Pb0 and polyiodide signatures, and identify the outcome that would instead favor a predominantly strain- or polaron-driven model.

You must down-select one lead-free perovskite-inspired absorber from three candidates: a structurally zero-dimensional vacancy-ordered compound, a layered two-dimensional compound, and a three-dimensional double perovskite. All three survive six months of dark shelf storage, but their band structures, carrier localization, and processing textures differ. Define a multi-objective selection protocol for a photovoltaic absorber and explain why neither structural dimensionality nor shelf stability can be used as a proxy for device suitability.

A grain-boundary passivation treatment makes a fresh perovskite film look better by two nanoscale metrics: KPFM surface photovoltage becomes more spatially uniform and pc-AFM photocurrent increases. However, stabilized device lifetime under combined humidity and electrical bias does not improve. Decide whether the treatment should advance to scale-up, and design a same-location, multi-stressor qualification that can determine whether the fresh-state nanoscale gains are causally relevant to operational stability.

A tandem-module team must choose among three routes with similar small-area cell efficiency: (A) an ultrathin indium-based TCO plus dielectric cap and metal grid, (B) an AZO-only transparent electrode, or (C) an indium-free silicon recombination junction combined with a non-indium transparent electrode. Build a stage-gated decision framework for commercialization. Explain why nominally ‘zero indium’ is not a sufficient selection rule, and include resource normalization, interface/process compatibility, accelerated reliability, and the risk that protective layers reintroduce the material being eliminated.

Because cadmium raises toxicity and supply-chain concerns, a team proposes replacing Cd2+ with another divalent metal while retaining an alkali iodide additive. Design a stage-gated strategy for deciding whether the replacement truly preserves the dual-site defect-engineering principle rather than merely improving morphology. State the atomistic, chemical, optoelectronic, ion-migration, and stability criteria, the essential controls, and at least three rejection conditions that should stop device optimization even if the first J–V curves improve.

Two low-loading copolymer additives produce perovskite films with matched grain size, absorption, and water contact angle. Polymer A has stronger interchain hydrogen bonding and a higher small-strain modulus; polymer B has weaker, faster-exchanging hydrogen bonds. Under cyclic tensile strain, B shows lower crack density, less strain-induced metallic Pb, smaller local PL broadening near cracks, and better device retention. Design a falsifiable program to determine whether B forms a polymer–perovskite hybrid dynamic network rather than acting as a simple plasticizer. Explain why stronger self-association can be mechanically inferior.

The same NiOx/interfacial-molecule concept is to be transferred from spin-coated laboratory cells to blade-coated large-area devices. Propose a go/no-go qualification plan that preserves the molecule's dual functions—uniform perovskite formation and selective hole extraction—while detecting failure modes that may emerge only at scale. Your answer should define process-critical variables, spatially resolved diagnostics, accelerated-stability tests, and at least one criterion that would reject an apparently high-efficiency formulation.

In a flexible perovskite solar cell, increasing the concentration of an elastic polymer additive first raises photoluminescence lifetime and bending-cycle retention, but at higher concentration the fill factor and photocurrent decline even though crack density remains low. Diagnose the most likely transition from beneficial polymer action to detrimental behavior. Describe a concentration-dependent characterization matrix that can distinguish defect passivation and stress absorption from charge-transport blocking, phase segregation, or disrupted crystallization.

A family of ionic-liquid additives shares the same imidazolium cation but contains different anions. One salt gives the strongest NMR perturbation, the best crystal texture, the lowest trap density, and the highest device efficiency. What experimental logic is required to establish that cation-to-Pb coordination is the primary defect-passivation interaction while the anion tunes interaction strength and crystallization, rather than the result arising from generic ionic strength, residual solvent, or anion-only chemistry? Give the key controls and the predicted evidence pattern.

Thiourea can be introduced either into the PbI₂ precursor or as a treatment on SnO₂ before a two-step FA-based perovskite conversion. Both routes improve the device. Design a causal experiment that separates three possible contributions: (1) a transient thiourea–PbI₂ intermediate that changes crystallization kinetics, (2) persistent buried-interface defect passivation, and (3) residual-stress relief. State the route-specific controls and the independent signatures expected for each contribution.
