An unencapsulated carbonyl-additive device retains efficiency well during humidity storage, but no long-duration heat-light maximum-power-point test has been performed. Design an experiment that separates two possible origins of the apparent stability: (A) a hydrophobic diffusion barrier that slows water ingress and (B) genuine chemical passivation of Pb-related defects that also remains beneficial under dry thermal and electrical stress. The study must be capable of deciding whether the additive will still help after high-quality encapsulation removes most external moisture ingress.

A conjugated block-copolymer post-treatment gives excellent small-area inverted cells, but a slot-die-coated 200 cm2 module shows a centre-to-edge gradient in polymer coverage. Low-coverage regions retain high PL but lose fill factor after C60 deposition; high-coverage regions show strong PL quenching but rising series resistance during 65 degrees C maximum-power-point operation. Design a scale-up study that finds a robust coverage and block-architecture window rather than optimizing only the mean polymer concentration. Include process variables, mechanistic controls, spatial diagnostics, and operational-stability acceptance criteria.

A paintable carbon perovskite cell uses a CuPc interlayer. Increasing CuPc loading progressively increases hydrophobicity and fills or smooths surface pinholes, yet device efficiency peaks at an intermediate loading. Two carbon formulations also trade higher initial efficiency against stronger aging retention. Develop a process window and qualification plan for transferring this contact to modules. Which variables must be controlled, which failure modes can reverse the small-cell optimum, and what measurements would constitute go/no-go evidence?

A mixed molecular interlayer on chemical-bath-deposited SnO2 lowers the ETL/perovskite TRPL lifetime, reduces the SCLC trap-filled-limit voltage, lowers the admittance-derived interface-state density, shifts Sn core levels, lowers the SnO2 surface energy, and produces larger perovskite grains. The performance gain is attributed to both chemical dual-side passivation and crystallization control. Construct a causal experiment that separates these two contributions, and explain how each mechanism should affect at least two independent observables.

A sulfonate/Na interlayer placed between a perovskite and Li-TFSI-doped Spiro-OMeTAD produces spectroscopic signatures of Li interaction and a lower Li signal deep in the perovskite and electron-transport layer after aging. Explain why this does not by itself prove interfacial Li immobilization rather than lower Li incorporation or altered Spiro oxidation. Design a mass-balance and transport experiment, including molecular controls, that can distinguish these mechanisms.

Within a pyrrole-core hole-transport-material series, fluorination coincides with a deeper HOMO, the highest hole-only SCLC mobility, a smooth pinhole-free film, a Pb 4f shift, the lowest ideality factor, and the fastest interfacial TRPL decay. A claim is made that the electronegative O/F-rich region of the fluorinated derivative directly passivates Pb-related surface defects. Design a causal identification strategy that determines whether this direct chemical passivation is necessary, rather than the device gain arising from morphology, transport, or energy alignment. State expected outcomes for the competing hypotheses.

An unencapsulated small-area perovskite cell with an approximately 100 nm small-molecule HTL retains about 80% of its output under nitrogen MPPT and low-humidity shelf storage, and the HTM has a high melting point. Evaluate what these results do and do not establish about module reliability. Build a staged qualification plan for large-area manufacturing and name the most likely scale-up failure modes.

An in-situ cross-linked additive yields larger grains, longer photoluminescence lifetime, lower residual strain, stronger buried-interface adhesion, and fewer cracks or delamination after thermal cycling. Explain why these observations do not by themselves distinguish stress relaxation by a compliant polymer network from increased cohesive or interfacial fracture toughness, or from simply starting with a lower defect population. Design controls and measurements that separate the three mechanisms.

For roll-to-roll flexible perovskite modules, an additive polymerizes during perovskite processing while also chelating the SnO2 buried interface. Develop a process-control and combined-stress reliability plan. Address cure heterogeneity, possible charge-transport penalties, neutral-axis and encapsulation effects, and why separate thermal-cycling and bending tests are insufficient. Specify the controls, in-line or post-process measurements, and go/no-go criteria needed for manufacturing transfer.

A pi-conjugated donor-acceptor spacer in a quasi-2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite simultaneously lowers exciton binding energy, raises the dielectric constant, improves vertical orientation, and lengthens carrier lifetime. A reviewer argues that the apparent electronic deconfinement is only a consequence of better morphology. Design a decisive experiment set that separates direct spacer-framework electronic coupling and dielectric screening from morphology-mediated transport. State the matched controls, measurements, opposite predictions, and falsification criteria.

A donor-acceptor semiconductor spacer that performs well in spin-coated small-area quasi-2D cells is proposed for blade-coated modules. The same conjugation and dipole that aid charge transport may also alter solubility, low-n phase distribution, crystal orientation, and spacer retention. Define a process-development and qualification plan. Which variables must be mapped, which spatially resolved measurements are essential, and what evidence would show that the molecular mechanism survives scale-up rather than being a small-area processing artifact?

Design an accelerated qualification study that determines whether a Li+-complexing hole-transport-layer additive truly prevents, rather than merely delays, coupled Li/I/Ag degradation. The study must separate HTL chemical failure, perovskite ion migration, and metal-electrode corrosion. Specify the device-factor controls, stress sequence, time-resolved readouts, and a pass/fail criterion suitable before module development.

A dihydroxy ammonium iodide treatment of PEDOT:PSS improves mixed Sn-Pb perovskite morphology, energy alignment, and recombination. Devise a control matrix that separates three candidate causes: neutralization or modification of acidic PEDOT:PSS, coordination/passivation of Pb/Sn defects, and nucleation templating. What matched controls and readouts would let you assign causality rather than merely correlate the best film with the best device?

An unencapsulated mixed Sn-Pb cell retains most of its efficiency for 2000 hours in nitrogen shelf storage after buried-interface treatment. What additional evidence is required before claiming suitability for an all-perovskite tandem module? Design a test plan that specifically addresses Sn2+ oxidation, acidic PEDOT:PSS, operational ion redistribution, and area-scaling losses.

During long-term maximum-power operation, a surface-treated perovskite device first degrades and then partially recovers. The proposed explanation is a light- or heat-assisted reaction of the molecular treatment with newly exposed PbI2 to form a protective low-dimensional surface phase. Design an operando or quasi-operando study that can prove this dynamic self-repair mechanism and distinguish it from reversible ion redistribution, contact conditioning, or measurement drift.

A multifunctional spacer cation has an optimum precursor-additive dose and also works as a post-treatment, but overdosing harms crystallization. You must transfer the combined strategy from antisolvent spin coating to a high-throughput antisolvent-free coating process. Define a design-of-experiments and in-line control scheme that preserves the distinct grain-boundary and surface functions without creating an insulating low-dimensional barrier.

A series of dopant-free phthalocyanine hole-transport materials has nearly identical frontier energy levels and similar film diffraction, yet one member shows stronger interfacial photoluminescence quenching, higher mobility, and lower charge-transfer resistance. Its superiority is attributed to the direction of an intramolecular electric field. Design experiments that distinguish a true bulk molecular-field or hole-delocalization effect from a simple interfacial dipole, thickness, or morphology artifact. State the decisive signatures.

A fluorinated asymmetric self-assembled monolayer gives excellent wetting, initial efficiency, and thermal robustness in small inverted cells. After transfer to a textured 100 cm2 transparent electrode, the average contact angle and average work function remain acceptable, yet electroluminescence imaging shows edge-localized dark regions and the module develops local hot spots during maximum-power-point operation. Design a process-transfer and qualification study that determines whether the failure originates from sparse monolayer pinholes, nonuniform molecular packing, over-wetting-induced perovskite defects, or a later transport-layer/encapsulation problem. Define the spatial measurements, mechanistic controls, and go/no-go criteria.

A thermally programmed additive is effective because it coordinates the precursor at low temperature, cleaves only during high-temperature annealing to expel residual solvent, and leaves an anchored passivating fragment at the buried interface. You must transfer this chemistry to a flexible substrate whose process temperature cannot exceed 120 °C. Explain why simply lowering the annealing temperature is unlikely to preserve the mechanism. Propose a redesign and validation plan that retains the required sequence of functions while preventing volatile entrapment, additive diffusion, and mechanical-instability penalties.

Adding a volatile Lewis-basic cosolvent to a rapidly drying perovskite ink produces a new room-temperature intermediate, fewer nuclei, larger oriented grains, and lower trap density. The cosolvent also evaporates more slowly than the primary solvent. Design an experiment that determines whether the specific coordinated intermediate is a causal mediator of film improvement or merely a marker of slower drying. Your design must independently vary coordination strength and evaporation rate, identify the intermediate in real time, and state the result pattern required for a causal conclusion.

An anti-solvent-free blade-coating process obtains its wide processing window from a volatile-solvent intermediate that contains methylammonium species and releases a volatile amine during annealing. You must adapt the process to a nominally methylammonium-free FA/Cs perovskite without sacrificing low-boiling-solvent compatibility. Identify which mechanistic assumptions cannot be transferred directly, and design a go/no-go development plan for a new intermediate-regulation chemistry, including composition control, in situ diagnostics, residual-species limits, and module-level stability tests.

A precursor additive lengthens the carrier lifetime and lowers trap density in bare perovskite films. In complete inverted devices, however, the open-circuit-voltage gain is substantially larger than the increase in bare-film quasi-Fermi-level splitting. Depth profiling shows one ionic fragment enriched near the perovskite/electron-transport-layer interface, and photoelectron spectroscopy shows a reduced interfacial energy offset. Construct a diagnostic framework that separates bulk chemical passivation from contact-specific field-effect or energetic passivation. Specify the split-component controls, layer-by-layer measurements, and the result pattern that would justify assigning the extra voltage gain to the contact.

A thiol-containing additive suppresses I2/I3- accumulation in aged perovskite precursor and forms disulfide species after oxidation. Illumination is proposed to regenerate active thiol groups, creating a self-sustaining redox cycle rather than one-time sacrificial iodine scavenging. Design a repeated-cycle chemical and device experiment that can prove regeneration, quantify capacity loss, and determine whether the mechanism remains beneficial under realistic light, temperature, oxygen, and maximum-power-point conditions. State the decisive go/no-go observations.

An inverted p-i-n perovskite solar cell uses a solution-cast C60 electron-transport layer blended with a curved pi-conjugated assembly assistant. Across 0-10 wt% assistant, AFM roughness falls rapidly and remains low, but electron mobility, conductive-AFM current, and fill factor peak at about 2 wt% and then decline; Voc changes little. Explain the non-monotonic optimum. Then specify two orthogonal experiments, with predicted outcomes, that would distinguish loss of C60 percolation/electrical dilution from residual morphology or interfacial-energy effects.

Two perovskite-surface modifiers contain the same terminal thiol and ammonium groups and have comparable surface coverage, but their spacer geometries differ. Modifier X produces a large work-function shift, lower trap density, higher ion-migration activation energy, and higher QFLS. Modifier Y produces a similar work-function shift but only modest changes in trap density and ion migration. Design a minimal set of locked or blocked molecular controls and measurements that can determine whether X acts through simultaneous dual-site chemical passivation rather than through a surface dipole alone. State the result pattern expected for each mechanism.

To establish that a larger aromatic pi system strengthens Pb2+ defect passivation indirectly by increasing carbonyl donor strength, rather than through direct pi binding or merely altered crystallization, design a minimal factorial molecular library and an evidence chain. Include at least one control that breaks conjugation between the aromatic core and the carbonyl, and state the qualitative trends that would validate or falsify the proposed mediation mechanism.

A buried-contact nucleation strategy eliminates thermal peeling and gives excellent 85 degrees C storage retention, but it does not improve one-sun maximum-power-point aging. Construct a two-interface reliability strategy for a single-crystal perovskite solar cell and a diagnostic stress matrix that assigns degradation to buried delamination versus top-interface ion migration or electrode reactions. State what evidence would justify combining, rather than replacing, the two interventions.

A DMA-like A-site cation simultaneously permits lower Br content, slows crystallization, reduces traps, changes residual strain, and raises ion-migration activation energy in a wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskite. Design a factorial control set that can determine whether suppression of light/bias-induced phase segregation is caused primarily by intrinsic lattice reinforcement rather than by lower Br fraction or improved morphology alone. State the decisive signature under coupled stress.

You want to apply a DMA-like lattice-reinforcement strategy to a 1.75 eV perovskite/silicon two-terminal tandem rather than a perovskite/organic tandem. Define the design constraints and validation sequence required before adopting the cation. Address bandgap/current matching, phase purity and transport, stress conditions representative of tandem operation, and scale-up uniformity. Give explicit rejection criteria.

A perovskite film containing a grain-boundary nitrile polymer network and an ultrathin nitrile-rich surface layer exhibits stronger PL and a much longer TRPL lifetime. However, a polymer overlayer can also increase photon recycling, screen electric fields, or slow carrier extraction. Design the minimum decisive experiment set needed to prove a true reduction of Pb-related nonradiative defects rather than an optical artifact or transport barrier. Include controls, excitation or thickness perturbations, and mechanism-specific signatures.

A staged bulk-plus-surface polymerization process is to be transferred from a small-area single-composition n-i-p cell to slot-die-coated wide-bandgap mixed-halide modules. Construct a design-of-experiments that prevents three competing failures: premature polymerization that disrupts crystallization, incomplete conversion or monomer loss, and an overthick surface network that impedes extraction. Include process-state variables, chemical and structural diagnostics, phase-segregation and ion-migration tests, module-uniformity metrics, and conditions under which the strategy should be rejected.

A roughly 10 nm low-dimensional perovskite interlayer on a 3D single-crystal absorber raises fill factor and carrier lifetime, lowers surface trap density, and suppresses iodine detected at the metal electrode, while open-circuit voltage remains unchanged. Construct an ablation experiment that quantitatively separates chemical vacancy passivation, ionic blocking, and electronic contact modification. Which thickness and composition controls and time-, temperature-, and bias-dependent measurements identify each contribution, and what result would reveal hidden extraction resistance despite improved stability?

A low-dimensional ion-blocking layer developed for a single-crystal perovskite solar cell is proposed for a high-field perovskite X-ray detector. Design the interface so that it suppresses field-induced polarization and electrode contamination without sacrificing charge collection. State the required energetic and ionic properties, thickness and processing window, matched device controls, operando diagnostics under dose and bias, and pass/fail criteria that distinguish genuine ion blocking from merely lowering current through an insulating contact.

A perovskite/MoS2 powder shows almost complete PL quenching, a shorter average PL lifetime, faster bleach recovery, stronger photocurrent, and higher hydrogen evolution after increasing interfacial Pb-S bonding. PL quenching alone could equally indicate trap-assisted loss. Devise a kinetic and control framework that distinguishes productive electron transfer to catalytically active MoS2 from new nonradiative recombination or simple optical reabsorption. Specify excitation-selective experiments, rate-model terms, controls, and mechanism-specific signatures.

A Sn-Pb ink gives its best film when coated within about 30 minutes of mixing but becomes turbid after roughly one hour. Design a scalable manufacturing strategy that uses, rather than ignores, this metastable precursor window. Define continuous-mixing or hold-up architecture, inline state variables and acceptance limits, feedback actions, sampling across coating width and run time, and device and stability validation. Explain what evidence would show that residence-time control is insufficient and the molecular formulation itself must be redesigned.

A multiaxial ferroelectric crystal initially shows switchable polarization and zero-bias photocurrent along both the b and c axes. After repeated illumination and electrical-poling cycles, the c-axis photocurrent still reverses with the poling direction, but the b-axis signal no longer reverses, drifts slowly in the dark, and is accompanied by increased dark conductance. Diagnose the competing mechanisms that could produce this axis-selective failure, and specify a minimal measurement sequence that can distinguish incomplete ferroelectric switching from mobile-ion/contact polarization and from loss of the bulk polar phase.

An engineer proposes increasing the inorganic-layer number of a Ruddlesden-Popper hybrid perovskite beyond the composition already known to be multiaxially ferroelectric, arguing that the narrower bandgap and higher conductivity should automatically improve multidirectional self-driven photodetection. Explain why this extrapolation can fail, and give a validation strategy for selecting an optimum composition and device architecture rather than maximizing layer number alone.

During prolonged CO2 electroreduction on a conductive Cu-based perovskite oxide, bulk X-ray diffraction remains unchanged and operando infrared spectra still show both adsorbed CO and CHO-like species, yet C2+ selectivity falls while methane formation increases. Explain why these observations do not prove that the original asymmetric adjacent Cu-site coupling motif remains active, and design tests that distinguish surface-motif reconstruction from a change in the local reaction environment or mass transport.

An inverted p-i-n perovskite solar cell shows higher photoluminescence yield and open-circuit voltage immediately after an ionic interfacial passivant is introduced. Under combined light and heat at maximum power point, however, the device develops larger hysteresis, increased low-frequency capacitance, and faster efficiency loss than the untreated control. Give a causal explanation that reconciles the initial gain with the later failure, and outline experiments that would distinguish mobile-ion accumulation from irreversible chemical or contact degradation.

A self-assembled-monolayer passivation strategy gives excellent voltage and fill factor in small spin-coated inverted cells on rigid glass, but a slot-die-coated flexible module made with the same chemistry shows large spatial variation, lower fill factor, and rapid failure during bending and damp-heat testing. Develop a transfer strategy that identifies why the laboratory result did not scale and specifies the process and reliability evidence needed before module adoption.

During operando testing of a mixed-halide perovskite solar cell, photoluminescence intensity falls and the low-frequency capacitance increases under light and bias, but GIWAXS shows no new crystalline phase. Construct a diagnostic argument that distinguishes reversible ionic redistribution or nanoscale phase segregation from irreversible chemical decomposition, and state how the perturbation sequence and synchronized measurements should be designed.

A pilot slot-die line can accommodate only two synchronized in situ modalities for monitoring perovskite film formation. Select one structure-sensitive and one scalable optoelectronic or optical modality, and explain how their signals should be calibrated and converted into closed-loop process control without confusing probe artifacts or sparse sampling with real coating defects.

The same perovskite composition yields high photoluminescence quantum yield and excellent PeLED external quantum efficiency at electrical injection, yet a solar cell made from it has a substantial voltage deficit and poor fill factor under one-sun operation. Explain how these results can coexist, and give a diagnostic framework that separates carrier-density effects, interface energetics, transport/extraction losses, and optical outcoupling.

A small-area spin-coated alpha-CsPbI3 device is stabilized by an additive and a thin low-dimensional surface phase. You must transfer the concept to slot-die-coated carbon-electrode modules without sacrificing current collection. Develop a go/no-go scale-up plan that defines the composition and drying window, detects nonuniform phase stabilization and insulating surface-layer formation, tests module-specific degradation, and identifies the minimum evidence required before claiming that the laboratory stabilization strategy is scalable.

A reductive additive in a narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb perovskite lowers the Sn4+ signal in surface XPS, increases the neat-film photoluminescence lifetime, and raises photoluminescence intensity. In complete devices, however, open-circuit voltage is unchanged and fill factor decreases. Explain why these observations do not prove that nonradiative recombination has been solved. Design a diagnostic workflow that distinguishes bulk defect passivation from suppressed charge extraction, interfacial recombination, altered self-doping, and a chemically unstable contact.

A narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb single-junction cell uses a reducing additive and a thin 2D interlayer to suppress tin oxidation and interfacial recombination. Formulate a go/no-go transfer protocol for incorporating this absorber into a monolithic two-terminal all-perovskite tandem. Your protocol must coordinate current matching, voltage preservation, recombination-junction compatibility, processing sequence, and long-term oxidation/ion-migration stability rather than judging the bottom cell only by its isolated efficiency.

A 3D/2D surface treatment that improves a perovskite solar cell is proposed for a perovskite light-emitting diode. Explain why the photovoltaic recipe cannot be transferred unchanged. Design an LED-specific 3D/2D architecture and validation program that balances defect passivation, carrier injection, exciton confinement, energy funneling, ion-migration suppression, and electrical stability.

In a halide perovskite, broadband transient absorption shows that the high-energy carrier distribution cools more slowly as pump fluence increases. At the same time, the band-edge bleach shifts with carrier density and a long-lived sub-bandgap signal appears at low fluence. Design an analysis that separates a hot-phonon bottleneck from trap filling and many-body bandgap renormalization. State the fluence, temperature, passivation, repetition-rate, and complementary-spectroscopy signatures expected for each process.

A compositional modification stiffens the halide-perovskite lattice and raises the activation energy for ionic motion, so it appears attractive for operational stability. Explain why this change cannot be evaluated only by reduced ion migration. Develop a materials-selection and experiment program that determines how lattice stiffening changes dielectric screening, polaron formation, exciton binding, carrier cooling, mobility, defect tolerance, and ultimately device stability and efficiency.

A mixed-halide lead perovskite film develops a new red-shifted photoluminescence peak within seconds of illumination, while its conventional laboratory X-ray diffraction pattern is initially unchanged. The new peak disappears after storage in the dark. Construct a mechanistic diagnosis that distinguishes light-induced halide redistribution from three alternatives: uniform lattice heating, trap filling, and irreversible chemical decomposition. Specify a minimal time-resolved measurement set and the mutually consistent signatures that would be required before assigning halide redistribution.

You must suppress illumination-induced compositional instability in a mixed-halide perovskite absorber without sacrificing the carrier collection of a three-dimensional device. Propose a mixed-dimensional design strategy and a falsifiable experiment that determines whether the improvement comes from reduced ion migration, altered segregation thermodynamics, or merely reduced carrier injection into the unstable region. Include the principal transport penalty that your design could introduce and how you would detect it.

A passivation chemistry gives excellent small-area devices when deposited by spin coating, but performance becomes spatially nonuniform and degrades under simultaneous light, heat, and electrical bias when transferred to a large-area coating process. Design a process-development and accelerated-testing matrix that determines whether failure is caused by incomplete surface-site coverage, excess passivator/secondary-phase formation, molecular redistribution under bias, or incompatibility with the underlying perovskite. Your answer must identify controllable process variables, spatially resolved observables, and a decision rule for the acceptable passivation window.

An FAPbI3 solar cell operated under simultaneous illumination and elevated temperature loses open-circuit voltage before short-circuit current, develops increasing hysteresis, and partially recovers after a dark rest. In-situ X-ray diffraction still shows predominantly the black perovskite phase. Diagnose whether the early failure is more consistent with bulk α-to-δ conversion, reversible interfacial ion redistribution, deep-trap generation, or strain-mediated band/defect changes. Provide a measurement sequence and the predicted signatures needed to rank these mechanisms rather than naming only one.

Develop a factorial device-design experiment for FAPbI3 that combines three interventions: A-site composition tuning, an ultrathin low-dimensional surface layer, and strain management through the substrate or processing history. The goal is not merely to find the best champion device, but to determine whether the interventions are additive, synergistic, or antagonistic under simultaneous light-heat-bias stress. Define the controls, response variables, interaction logic, and the main failure trade-off associated with each intervention.

A surface treatment increases the low-fluence time-resolved photoluminescence lifetime of a perovskite film by an order of magnitude, yet the one-sun absolute photoluminescence quantum yield, device open-circuit voltage, and electroluminescence efficiency remain essentially unchanged. Explain why the longer decay alone does not demonstrate suppression of the voltage-limiting recombination pathway. Construct a minimum diagnostic sequence that distinguishes bulk Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, interfacial recombination or extraction, trap filling, radiative recombination, and high-injection Auger loss.

In a perovskite film, pixels with tensile lattice strain also show red-shifted photoluminescence and stronger defect-related emission. This spatial correlation is often interpreted as proof that strain creates electronic defects. Design a causal experiment that can determine whether strain is the driver, a consequence, or merely a covariate of composition, thickness, grain size, local heating, or light-induced ion segregation. Include the temporal and spatial evidence required for a defensible conclusion.

A strain-regulation treatment gives a nearly zero average residual strain in a 1 cm rigid perovskite cell. You must transfer it to a 20 cm flexible module that will experience thermal cycling and repeated bending. Propose a strain-management and validation strategy that avoids the common mistake of optimizing only the mean strain. Explain the materials, process, mechanical, spatial-metrology, and device-level criteria you would use.

Exchanging long oleate/oleylamine ligands on perovskite quantum dots for a short ligand increases film conductivity by two orders of magnitude, but the photoluminescence quantum yield and device open-circuit voltage fall. Develop a mechanistic diagnosis that distinguishes beneficial interdot electronic coupling from ligand stripping, halide loss, undercoordinated lead formation, dot fusion, energetic disorder, and simple extraction-induced photoluminescence quenching. Specify an orthogonal measurement set and the decisive outcomes.

Design a surface-chemistry package for a scalable perovskite-quantum-dot photovoltaic film that must withstand orthogonal-solvent deposition, prolonged illumination at elevated temperature, and electrical bias while retaining efficient charge transport. State the ligand or shell architecture, how it would be locked during processing, the principal degradation modes it is intended to block, and a qualification matrix that can reveal hidden trade-offs.

An ordered halide-perovskite nanocrystal assembly shows faster photoluminescence decay, narrower emission, and more directional light output than a disordered film of the same nanocrystals. Evaluate whether these observations are sufficient to claim cooperative or superradiant emission from a supercrystal. Design an evidence chain that discriminates collective radiative coupling from Förster energy transfer, photon reabsorption, size sorting, optical-cavity effects, and trap-assisted quenching.

A compositionally identical series of lead-halide perovskite quantum dots is made progressively smaller until the particle diameter is below the exciton Bohr radius. The absorption and emission peaks shift to higher energy as expected, but the ensemble photoluminescence linewidth broadens, single-dot spectra wander with time, blinking becomes more frequent, and the ensemble photoluminescence quantum yield decreases. Separate the observations that can arise intrinsically from strong quantum confinement from those that instead diagnose inadequate size control or surface chemistry. Then propose a minimal, orthogonal measurement set that can distinguish size polydispersity, dynamic charging/trapping, and phonon-coupled spectral diffusion.

A long-chain ligand shell gives strongly confined blue perovskite quantum dots near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield in dilute solution. Replacing it completely with a short bidentate ligand increases film conductivity by two orders of magnitude, but solution PLQY falls and an LED made from the exchanged dots develops a progressive red shift and efficiency roll-off under bias. Design a transfer strategy that preserves confinement and surface stoichiometry while enabling charge transport. Explain why complete ligand stripping or simply choosing the shortest possible ligand is not a valid optimization rule, and define the measurements that would constitute a go/no-go decision for device use.

A nitrogen- and sulfur-containing additive yields efficient tin-perovskite cells by spin coating in a dry glovebox. In slot-die coating under low but nonzero oxygen and humidity, the upstream region of the web remains efficient, whereas the downstream edge dries more slowly, contains more Sn4+, and shows lower open-circuit voltage. Propose a molecular-and-process co-design for transferring the additive to scalable coating. Your answer must define which coordination properties should be retained, which molecular properties should be changed, how drying and oxygen exposure should be controlled, and how spatially resolved validation would determine whether the transfer is successful.

Matrix-encapsulated halide perovskite nanocrystals are placed in physiological buffer. After 24 hours, powder XRD still shows the original perovskite phase and the ensemble absorption edge is nearly unchanged, but photoluminescence quantum yield falls by 80%, the emission red-shifts, the lifetime becomes strongly biexponential, and dynamic light scattering reports a threefold increase in hydrodynamic size. Diagnose the most plausible failure sequence. Then specify how to distinguish reversible aggregation and energy transfer from ligand loss, halide exchange, water/oxygen-induced surface traps, and irreversible lattice dissolution.

A polymer-encapsulated perovskite nanocrystal composite retains its initial PLQY after 1000 hours of dark shelf storage. Nevertheless, an LED made from the composite fails rapidly under current injection, and an X-ray scintillator made from the same composite loses light yield with accumulated dose. Construct an application-specific qualification matrix that can determine whether the matrix is a genuine stabilization platform rather than only a dark-storage barrier. Explain which degradation pathways are invisible to shelf PLQY and which performance readouts are required for the LED and the scintillator.

Two perovskite single crystals have comparable bulk mobility-lifetime product and similarly low trap density by a bulk spectroscopy measurement. As radiation detectors, crystal A has low dark current and stable charge collection, whereas crystal B shows high dark current, time-dependent current decay under constant bias (“polarization”), and poor energy resolution. Explain how contact injection, surface leakage, mobile-ion redistribution, and internal-field distortion can dominate despite similar bulk quality. Then propose a diagnostic sequence that separates contact/surface failure from bulk trapping.

A millimeter-thick perovskite single crystal gives excellent X-ray detection, but a photovoltaic product requires a continuous 20–50 micrometre single-crystal absorber over a large area with scalable contacts. Propose a realistic transfer route from bulk crystal growth to a thin, large-area photovoltaic architecture. Explain why simply slicing and polishing a bulk crystal may not preserve the expected advantages, and define the evidence needed to justify superiority over a high-quality polycrystalline film.

A red-emitting tin-halide LED reaches high efficiency in small spin-coated pixels under inert testing and is proposed for large-area coated panels. Build a process-development and reliability-qualification plan that preserves tin redox control, quasi-2D phase distribution, radiative recombination, and balanced charge injection. Which process variables and spatial diagnostics must be mapped, and what operational evidence would distinguish a scalable materials solution from a fragile champion-device result?

Two perovskite films exhibit the same average illumination-induced lattice expansion, yet one forms PbI2 rapidly and the other remains stable. Test the hypothesis that degradation is governed by grain-contact topology and local compressive stress rather than the scalar photostriction amplitude alone. Design an orthogonal microstructure-chemistry experiment, identify the required local measurements and temporal ordering, and state predictions that distinguish contact mechanics from uniform-strain or chemical-passivation explanations.

A soft intergrain polymer suppresses photomechanical degradation in small perovskite cells, but increasing polymer content may create insulating barriers, alter crystallization, or redistribute during large-area coating. Define a scale-up and qualification strategy that finds the mechanical-compliance/electrical-transport optimum. Which process variables, spatially resolved measurements, accelerated stresses, and acceptance criteria are necessary before adopting the approach in modules?

An ultrathin oxide deposited directly on a perovskite by metal-organic precursor/water atomic layer deposition increases open-circuit voltage, yet chemical analysis also suggests nitrogen loss and PbI2 formation. Determine whether the benefit comes from genuine self-limiting defect passivation, controlled surface etching/reconstruction, or a physical diffusion barrier. Design half-cycle and thickness controls, in situ reaction measurements, electronic tests, and mechanism-specific falsification criteria.

A monolithic perovskite tandem uses a temporal-ALD SnO2 layer as a conformal electron contact and sputter-damage buffer, but commercial throughput requires high-speed spatial ALD. Develop a transfer and qualification plan that preserves band alignment, out-of-plane transport, sputter protection, and subcell isolation. Which spatial-ALD variables, inline metrology, module-level failure modes, and reliability tests determine whether the laboratory function has survived scale-up?

A volatile carbonyl additive improves a flexible perovskite film's residual strain, carrier lifetime, and crystallinity. Three mechanisms remain possible: transient coordination followed by sublimation releases stress, permanent chemical passivation lowers defects, or altered nucleation alone improves morphology. Design a molecular-control and processing experiment that separates these mechanisms. Include matched analogues, in situ measurements, residual-additive tests, opposite predictions, and decisive falsification criteria.

A transient, sublimating stress-regulator is to be transferred from small spin-coated flexible cells to roll-to-roll coated modules. Because coordination, crystallization, and additive departure must occur in the correct sequence, define a manufacturing process window and qualification plan. Which web-processing variables, inline measurements, across-web uniformity metrics, and coupled mechanical-operational tests would prove that stress release remains controlled at scale?

Two treatments deposit the same bulky ammonium halide onto the surface of an inverted 3D perovskite absorber. The total organic-salt dose, surface Br content, film roughness, trap-filled-limit voltage, and absolute photoluminescence quantum yield are matched. Nevertheless, treatment V gives substantially higher cross-plane current, faster photoluminescence decay only after the electron-selective contact is added, and a higher device fill factor than treatment S. Conventional theta-2theta XRD detects no low-angle layered-perovskite peak in either sample. Diagnose whether V's advantage is caused by vertical orientation of an ultrathin Ruddlesden-Popper layer rather than by a thinner, patchier, or more heavily Br-doped layer. Specify the minimum counterfactual experiment set and the outcome pattern required to sustain the orientation claim.

A Cu electrode in direct contact with an iodide perovskite shows no detectable CuI or electrical damage after prolonged heating in dry nitrogen, but CuI and PbI2 appear rapidly when the same stack is heated in laboratory air. Construct a causal experiment that determines whether Cu is the primary initiator of degradation or a secondary sink for iodine-containing products generated by oxygen- or moisture-assisted absorber decomposition. Use a controlled-atmosphere matrix, appropriate electrode and no-electrode controls, time-resolved measurements, and explicit decision rules.

Cu/perovskite coupons pass dry-inert thermal tests, yet pilot modules develop corrosion and shunts near edge seals during illuminated damp-heat operation while central cells remain stable. Develop a module-qualification and mitigation plan that determines whether the limiting defect is Cu chemistry, Cu transport through pinholes or interfaces, or package ingress. The plan must include architectural changes, a discriminating test matrix, sensitive failure diagnostics, and a mechanism-specific lifetime criterion.

At a low coating temperature, a small-Cs FA/MA mixed-halide film becomes black during deposition, whereas an otherwise matched Cs-free film remains red until annealing. After extended annealing, both films are largely black, but the Cs-free film retains more yellow-phase and PbI2 signatures; the Cs-containing film also shows a small optical blue shift. Determine which observations support a kinetic nucleation effect and which support a thermodynamic or compositional stabilization effect. Design a decisive experiment that separates these mechanisms, and state the result pattern expected for a purely kinetic, purely thermodynamic, or coupled mechanism.

A coating line for FA/MA mixed-halide perovskite operates across 15-30 degrees C and experiences variable solvent-vapor history. Adding Cs sharply reduces failed batches at the cold end, but excessive Cs produces a wider optical band gap, lower photocurrent, and declining mean efficiency. Design a robust-manufacturing optimization that maximizes production yield and long-term performance rather than champion-cell PCE. Define the experimental factors, fixed-composition controls, in-line process observables, statistical objective, and stability qualification needed to choose the Cs process window.

Under heat-light maximum-power-point stress, an iodide-rich perovskite device develops a few circular inactive lesions that nucleate inside the active area and expand laterally. Design a source-receiver experiment that decisively distinguishes an autocatalytic volatile-I2 propagation mechanism from purely solid-state ion migration, an electric-field-driven front, or local thermal runaway. The experiment must remove any continuous perovskite path between source and receiver and must state the spatial, chemical, and kinetic result expected for each mechanism.

A semitransparent perovskite top cell in a tandem stack is protected by a highly impermeable transparent electrode and hermetic encapsulation. Moisture ingress is reduced, yet isolated heat-light defects still evolve into expanding PbI2-rich lesions and occasionally bulge or rupture the top contact, consistent with trapped volatile products. Propose a multilayer mitigation strategy that suppresses initiation, interrupts iodine-mediated propagation, and manages volatile products without sacrificing transparency or carrier extraction. Define the validation experiments and the failure modes that must be monitored.

You must transfer a high-mobility, dopant-free polymer HTL from spin-coated 0.1 cm2 cells to slot-die coating of a 100 cm2 perovskite module. The neat polymer retains its HOMO and SCLC mobility, but the module shows center-to-edge fill-factor variation and humidity-induced failure beginning at scribe lines. Define the molecular and coating-process design window and give a staged go/no-go validation plan. Address molecular orientation, conformal coverage, solvent orthogonality, thickness/contact resistance, residual solvent, water and ion ingress, and metal-electrode compatibility. Explain why neat-film mobility, HOMO, and water contact angle are insufficient acceptance criteria.

A continuous gas-medium annealing trial gives delayed nucleation, larger grains, higher Jsc and fill factor, but almost no gain in Voc, PLQY-derived QFLS, or deep-trap density. XPS detects strong nitrogen coordination but weak sulfur coordination, and ToF-SIMS shows the sulfur-containing species concentrated near the gas inlet. Diagnose which part of the coupled process is working and which is failing. Design a minimal experiment set that distinguishes intrinsic gas chemistry from reactor mass-transfer nonuniformity and separates crystallization control from surface passivation. State the spatial and photovoltaic result pattern expected for each hypothesis.

A low-temperature TiO2 electron-transport layer is blended with increasing amounts of reduced graphene oxide. Sheet resistance decreases monotonically and contact-selective PL decays faster, but Voc peaks at an intermediate loading and then falls; hysteresis and spatial dark-current hotspots increase at high loading. Explain how improved conductivity and apparently faster extraction can coexist with worse voltage and hysteresis. Design a loading/structure experiment that distinguishes bulk-ETL transport improvement from direct graphene-perovskite contact, agglomeration, or a work-function/selectivity shift. State the decisive spatial and electrical signatures.

A graphene-based interlayer gives a flexible perovskite module excellent retention after 1000 bending cycles and good dark shelf stability, yet under one-sun MPP at 60 C the module loses Voc near the metal grid and develops a rising series resistance. Build a failure-analysis and redesign plan that determines whether the graphene layer is acting as a useful mechanical/barrier layer, a current-spreading bottleneck, or a chemically active interface. Separate metal-ion intrusion, moisture/oxygen transport, Joule heating, contact delamination, and graphene reduction/functionalization effects. Define the operational evidence required before claiming a stability benefit.

A post-treatment of a 1.7 eV mixed-halide perovskite creates new low-q GIWAXS peaks and triples the TRPL lifetime of the bare film. After PCBM deposition, however, the treated stack also has a longer TRPL lifetime than the untreated stack, transient photocurrent extraction is slower, and device Voc is unchanged. Does this evidence establish a beneficial surface 2D/3D heterostructure? Construct a diagnostic chain that distinguishes an ultrathin passivating, electron-selective 2D layer from a transport-blocking thick layer, bulk low-dimensional conversion, or an unintended spacer-host side-reaction product. Give the expected structural, depth, energetic and kinetic signatures.

You want to transfer a dual-cation strategy that suppresses a diammonium-spacer/FA side reaction to a different wide-bandgap absorber with lower FA content, higher Br fraction, and a different electron-transport layer. Design the minimum chemical factorial and validation sequence needed before using the same recipe. Determine whether the small cation still suppresses the unwanted reaction, whether it instead drives halide exchange or the wrong low-dimensional n phase, and whether the resulting surface remains electron selective. Include coupled light-bias stability and explicit rejection criteria.

During low-temperature single-solvent vacuum flashing, XRD collected immediately after a 40 s pump-down shows no solvent-adduct peaks. After the film is held for two minutes at room temperature, adduct peaks appear and then disappear as the film dries, while FTIR indicates residual solvent from the beginning. A researcher concludes that the adduct forms only after vacuum flashing and is irrelevant to the initial capping/solvent-flux mechanism. Critique this inference and design a time-resolved experiment that distinguishes de novo adduct formation during aging from ordering of a pre-existing amorphous or nanoscale solvent-rich intermediate. State how the result should be related to buried-void formation.

A pilot line must screen a new single solvent for vacuum-flash deposition of a perovskite absorber. The team proposes to copy the coldplate temperature, pressure and hold time optimized for DMF. Build a solvent-selection and process-map framework that determines whether the new solvent can form a useful transient capping state without leaving a persistent coordinating adduct. Address vapor pressure/boiling behavior, metal-ion coordination strength, adduct lifetime, freezing point and viscosity, hygroscopicity, wet-film thickness and web speed. Predict the high-flux and low-flux failure morphologies and define film, device and operational go/no-go tests.

A lightly alkali-modified planar perovskite shows a longer photoluminescence lifetime, slightly higher contactless mobility, and comparable current-voltage hysteresis only when scanned two to three orders of magnitude faster than the control. Determine whether the change arises mainly from lower mobile-ion density, faster ionic equilibration, reduced electronic recombination, or altered contact capacitance. Design the minimum orthogonal measurement set and give the expected signature of each mechanism.

Two semi-transparent photovoltaic windows have the same power-conversion efficiency and photopically weighted average visible transmittance. Device A transmits narrow green and red bands but suppresses blue light; Device B is nearly neutral in the visible yet transmits substantially more near-infrared solar heat. Explain why the two devices are not application-equivalent, and construct a measurement and modeling framework that ranks daylight quality, thermal performance, and photovoltaic output without collapsing them into a single AVT value.

A one-square-metre laminated semi-transparent photovoltaic window meets its average PCE and AVT targets, but shows cross-window color bands, fill-factor loss toward the busbars, and edge-localized degradation after thermal cycling. Build a transfer and qualification plan that separates transparent-electrode sheet resistance, optical-thickness nonuniformity and cavity effects, coating defects, and encapsulation failure. Define spatial metrology, accelerated stresses, and pass/fail criteria appropriate for a building product.

The selective-layer/mesoporous-scaffold concept must be transferred to a flexible inverted perovskite module whose polymer substrate cannot tolerate the high-temperature NiOx and Al2O3 processes used on glass. Propose a low-temperature functional equivalent and a qualification plan. Preserve hole selectivity, conformal coverage of rough electrodes, optical transmission, perovskite infiltration, and mechanical reliability, while defining failure signatures and rejection criteria.

After light soaking an all-perovskite two-terminal tandem, short-circuit current and fill factor decrease while total open-circuit voltage changes little. Construct a diagnostic sequence that distinguishes wide-bandgap halide segregation, narrow-bandgap Sn oxidation or self-doping, and increased interconnecting-layer resistance or recombination. Use subcell-selective optical and electrical measurements, and state the signature that would assign the dominant loss to each subsystem.

An all-perovskite two-terminal tandem is being scaled to a monolithic module using solution-coated wide- and narrow-bandgap absorbers and a thin recombination interlayer. Local spectral or thickness variation creates current mismatch, and partial shading produces hotspots. Build a process, architecture, and qualification strategy that prevents lower-subcell damage, interlayer failure, reverse-bias cascading, and hidden local mismatch. Include spatial controls, coupled stresses, and module-level rejection rules.

A molecular additive for a lead-halide perovskite both absorbs near-ultraviolet light and coordinates Pb species. Relative to an untreated film, the treated film shows stronger and more uniform photoluminescence, a longer TRPL lifetime, a lower SCLC trap-filled-limit voltage, less non-perovskite-phase diffraction, and much less metallic Pb after 365 nm aging. Explain why this evidence does not uniquely identify a single protection mechanism. Design the smallest convincing control matrix and measurement logic that can separate three contributions: (i) chemical passivation of Pb-related deep traps, (ii) optical attenuation or down-shifting of ultraviolet photons, and (iii) stabilization of perovskite crystallization or phase thermodynamics. State the signatures that would support each contribution.

Two organic molecules have comparably high photoluminescence quantum yield and are deposited at a SnO2/perovskite buried interface. Both modestly smooth SnO2 and accelerate perovskite conversion, but only molecule A produces favorable electron-extraction energetics, a low trap density, a void-poor buried interface, and a large gain in Voc and fill factor; molecule B gives much smaller device gains. Construct a mechanistic diagnosis showing why high PLQY or photon down-conversion alone is insufficient. Design a minimal set of controls that partitions four possible contributions: optical wavelength conversion, chemical coordination to undercoordinated Pb, interfacial electrostatic/band-alignment effects, and crystallization or void suppression. State how the expected signatures differ.

A fluorescent buried-interface treatment is being transferred from small cells to a monolithic perovskite module. Preliminary tests show improved UV durability, but the stability devices use a different hole-transport material than the champion cells, and the encapsulation status is not consistently documented. Design an attribution and scale-up qualification matrix that can establish whether the treatment itself improves module durability rather than the altered stack, encapsulation, temperature, or nonuniform light distribution. Include spatial diagnostics and a falsifiable criterion that distinguishes optical UV protection from chemical/electronic interface stabilization.

A buried-interface coordinator produces a perovskite film with stronger preferred orientation, a smaller near-interface tensile-strain gradient, fewer electronic traps, and faster selective charge extraction. These endpoint correlations do not establish whether surface-templated nucleation causes strain relief and defect reduction, whether strain relief drives the improved orientation, or whether defect passivation changes crystallization secondarily. Propose a time-resolved and depth-resolved experiment that can determine the causal order among these three mechanisms. Include molecular controls and state the temporal signatures expected if each mechanism is primary.

After thermal aging of a perovskite/organic-hole-transport-layer stack, the measured TRPL lifetime becomes longer even though device Voc, fill factor, and shunt resistance deteriorate and microscopy reveals holes or ruptures in the transport layer. Explain why the longer lifetime must not be interpreted automatically as fewer perovskite defects. Propose a diagnostic sequence that distinguishes genuine bulk or interfacial passivation from slowed hole extraction caused by an extraction barrier, transport-layer rupture, or formation of a wide-bandgap interfacial product. State the mutually consistent optical, electrical, and morphological signatures for the competing explanations.

Hydroxylating textured FTO before depositing a phosphonic-acid self-assembled monolayer produces a lower water contact angle, more uniform work function, stronger phosphorus signal after deposition, and much better SAM retention after a DMF wash. Design a mechanistic experiment that rules out the simpler explanation that increased wettability and initial coverage alone account for the solvent resistance. Your design should independently vary surface hydroxyl reactivity and wettability, include a molecular control for phosphonate condensation, and specify direct or near-direct evidence for P-O-Sn chemical anchoring. State the outcome pattern that would establish chemical bonding as the controlling factor.

A new molecular interlayer raises the initial VOC by 80 mV and increases absorber/contact PLQY, but under 85 °C maximum-power-point operation the device gradually loses fill factor, develops stronger hysteresis, and shows increased leakage current. Formulate a go/no-go validation plan that determines whether the interlayer genuinely suppresses non-radiative recombination without merely shifting the dominant failure mode to ion migration or contact instability. Specify the evidence required at absorber, interface, and complete-device levels, and state clear rejection criteria.

A surface-treated CsPbI3 film shows stronger steady-state PL and a longer lifetime when measured without an electron-transport layer, but shows much stronger PL quenching after PCBM is deposited. UPS places the treated surface Fermi level closer to the conduction band, and depth profiling confines the treatment-derived ions to the near-surface region. Explain why these observations are mutually consistent rather than contradictory. If the treatment works as intended, predict the directions of change in VOC, fill factor, dark current, ideality factor, built-in potential and hysteresis.

A 20 cm blade-coated perovskite wet film has nearly uniform thickness immediately after coating. During drying, the edges crystallize first while the center retains a solvent-Pb2+ intermediate. After annealing, the edges are dense and fine-grained, but the center contains sparse large grains and pinholes. Explain the spatial failure mechanism in terms of supersaturation, nucleation density, intermediate-phase conversion, and mass/heat transfer. Distinguish a crystallization-kinetic defect from an initial coating-hydrodynamic defect, and identify in situ measurements that would discriminate between them.

After a thermally activated bulky-ligand treatment, UPS shows a 0.58 eV work-function decrease, the valence-band onset shifts relative to the Fermi level, and all perovskite XPS core levels move by about 0.20 eV toward higher binding energy. The chemical signal is confined to approximately the top nanometre. After deposition of a thin C60 layer, the electron-extraction barrier is nearly eliminated. Separate the likely contributions of a surface dipole and genuine n-type surface band bending. Why is the work-function change alone insufficient to prove doping, and what depth-dependent experiment would most directly resolve the two effects?

Develop a screening framework for a new bulky ammonium halide intended to form a thermally activated, anchored surface layer on an inverted perovskite before C60 deposition. The design must avoid a thick physisorbed organic barrier and early burn-in while preserving the three-dimensional absorber. Define the required chemical, thermal, electronic, device and stability criteria, and give explicit rejection conditions.

During operando testing of a 1.75 eV mixed-halide perovskite device, a weak red-shifted PL shoulder near 1.60 eV appears at the illuminated surface within tens of seconds and JSC decreases, although the bulk absorption edge remains nearly unchanged. Over the next hour, iodide enrichment becomes visible along grain boundaries and hysteresis grows. Assign the fast and slow processes, explain why a small-volume surface phase can cause a large current loss, and state one observation that would falsify the proposed assignment.

Two 1.75 eV tandem-top-cell absorbers have the same composition. A thicker, more strained film shows a smaller bulk ionic response in impedance measurements but develops stronger surface red-shifted PL and loses JSC under illumination. A thinner film shows a larger ionic response yet better carrier extraction and more stable maximum-power output. How should thickness and interface architecture be optimized? Explain why minimizing a single ion-migration proxy can select the wrong design, and propose a multi-objective validation protocol.

An inverted MAPbI3 planar cell with a fullerene electron-contact layer gives nearly identical forward and reverse J-V curves under one scan protocol, while a TiO2-based normal cell shows a larger scan-direction difference. The fullerene stack also shows faster photoluminescence decay and higher electron-transport conductivity. Explain why these observations do not by themselves prove that the inverted device is intrinsically hysteresis-free or that ion migration has been eliminated. Design a measurement protocol that distinguishes true suppression of interfacial charge accumulation and recombination from scan-rate masking, preconditioning, capacitive displacement current, and faster electronic extraction that merely outruns a slower ionic process. State the signatures required for a defensible mechanistic conclusion.

A technoeconomic study predicts that a locally owned perovskite-module factory can reach cost competitiveness at tens of megawatts per year, whereas crystalline-silicon manufacturing requires a much larger plant. The model also assumes lower local labour costs, avoided import tariffs, and a favourable demand forecast. Design an analysis that determines whether the apparent small-scale advantage is genuinely caused by the perovskite manufacturing route rather than by optimistic country assumptions or by comparing unlike factory boundaries. Specify the causal variables, normalization, sensitivity and uncertainty methods, counterfactuals, and decision criteria that should be reported.

A printable low-melting alloy back electrode gives fresh inverted perovskite cells with faster transient photocurrent and a longer transient-photovoltage decay than a Cu control, yet the alloy cells have lower short-circuit current and a higher electron-trap density. After prolonged air aging, the Cu-containing electron-only stack develops an extremely long photoluminescence decay while its charge extraction becomes much slower and device performance collapses. Reconcile these apparently contradictory observations. Explain why a longer or shorter optical/electrical lifetime can change meaning with stack and aging state, and construct a diagnostic decision tree that distinguishes productive extraction, reduced recombination, trap filling, contact blocking, electrode corrosion, and optical artifacts.

A blade-printed fusible alloy is proposed as the back electrode for a commercial inverted perovskite module because it avoids vacuum deposition and is less reactive toward iodide than Cu or Ag. Develop an alloy-selection and module-integration specification that balances printing temperature, service-temperature margin, creep and thermal expansion, work function and contact selectivity, wetting and pattern fidelity, oxidation/corrosion resistance, and compatibility with the electron-transport/buffer layers. Then design an accelerated validation program that distinguishes true operational durability from favourable room-temperature shelf storage.

An ordered porous PbI2 scaffold gives excellent 0.05 cm2 cells, but transfer to a 15 cm2 six-subcell module produces fill-factor loss and spatially intermittent shunts. Design a scale-up and reliability plan that tests whether the fast-conversion mechanism remains beneficial at module scale rather than creating local over-conversion, residual PbI2, or imprint-induced thickness defects. Define controllable process variables, spatially resolved acceptance metrics, precursor-aging controls, and at least two operational stability tests that go beyond shelf storage.

In a co-evaporation study, increasing absorber deposition rate by fiftyfold preserves average composition and XRD orientation, yet PLQY, carrier lifetime, and device Voc all decrease while grains become smaller. Bulk XRF still reports the target elemental ratio. Construct a diagnostic decision tree that separates organic-precursor decomposition or incorrect incorporation, kinetically frozen bulk defects, interface-limited recombination, and optical or morphological artifacts. State the rate-matched controls and measurements that make each explanation falsifiable, and explain why bulk composition and XRD alone are insufficient.

A manufacturer must choose fully co-evaporated, sequential-vapor, or vapor/solution-hybrid top-cell processing for a textured-silicon tandem line. The target is conformal coverage, approximately one-minute absorber formation, high yield, and minimal damage to the bottom cell. Develop a stage-gated route-selection framework rather than naming a universal winner. Identify the dominant risk unique to each route, the measurements required before CAPEX commitment, and the conditions under which a hybrid route should be preferred despite adding a wet step.

An epitaxial perovskite heterostructure performs well on a 5 mm crystal but loses uniformity after transfer to a 150 mm substrate and after deposition of charge-selective contacts. Propose an integration-qualification plan that tests whether epitaxial coherence, strain, band alignment, and low defect density survive both scale-up and full-stack fabrication. Include spatial metrology, thermal-expansion and phase-transition risks, contact compatibility, and a decision rule for choosing a lattice-matched substrate, a compliant buffer, or a van der Waals template.

A directional-crystallization recipe developed by spin coating must be transferred to blade-coated wide-bandgap perovskite on a thermally fragile self-assembled monolayer for tandem manufacturing. Copying seed and inhibitor concentrations directly fails because drying, solvent extraction, and thermal gradients differ. Define a transferable process-control strategy based on nucleation asymmetry rather than recipe identity. Which measurable descriptors should be held constant or deliberately scanned, and which device and stability gates would demonstrate that high-dimensional defects—not only surface traps—remain suppressed after scale-up?

A lead-free absorber has a nominally optimal band gap, strong visible absorption, and a low trap density inferred from SCLC, yet complete devices show low EQE, low Jsc, and poor fill factor. Build a diagnostic hierarchy that tests whether the bottleneck is an indirect or parity-forbidden transition, high exciton binding, poor mobility or network connectivity, oxidation-driven self-doping, unfavorable interfaces, or film morphology. Explain why band gap, absorption coefficient, and SCLC trap density cannot by themselves establish photovoltaic suitability.

A nanoimprinted texture in the perovskite active layer increases band-edge absorption and short-circuit current in a solar cell. When the same texture is copied directly into a perovskite LED, the initially extracted light increases but the external quantum efficiency, operating voltage and lifetime deteriorate. Redesign the photonic intervention so that it improves LED outcoupling without sacrificing internal radiative efficiency, charge injection or operational stability. Specify the preferred structure location, optical design variables, electrical controls and acceptance criteria.

During zero-bias operation of a perovskite-BiVO4 artificial leaf with a Cu-In cathode, the total photocurrent remains nearly constant for many hours, but the CO faradaic efficiency decreases while the H2 faradaic efficiency increases. Construct a diagnostic strategy that distinguishes (i) Cu-In surface reconstruction, (ii) CO2 availability or local-pH drift, and (iii) degradation of the photovoltaic absorber or photoanode. State the expected signatures and the controls required for a causal conclusion.

A millisecond plasma-spray process produces a best perovskite solar cell comparable to the best spin-coated control, yet its 25-device batch has a lower mean efficiency and a much larger spread. Explain why these results are not contradictory and design a spatially resolved experiment that identifies whether the variance originates from nonuniform wet-film deposition, nonuniform plasma dose, an excessively narrow crystallization window, or downstream device fabrication. State the expected signatures of under-processing and over-processing.

A rapid air-plasma curing recipe optimized for MAPbI3 on rigid glass is to be transferred to a flexible, mixed-cation FA/Cs perovskite module on a moving web. Propose a transfer and qualification strategy that preserves millisecond crystallization while avoiding plasma damage, substrate distortion and false claims of durability. Identify which chemical and process parameters must be re-derived rather than copied, the inline feedback required, and the mechanical and operational tests needed before module deployment.

During a temperature ramp of a chloride-assisted methylammonium lead halide film, the perovskite diffraction peak first shifts much faster than expected from ordinary thermal expansion, then follows the expansion trend of chloride-free MAPbI3 after substantial volatile release. At the onset of structural degradation, mass spectrometry detects methylamine- and chloromethane-related fragments, but crystalline PbI2 does not rise strongly. Construct a diagnostic strategy that distinguishes lattice-composition change from thermal strain, phase coexistence, and instrument drift. Then infer a chemically consistent two-stage degradation pathway and state which observations would falsify it.

A small amount of chloride is used as a transient processing aid because it accelerates formation of dense MAPbI3 films, but chloride-assisted films can also begin thermochemical decomposition earlier than chloride-free films. Design a manufacturing process window and qualification protocol that preserves the crystallization benefit while minimizing volatile-assisted degradation. Your answer must address solvent choice, film-thickness and heating-rate effects, residual chloride, thermal-budget definition, and the difference between a film-level decomposition test and operational device stability.

A nominally single-phase, high-bromide mixed I/Br perovskite has a clean absorption edge and no resolvable secondary phase in conventional XRD, yet it develops a strong red-shifted sub-bandgap photoluminescence band. Design a decisive experiment to distinguish among three explanations: pre-existing iodide-rich minority domains, light-induced halide segregation, and radiative emission through deep localized traps. Predict the time, fluence, temperature, spatial, and structural signatures expected for each mechanism, and explain why the steady-state PL spectrum alone is insufficient.

You must develop a roughly 1.7-1.8 eV mixed-cation mixed-halide top cell for a perovskite/silicon tandem. A composition-only calculation identifies several MA/FA-I/Br formulations with the target band gap, but some show sub-bandgap emission, hysteresis, and asymmetric residual lead-halide conversion. Propose a multiobjective composition-process-device optimization strategy. Define the minimum screening matrix, the measurements that prevent selection of a deceptively suitable band gap, and the operational stability criteria for choosing a manufacturable top-cell formulation.

A dual-source vapour-deposition process is scaled from small substrates to a large planar perovskite module. The large-area film has nearly unchanged absorption, but local fill factor and electroluminescence degrade near the chamber edges after thermal aging. Develop a process-transfer and aging protocol that determines whether the failure originates from absorber mobility-lifetime degradation, precursor-flux/stoichiometry gradients, or contact and interconnection resistance. Explain how film-level THz results should be used without treating them as a substitute for device measurements.

During maximum-power-point aging of a perovskite device, external electroluminescence efficiency and TRPL lifetime both decline, while the absorber's steady-state absorption spectrum remains nearly unchanged. Design a before-and-after diagnostic protocol that separates changes in the intrinsic radiative coefficient from increased nonradiative recombination, altered optical outcoupling or photon recycling, and contact/injection degradation. State the minimum measurements and the decision logic needed before using luminescence loss as a stability metric.

A fully alkylated, hydrophobic onium additive improves humid-dark stability in a spin-coated MAPbI3 proof-of-concept, but increasing its concentration lowers module fill factor when the concept is transferred to a mixed-cation wide-bandgap absorber. Develop a go/no-go transfer program that distinguishes molecular suppression of proton-transfer chemistry from a simple physical water barrier, detects formation of transport-blocking low-dimensional phases, and determines the required additive dose and spatial localization for scalable devices.

A candidate coordination molecule used during deposition of a wide-bandgap top absorber produces room-temperature alpha-phase nuclei, columnar grains, little residual PbI2, and complete conversion after a mild anneal on textured silicon. Yet adding the electron-selective fullerene contact gives no voltage improvement and lowers fill factor. Explain why the structural success does not identify the electronically limiting step. Build a diagnostic tree that distinguishes a defective buried hole contact, recombination at the exposed top surface, unfavorable contact energetics, and a resistive molecular residue, and state the signature expected for each failure mode.

A mild-anneal coating chemistry has produced a high-efficiency 1 cm2 monolithic tandem on micrometer-textured silicon. Develop a go/no-go program for transferring the process to large-area modules. The program must control conformal phase conversion over pyramid tops, sidewalls, valleys, and edges; molecular residue at the electron contact; subcell current matching; sheet and interconnect resistance; spatial yield; and operational durability. Explain why low thermal budget and a champion small-cell result are not sufficient evidence of manufacturability.

In a dose series of an amidino Dion-Jacobson additive in a 3D FAPbI3 absorber, low dose introduces weak low-n excitonic features, fast low-n-to-3D energy transfer, higher quasi-Fermi-level splitting, and better fill factor. At higher dose, the low-n features intensify, PL lifetime continues to increase, but mobility, short-circuit current, and fill factor decline. Diagnose the transition from a beneficial sparse 2D/3D skeleton/passivating heterostructure to a transport-blocking low-dimensional network. Design depth-, orientation-, kinetic-, and device-level measurements that distinguish true passivation from carrier confinement or extraction blockage.

A low-dose amidino Dion-Jacobson additive is proposed for both rigid TiO2-based and flexible SnO2-based perovskite cells. In the rigid process, every film also receives a PEAI surface treatment, while the flexible process uses a lower annealing temperature and a different substrate/contact stack. Design a factorial study that determines whether the efficiency and stability gains are intrinsic to the bulk 2D/3D additive, arise from synergy with PEAI, or depend on the processing temperature and substrate. Include mechanistic readouts and condition-specific ambient, light, thermal, and bending tests.

Design a perovskite photovoltaic module around a triggered-disassembly interface that remains mechanically and chemically stable during multi-year outdoor operation but separates cleanly at end of life. Explain the fundamental conflict between operational stability and easy delamination, propose a trigger and stack placement that avoid accidental activation, and define the tests needed to prove that the design improves closed-loop recovery without increasing lead-release risk or merely shifting environmental burden to the disassembly chemistry.

A formamidinium-halide treatment of a PbS colloidal-quantum-dot solid increases conductivity, usable active-layer thickness, short-circuit current, and fill factor. Steady-state photoluminescence decreases slightly, yet a pump-probe or terahertz photoconductivity signal decays more slowly. A researcher concludes that the treatment simultaneously increases carrier lifetime and mobility through trap passivation. Critique this conclusion and specify the minimum measurement set needed to separate carrier-population recombination, time-dependent hopping mobility, stronger interdot coupling, unintentional doping, and contact-layer effects.

A laboratory formamidinium-halide treatment is to be transferred from thin, small-area PbS quantum-dot films to approximately micrometre-thick coated modules. Define a scalable process window that yields a uniform monolayer-bridge regime rather than under-treated regions or residual bulk perovskite/PbI2. Specify the critical variables, in-line or lot-release measurements, and accelerated tests needed to show that improved coupling survives thickness scale-up, thermal stress, and contact integration.

During an illumination experiment, operando XPS shows a metallic-Pb signal growing in a perovskite film, and the investigator attributes it to intrinsic photoreduction of the stoichiometric perovskite lattice. Design a falsification workflow that separates three possibilities: metallic Pb existed before measurement, illumination generated it from residual PbI2, or the X-ray probe generated it during acquisition. State the decisive controls and the different outcome expected for each mechanism.

A manufacturing line intentionally uses a small excess of PbI2 because it improves initial fill factor, but module batches show variable light-soaking stability after the PbI2 precursor has been stored or transported. Develop a process-control strategy that preserves any useful passivation while suppressing metallic-Pb formation. Include precursor-history controls, a post-crystallization intervention, in-line or release diagnostics, and a stress matrix that can distinguish a bandgap/current-generation change from recombination, electrostatic, and trap-mediated degradation.

A quasi-two-dimensional surface treatment suppresses low-frequency capacitance growth and scan hysteresis and improves humidity tolerance, but the treated device gains open-circuit voltage while losing short-circuit current and fill factor. Develop a design-transfer strategy that retains ionic and chemical stabilization without imposing an excitonic or transport bottleneck.
