Specify where the low-dimensional phase should be placed, how its composition and thickness should be optimized, and which electronic, ionic, and stability measurements must agree before the treatment is judged beneficial.

On a coating scale-up line, flat witness films made from the same perovskite ink are dense and show good PL and TRPL, but tandems coated on sub-micrometre-textured silicon develop local shunts, low fill factor, and large spatial variation. Construct a falsifiable diagnosis that distinguishes buried interfacial voiding or premature crystallization, inadequate wetting/planarization, excessive PTAA or contact resistance, and bulk perovskite defects. State the control matrix and the signature expected for each failure mode.

A 26%-efficient small-area blade-coated perovskite/silicon tandem retains most of its efficiency for 100 h under controlled laboratory illumination. Define the design changes and qualification plan required before transferring the architecture to a square-metre outdoor module. Your plan must address coating and texture uniformity, two-terminal current matching, optical layers and encapsulation, interconnection/resistive scaling, and coupled environmental-mechanical stresses. Explain why the 100 h result is insufficient evidence of module durability.

A pilot line produces a 30%-efficient perovskite tandem module whose direct manufacturing cost per square metre is close to target, yet its modeled levelized cost of electricity is worse than that of a 22%-efficient single-junction perovskite module. The tandem uses costly evaporated contact and recombination layers, has lower production yield, a shorter service life, and faster annual degradation, while the two lines have similar facility cost. Diagnose why the efficiency advantage fails to translate into lower LCOE, and specify a sensitivity analysis that would identify the dominant economic penalty.

Two all-perovskite tandem designs are being considered for scale-up. Design A has the higher certified cell efficiency but uses gold, costly organic transport layers, and several vacuum steps. Design B is slightly less efficient but uses abundant electrodes and transport layers compatible with high-utilization printing. Construct a staged down-selection framework that determines which design is more likely to deliver lower commercial LCOE. Include the minimum manufacturing, reliability, and modeling evidence required for a go/no-go decision.

A post-treatment applied to a wide-bandgap perovskite/CsPbI3 quantum-dot bilayer simultaneously replaces or reorganizes quantum-dot surface ligands and drives Br/I interdiffusion across the buried interface. The treated device shows higher photocurrent and fill factor. Design a control matrix that separates the contributions of quantum-dot transport/passivation, a true graded bandgap, and simple extra optical absorption or thickness. State the decisive measurements and the expected signature of each mechanism.

Translate a sequentially deposited wide-bandgap perovskite/CsPbI3 quantum-dot graded absorber from spin coating and repeated dip treatments to a continuous coating process. Propose the critical process window, in-line or at-line quality controls, and reliability safeguards needed to preserve the intended gradient without sacrificing quantum-dot transport or moisture stability.

A buried-interface modifier makes the perovskite photoluminescence decay longer on inert glass but much shorter when the same perovskite is deposited on an electron-selective SnO2 contact. A student argues that the shorter lifetime on SnO2 proves the modifier creates more defects. Explain why the two lifetime trends can instead be mutually consistent with bulk passivation and faster electron extraction, and specify the evidence needed to exclude interfacial non-radiative quenching.

A module line adopts a dipolar self-assembled monolayer intended to strengthen and work-function-match a buried perovskite homojunction, but early modules show cross-web variation in fill factor and localized delamination after light soaking. Design a process-qualification and reliability matrix that determines whether the failure is caused by incomplete monolayer coverage, an incorrect dipole, insufficient adhesion, or downstream perovskite processing. Define suitable negative controls and go/no-go criteria.

A precursor additive produces both strong (100) texture in FAPbI3 and enrichment at the buried SnO2/perovskite interface, where it can coordinate defects. Design a molecular-control experiment that determines how much of the device improvement comes from facet-selective nucleation and how much comes from buried-interface passivation. State the minimum analogue set, measurements, and outcome pattern needed for a causal conclusion.

A one-step bifunctional precursor additive works in spin-coated FAPbI3 because it migrates to the buried SnO2 interface while also directing crystal orientation. You must transfer the concept to slot-die coating and to a different electron-transport layer. Explain why spontaneous buried enrichment may not survive the transfer, and propose a process and materials-validation plan that preserves both orientation control and interface passivation at module scale.

An inverted NiOx/perovskite device is modified with a molecular interlayer. Relative to the control, the SCLC-derived trap density decreases, the slope of Voc versus ln(light intensity) falls from about 2 to about 1.6 kBT/q, and the transient-photovoltage lifetime increases; however, the TRPL lifetime of the perovskite on the modified substrate becomes shorter. UPS and depth-resolved diffraction also show altered interfacial energy alignment and reduced tensile strain. Reconcile these observations. What mechanistic conclusion is justified, and what stronger conclusion is not justified?

A photoactive molecular interlayer is claimed to improve both efficiency and durability through three coupled functions: UV attenuation, buried-interface passivation, and strain relief. Design the smallest convincing aging-and-diagnostics matrix that can separate these contributions and support transfer from small spin-coated cells to coated modules. Specify the stresses, the essential controls, and the readouts that would make the mechanism assignment credible.

Suppose a precursor strategy increases the exciton binding energy of a perovskite absorber without changing its electronic band gap. Under what conditions should this raise Jsc, and under what conditions could it reduce device performance? Give a go/no-go experimental criterion for transferring the strategy to a perovskite with a different band gap and halide composition.

Three hole-transport materials are coated on CsPbI3 nanocrystal films. Material A has the highest bulk hole mobility but gives only moderate device efficiency. Material B has lower mobility, favorable energy levels, a shorter mean PL lifetime with spatially uniform quenching, and interfacial XPS shifts. Doped material C produces dark PL patches even though its AFM surface is smooth. Explain why neither mobility nor mean PL lifetime alone identifies the best contact, and design a control set that distinguishes efficient hole extraction, chemical passivation, and processing-induced damage.

A dopant-free polymeric hole-transport material is selected for a small-area CsPbI3 nanocrystal cell because it gives low voltage loss and reproducible efficiency. Define a transfer protocol for deciding whether it remains the best choice after the nanocrystal surface treatment, band edges, and coating area are changed. Include the materials-screening descriptors and the stability/scale-up stop criteria.

In a wide-band-gap p-i-n perovskite top cell, a low dose of a hydrophobic Lewis-base precursor additive raises Voc and measured FF, but the pseudo-FF changes little and SEM reveals thinner regions and nanoscale pinholes. Adding sparse insulating SiO2 nanoparticles at the Me-4PACz-coated substrate increases FF by several absolute percentage points with less than a 5 mV Voc change, whereas high nanoparticle coverage raises series resistance and hysteresis. Diagnose which loss channels each intervention changes and explain why the optimum must be non-monotonic and conditional.

Translate a coupled hydrophobic-additive/sparse-dielectric-substrate strategy from small spin-coated, front-side-flat tandem cells to slot-die-coated monolithic two-terminal tandems on textured silicon. Which variables must be re-optimized together, and which measurements would show that the apparent synergy survives rather than merely shifting loss among shunting, series resistance, optical current mismatch, and instability?

A molecule that homogenizes strain in a 1.67 eV wide-band-gap perovskite is proposed for a monolithic two-terminal perovskite/silicon tandem using a different Br/I ratio. Give a molecular design rule and a validation plan for this transfer. Explain why maximizing compressive strain is not itself the correct optimization objective.

A manufacturer wants to replace a water-delaminated polyimide/soda-lime-glass carrier with a reusable ceramic carrier and a thin release/barrier stack for flexible perovskite/CIGS tandems. Define which substrate functions must be preserved, how alkali delivery should be re-engineered, and what staged experiments would demonstrate electronic equivalence, tandem-integration compatibility, and reliable release without assuming that identical CIGS crystallinity guarantees identical devices.

In a two-step MA-free perovskite process, adding PbCl2 to the lead-halide precursor improves conversion and grain growth, yet chlorine is absent from the final film. Distinguish two transient mechanisms: chloride templates the precursor before FAI arrival, or chloride acts mainly during FAI conversion through a volatile FACl-containing intermediate. Propose time-resolved placement controls, intermediate-state measurements, opposite predictions, and a causal decision rule.

A hybrid solution-plus-FAI-evaporation process that works on 1 cm2 cells is being developed for 100 cm2 substrates. Build a manufacturing-control and qualification plan for uniform FAI dose, complete conversion, transient chloride removal, and shunt suppression. Which spatial process variables and inline observables should be controlled, and what statistical and aging evidence would justify calling the process scalable rather than merely large-area compatible?

A near-infrared-absorbing multifunctional interlayer that benefits a single-junction inverted perovskite cell is proposed for the perovskite top cell of a monolithic tandem. Explain why this transfer may reduce tandem power even if top-cell Jsc rises. Build an optical-electrical-stability decision workflow comparing full-thickness, ultrathin, nonabsorbing-analog, and ion-blocking-only designs, with subcell-resolved acceptance criteria.

A large-area surface-treatment line for alpha-FAPbI3 must deliver cationic passivation without creating local iodine-rich hot spots that seed phase conversion. Develop a manufacturing control and reliability protocol covering solution composition, coating/drying uniformity, inline defect or phase proxies, spatial acceptance limits, and accelerated tests. How would you prevent a high average PL from hiding a small unstable tail of the coated area?

An ultrathin ligand-seeded Al2O3 barrier optimized on spin-coated wide-bandgap perovskite cells must be transferred to a 100 cm2 slot-die-coated module. The scalable film has greater roughness and a broader surface-composition distribution, while electron extraction cannot tolerate a thick insulating oxide. Propose a scale-up strategy that preserves ion blocking without sacrificing fill factor. Define the molecular and ALD process variables, spatial quality-control metrics, electrical go/no-go criteria, and an accelerated stress matrix capable of locating whether failure originates in the barrier, the electron-transport contact, or another subcell.

CsPbI3 quantum dots are made progressively smaller. The smallest dots retain the photoactive black phase at room temperature and show high PLQY in dilute solution, but their dense films exhibit lower mobility, stronger thermally activated hopping, larger hysteresis, and rapid PL loss after aggressive ligand removal. Explain why these observations are not contradictory. Construct the mechanism linking surface strain, vacancy-rich surfaces, ligand-mediated interparticle coupling, and ion motion, and state which measurements would reveal an optimum rather than a monotonic “smaller is better” or “shorter ligand is better” rule.

An all-quantum-dot CsPbI3 solar cell is efficient when films are deposited from a freshly purified ink and treated by several sequential solid-state ligand exchanges. For roll-to-roll coating, the ink must remain stable for hours, drying is continuous, and ligand exchange must be compressed into one or two passes. Design a manufacturing transfer that preserves black-phase stability and electronic coupling. Identify which ink, exchange, drying, and device-level stability variables must be controlled, and explain why high initial PLQY or a single reverse-scan PCE cannot qualify the process.

Two perovskite precursor formulations produce films with the same final average XRD phase and similar mean grain size. Nevertheless, formulation A gives low hysteresis and uniform luminescence, whereas formulation B develops local voids, broad lifetime distributions, and large hysteresis. Time-resolved diffraction during drying shows that A passes through one dominant intermediate and converts nearly synchronously; B forms several overlapping solvent-adduct intermediates and retains coordinating solvent late into annealing. Explain how the intermediate-state history can create different electronic films despite similar final XRD. Then define the measurements that would distinguish kinetic heterogeneity, residual chemistry, and a purely interfacial device effect.

A spin-coated FAPbI3 recipe using an antisolvent and a volatile additive performs well in a glovebox, but direct transfer to slot-die coating gives large run-to-run variation as humidity, web speed, and solvent evaporation change. Propose a feedback-controlled manufacturing strategy in which the controlled variable is the intermediate-state trajectory rather than a fixed solvent ratio or annealing time. Specify the in-line observables, manipulable process variables, endpoint criteria, and validation needed to show that the same intermediate pathway—not merely a similar final XRD pattern—has been reproduced.

A FIB-prepared lamella from a mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite shows a Cs/Rb-rich feature at several grain boundaries by HAADF-STEM and EDS, although bulk XRD is single phase. During repeated EDS scans of the same boundary, the heavy-cation contrast grows while the halide signal falls. Diagnose the competing explanations: a genuine pre-existing boundary phase, FIB-preparation damage, and electron-beam-induced redistribution or decomposition. Construct the evidence hierarchy needed to decide among them without assuming that either bulk XRD or a single atomic-resolution image is definitive.

After a short UV exposure, low-dose cryo-EM detects approximately 5 nm PbI2 nanograins near the surfaces of MAPbI3 nanowires, while ensemble XRD, absorption, and average photoluminescence show little or no change. Explain why these observations are not contradictory and what they imply about the earliest degradation regime. Then design a discriminating experiment that tests whether PbI2 forms by surface- or defect-localized heterogeneous nucleation rather than by spatially uniform bulk decomposition, without confusing environmental damage with imaging damage.

A research group wants to capture the first seconds of combined light-and-bias degradation in a complete perovskite solar cell by cryo-EM rather than in isolated nanowires. Design a freeze-quench workflow that preserves a defined electrical and optical state while keeping preparation and imaging damage below a specimen-specific dose budget. Specify how the device state should be triggered and frozen, how a cross-sectional lamella should be prepared and imaged, which correlative controls are required, and what conclusions remain invalid because the experiment produces ex situ snapshots rather than a true operando movie.

Identical mixed-halide lead-perovskite films are exposed at equal water activity and equal total oxygen dose to (i) dry O2 under illumination, (ii) H2O vapor under illumination, or (iii) a brief H2O2 vapor pulse in the dark. Only the H2O2-treated films show a large increase in absolute photoluminescence quantum yield and quasi-Fermi-level splitting, while absorption, thickness, roughness, and bulk XRD remain unchanged. XPS shows a new oxygen-related component and a smaller metallic-Pb-related signal, but those correlations do not by themselves prove that peroxide-derived Pb–O formation is the causal passivation event. Design the minimum isotope and counterfactual experiment set needed to distinguish Pb–O defect passivation from solvent cleaning, mild etching, oxygen-induced doping, or a transient surface dipole. State the result pattern that would sustain the Pb–O mechanism and the observations that would falsify it.

A continuous coating line is being developed for gas-phase peroxide passivation of perovskite modules. The vapor dose that maximizes the immediate in-line PL brightness produces lower module output after a downstream 100 °C anneal and encapsulation step. Formulate a process-window and qualification strategy that decides whether the remedy is to lower the oxidative dose, change the treatment position in the stack, or reject the chemistry for that process. Your answer must specify the variables to map, the in-line and off-line endpoints, architecture-specific controls, and the accelerated tests needed to prevent “bright but unstable” films from being accepted.

A manufacturer wants to transfer an interface-confined nucleophilic scavenger strategy from doped Spiro-MeOTAD to a different oxidatively doped triarylamine HTL. The radical cations are necessary for bulk conductivity, but an excess population at the perovskite interface may be recombination-active. Define a go/no-go screening workflow for the new HTL/scavenger pair. Which chemical descriptors, spatial-selectivity tests, transport measurements, and stability experiments are required to prove that the scavenger neutralizes only the harmful interfacial population rather than destroying the useful bulk doping?

Two CIGS/CdS interconnection surfaces have the same RMS roughness, surface chemistry, work function, optical haze, and thickness of every overlying layer. Surface A is a continuous, long-wavelength corrugation with broad concave valleys; surface B contains sparse, sharp convex asperities. Fresh wide-bandgap perovskite films on the two surfaces have matched grain size, XRD, PLQY, and tandem current matching, yet films on A develop fewer deep traps and much less halide segregation during photothermal aging. Explain why RMS roughness is not a sufficient mechanical descriptor. Design the decisive local mapping and counterfactual experiment, and state the spatial correlation pattern required to attribute the stability difference to residual-stress relief rather than to an unrecognized optical, compositional, or contact-resistance effect.

A monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem uses an optically optimized, nearly planar silicon bottom cell that cannot be randomly roughened without causing parasitic absorption, shunts, or current-matching loss. Propose a mechanically equivalent interconnection design that transfers the stress-relief principle without copying the rough CIGS surface. Define the mechanical design variables, the optical/electrical constraints, the decisive validation measurements, and the module-relevant stability tests that would justify adoption.

A tripodal phosphonic-acid hole-collecting molecule on a transparent oxide shows a face-on-sensitive MAES/UPS signature and better device fill factor than a monopodal analogue. However, the tripodal molecule also has a larger molecular footprint and produces more complete effective surface coverage, so orientation and coverage are confounded. Design an orientation-switched counterfactual that uses the same conjugated core and nearly matched anchor chemistry, areal coverage, work function, and HOMO level. Specify how orientation, coverage, vertical transport, and recombination must be measured, and state the outcome pattern required to conclude that face-on orientation itself improves vertical hole extraction.

A roll-coated tripodal phosphonic-acid monolayer on rough FTO has the same average phosphorus loading and average work function as a laboratory spin-coated film on flat ITO, yet large-area devices show a wide distribution of fill factor and thermal stability. Diagnose why the tripodal strategy can fail at scale despite matching those averages. Propose a process-control and quality-assurance hierarchy that detects the relevant low-coverage or misorientation tails before perovskite deposition and verifies that the monolayer remains stable during device operation.

A perovskite deposited on a planar-core dopant-free hole-transport material shows a much shorter bilayer TRPL lifetime than the same perovskite on a nonplanar control. In complete devices, however, the planar-core contact gives a longer transient-photovoltage decay, a lower light-intensity Voc ideality factor, and a higher Voc and fill factor. Explain why the shorter bilayer TRPL and longer device TPV lifetime are not contradictory. Design the minimum measurement sequence that distinguishes fast hole extraction from harmful interfacial quenching and states the result pattern needed to claim simultaneous extraction enhancement and recombination suppression.

A new dopant-free HTM is made even more planar than a successful spiro-linked planar-core molecule. It matches the desired HOMO and gives high hole mobility in small spin-coated cells, but blade-coated 1 cm² films develop crystalline domains during drying and coarsen further during 85 °C aging, causing spatially localized fill-factor loss. Develop a go/no-go screen and molecular/process redesign strategy that preserves the transport benefit of planarity without accepting morphology-driven instability. Include the measurements that must be performed before coating, during scale-up, and under operational stress.

A selectively excited perovskite-nanocrystal/dye hybrid shows three observations: the nanocrystal absorption edge is unchanged by Mn doping; the prompt dye singlet yield is nearly independent of Mn loading; and a microsecond dye-triplet signal grows strongly with Mn loading. A reviewer argues that the triplet is produced by photoinduced charge separation followed by spin-mixed recombination, or by Mn-enhanced intersystem crossing inside the dye, rather than by Mn-to-dye triplet energy transfer. Design a decisive mechanism test. Specify the kinetic correlations, spectral controls, energetic or distance perturbations, and radical-versus-triplet signatures that would discriminate the three hypotheses, and state the expected result pattern for a sequential exciton-to-Mn-to-dye pathway.

A formamidinium-rich iodide perovskite is nearly stable in humid nitrogen and in dry oxygen, but rapidly loses nitrogen and iodine, develops surface iodate species, and converts to nonperovskite phases in humid oxygen. Design an isotope-resolved operando experiment that determines whether water mainly removes FAI while molecular oxygen supplies the oxygen incorporated into iodate, rather than water supplying the iodate oxygen or a hydrate/superoxide pathway independently causing the phase change. Specify the isotope matrix, time- and depth-resolved measurements, volatile products, and the result pattern required for a sequential surface-to-bulk mechanism.

A 100 cm2 formamidinium-rich perovskite module is stable in the interior but begins to fail at laser scribes, pinholes, and poorly sealed edges during humid-air maximum-power operation. Build a prevention and validation strategy based on a coupled water-plus-oxygen, surface-initiated degradation loop rather than on a generic moisture-barrier argument. Specify the surface chemistry, edge/scribe architecture, encapsulation functions, stress matrix, spatial diagnostics, and go/no-go criteria needed to show that FAI loss, iodate formation, and vacancy-assisted inward propagation have all been interrupted.

Across an all-iodide lead-halide series, combining a small A-site cation with intermediate-size organic cations increases the fraction of corner-sharing octahedra and narrows the optical gap, but cation identity also changes strain, electrostatic fields, dynamic disorder, and face-sharing content. Design a causal experiment that determines whether octahedral connectivity is the dominant cause of the bandgap change rather than an incidental correlate of organic-cation chemistry. Include the structural variables, matched chemical controls, lattice-only or cation-only perturbations, electronic-structure tests, and the result pattern that would establish connectivity as the mediator.

An all-iodide 2.0 eV perovskitoid is considered for a monolithic tandem top cell because it does not undergo mixed-halide light segregation. Its film and XRD are light-stable, but the first devices have a high open-circuit voltage, low fill factor, broad luminescence, and highly anisotropic calculated bands. Define the structure, texture, contact, and thickness design window needed to decide whether the intrinsic stability advantage can become a useful top-cell technology. Give matched controls and operational go/no-go criteria that separate absorber stability from transport, interface, and electrode failure.

A methylammonium-chloride-assisted FAPbI3 process gives larger grains and a small bandgap increase, but the result depends strongly on solvent, ink residence time, and thermal history; long heating also produces a yellow low-angle-XRD phase. Design a factorial and isotope-tracing experiment that separates three possible contributions: a transient volatile methylammonium crystallization aid, residual chloride in cubic FAPbI3, and irreversible methylamine attack on formamidinium producing methylated FA species and a stable 2H side phase. Specify the additive controls, labels, time-resolved measurements, and the signature assigned to each contribution.

A slot-die FAPbI3 line uses an MACl-containing ink that may remain in a 35-45 C reservoir for eight hours before coating. The web later passes through a nonuniform thermal zone, and production shows roll-to-roll drift in color, bandgap, phase purity, and device voltage. Build a process-control and reformulation plan that treats the ink as a reactive chemical system rather than a stable salt solution. Define the critical material attributes, inline/offline assays, thermal-residence controls, alternative-additive logic, sampling plan across the web, and explicit rejection criteria for methylated-FA side products, residual chloride, and 2H-phase nucleation.

A manufacturer wants to coat an n=3 layered lead-iodide absorber using an allylammonium/iodopropylammonium spacer mixture. In concentrated iodide acid and heat, the allyl group can convert to the iodopropyl product; small changes in thermal history therefore shift spacer ratio, dimensionality, stacking, and trap emission, and low-n byproducts may be 0D or 1D. Define a chemically robust precursor and coating strategy and a staged go/no-go plan. Address spacer identity control, reaction kinetics, phase-map construction, orientation, trap-state control, mechanical/thermal reliability, and why nominal precursor stoichiometry or PXRD alone is insufficient.

A metal-halide perovskite shows two responses when holes accumulate: its photoluminescence lifetime falls within microseconds, whereas a halide-composition gradient develops over seconds to minutes. Design a causal experiment that distinguishes a direct hole-induced increase in nonradiative recombination from an indirect pathway in which holes first accelerate ion migration and the migrated ionic configuration then increases recombination. Specify the perturbation matrix, time-resolved measurements, decisive signatures for each pathway, and controls for electric-field and heating artifacts.

A device team proposes suppressing halide migration by making the hole-transport layer thicker and shifting its ionization energy farther from the perovskite valence band. Evaluate why this strategy could worsen, rather than cure, coupled ionic and nonradiative losses. Propose a functionally safer contact design and a qualification plan that demonstrates reduced hole accumulation and ion motion without sacrificing voltage or fill factor.

Develop a minimally perturbative protocol for diagnosing a metastable perovskite/silicon tandem during accelerated aging. The protocol must separate recombination, contact selectivity, transport resistance, current mismatch, and spatially localized damage while also proving that the diagnostic sequence itself has not light-soaked, polarized, or otherwise changed the device state.

Design a perovskite/silicon tandem module strategy for suppressing negative-potential-induced degradation when the suspected failure involves perovskite constituents entering the encapsulant rather than sodium entering from glass. Address module electrical architecture, encapsulation and barrier materials, accelerated qualification, subcell-resolved diagnostics, and the tradeoffs that prevent simply specifying a thicker electrical insulator.

A researcher wants to convert electrically programmed halide redistribution in a two-dimensional perovskite heterostructure into a nonvolatile ionic diode or optical memory. Define a device architecture, programming/read scheme, and qualification matrix that demonstrate useful, repeatable ionic state control rather than progressive electrochemical degradation. Include geometry, edge management, retention, endurance, thermal controls, and chemical failure criteria.

A perovskite-ink additive is a salt containing a redox-active anion and a coordinating divalent metal cation. Devices show higher voltage and fill factor, but the films also develop smaller grains. Design a minimal orthogonal experiment that determines whether the gain arises from iodine reduction, sequestration of excess iodide by metal coordination or precipitation, generic morphology change, or synergy between the two ionic components. Include chemical challenge experiments and decisive solution, film, and device readouts.

A pilot line selects a textured p-type TOPCon recipe solely because it gives the highest implied open-circuit voltage on small symmetric lifetime coupons. When transferred to full bottom cells, the actual voltage gain is small, fill factor decreases, and monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems show large device-to-device spread. Propose a staged qualification strategy that determines where the coupon-level gain is being lost and whether the process is suitable for scale-up. Your strategy must separate precursor passivation, completed-contact transport, full-wafer uniformity, tandem-integration effects and operational stability. Define scientifically justified go/no-go criteria and explain why maximizing coupon iVOC is not an adequate production objective.

A carbonyl-containing polymer additive produces larger perovskite grains, longer carrier lifetime, lower hysteresis and improved moisture, heat and light stability. These observations could arise from at least three different causes: altered solution rheology/drying and nucleation, Lewis-base passivation of undercoordinated Pb, or a thermally retained macromolecular bridge that impedes ion migration after crystallization. Design an orthogonal control and perturbation strategy that separates these three contributions. State which in-situ, post-anneal and stress-dependent signatures would be required before concluding that a retained perovskite-polymer composite bridge is the dominant mechanism rather than a transient crystallization aid or a generic hydrophobic coating.

A polymeric Lewis-base additive that works in a small-area single-halide perovskite must be transferred to a slot-die-coated, wide-bandgap mixed-halide top cell for a tandem module. Propose a design-of-experiments and qualification framework for selecting polymer coordination density, molecular weight, loading and coating conditions. Explain the competing risks created by stronger binding and higher molecular weight, how mixed-halide phase segregation and inter-grain transport should be tested, and why open-circuit shelf or illumination stability cannot substitute for module-relevant maximum-power-point qualification.

Two amine treatments are applied to the same lead-halide perovskite surface. A monodentate molecule and a bidentate molecule are chosen so that both produce nearly the same initial work-function shift and similar improvement in quasi-Fermi-level splitting. Only the bidentate treatment forms a compact chelated lead-halide surface phase and retains low iodide migration during prolonged bias and illumination. Design an evidence chain that determines whether the long-term advantage is caused by a persistent chelated surface skeleton rather than by an interfacial dipole, generic defect passivation or hydrophobicity. Include matched controls, structural perturbations, electronic measurements and stress-dependent predictions.

A chelated lead-octahedron surface layer was optimized on the hole-extraction side of an n-i-p perovskite cell, where its wide bandgap and upward band bending were beneficial. You now want to use the same chemical concept on the electron-extraction side of a wide-bandgap p-i-n top cell in a monolithic tandem. Develop a transfer protocol that decides whether the surface reconstruction is compatible with electron extraction. Address energy-level orientation, conversion depth and thickness, mixed-halide ion/phase stability, contact formation and tandem-level qualification. State the evidence that would justify transfer and the observations that would force redesign rather than simple concentration adjustment.

A thick graphene-filled fullerene layer is to be scaled from a small rigid cell to a large-area, low-temperature-processed perovskite module. Increasing thickness and graphene loading should increase tortuosity against ions and water, but can also increase series resistance, roughness, aggregation and coating defects. Develop a transport-barrier co-optimization and qualification framework. Explain how you would select thickness, filler loading and electrode-contact modifier, diagnose rare pinholes or agglomerates at module scale, and demonstrate that long lifetime is not merely an artifact of encapsulation or an initially favorable contact.

In a laterally decoupled perovskite photocathode, catalyst-side near-infrared excitation produces an immediate current increase but a much larger long-term stability improvement. Design a dynamic perturbation experiment that separates four possible contributions: faster interfacial HER charge transfer, faster bubble detachment, direct heating of the perovskite photovoltaic subcell, and reduced charge-accumulation-driven ion migration. Use independently modulated catalyst heating/NIR, mechanical stirring, electrical load and illumination intensity. Specify the observables and response times that would support or falsify each contribution.

A sequential crown-ether/alkali host treatment followed by an organic-ammonium guest treatment works on small spin-coated cells, but it must be transferred to a 100 cm2 coated module. The main scale-up risks are nonuniform host-guest stoichiometry, crown-rich insulating patches, incomplete guest complexation, and accidental formation of a layered 2D perovskite. Define a process-control and acceptance protocol that can detect these failure modes before long-duration MPP testing. Include chemical/phase, spatial, electronic and device-level criteria.

A particle-assisted nucleation process developed on 2 micrometer pyramids must be transferred to a production texture whose height varies from 2 to 4 micrometers and to a scalable coating/drying route. Explain which geometric and kinetic ratios should be preserved rather than copying a single particle loading. Define a scale-up process window and the measurements required to reject optical, electrical or stability penalties.

A porous amine/amide-functionalized carbon trap removes about 88% of dissolved Pb within 5 minutes and more than 98% at equilibrium. Its uptake is fitted well by a pseudo-second-order model, but Pb sequestration is weaker in river water than in deionized water. State what these observations do and do not prove about the adsorption mechanism. Design a control set that quantitatively separates capillary/mass-transfer capture from ligand chelation and explains the matrix dependence.

A phosphonic-acid self-assembled monolayer with a conformationally flexible donor head and a rigid conjugated linker gives better buried-interface contact, lower perovskite strain and better charge extraction than controls. Design a 2 x 2 molecular experiment that can prove a genuine head-linker synergy rather than two unrelated improvements. Specify the four molecular classes, the variables that must be held constant, the diagnostic measurements and the interaction pattern that would support synergy.

A SAM selected for high efficiency on rigid glass is being transferred to a flexible perovskite module that will experience repeated bending together with 85 degrees C illumination. Design a qualification protocol that distinguishes reversible molecular conformational reorientation from irreversible chemical degradation, loss of SAM anchoring, or electronic discontinuity. State how the protocol should decide between an overly rigid head group and an overly flexible nonconjugated linker.

A semitransparent planar perovskite solar cell delivers a substantially lower short-circuit current under rear illumination than under front illumination. The rear contact is a transparent conducting oxide deposited through a protective buffer. Design a diagnosis that can determine whether the directional asymmetry is dominated by optical filtering and optical-field redistribution or by electrically damaging the rear interface during electrode deposition. State the directional measurements and the result patterns that would support each interpretation.

A low-temperature semitransparent perovskite cell is proposed for flexible bifacial modules and four-terminal tandems, but the available durability evidence is only a short maximum-power-point screen in moderate-humidity air. Build a qualification plan that separates thermal-budget compatibility from sputter damage, moisture/oxygen ingress, transparent-electrode sheet-resistance drift and optical-coupling losses. State what evidence would be required before claiming flexible or tandem readiness.

Depth-resolved diffraction and photoluminescence in a mixed-cation perovskite both shift from the free surface toward the buried interface. Explain why this correlation alone cannot establish that residual strain causes the vertical bandgap gradient. Propose an orthogonal, falsifiable experiment set that separates elastic strain, composition gradients, crystallinity/defects and photon reabsorption, and state the decisive outcome for a strain-causal model.

A strain-relief annealing method developed for spin-coated glass devices is to be transferred to slot-die-coated large-area or flexible perovskite modules. Identify the physical process variables that control the vertical strain profile, define an acceptance map for the scaled process, and explain why minimizing the area-averaged strain is insufficient. Include the expected failure modes from inverting or mechanically reorienting the film too early, excessive thermal treatment and substrate thermal-expansion mismatch.

An absorbing organic front layer on a perovskite film shows donor photoluminescence quenching, a shorter donor lifetime and sensitized perovskite emission. Construct a diagnostic matrix that distinguishes Förster energy transfer from radiative photon reabsorption, Dexter transfer and interfacial charge transfer. Specify at least one perturbation and the expected distance, spectral or kinetic signature for each mechanism.

A molecular bridge blended into P3HT produces stronger steady-state PL quenching and a shorter TRPL decay in perovskite/P3HT stacks, while the device open-circuit voltage and fill factor improve. Explain why the optical lifetime change is mechanistically ambiguous. Design a cross-validated measurement set that would demonstrate faster selective hole extraction together with defect passivation, rather than creation of a new non-radiative quenching interface.

A chemical modification of a SnO2 electron-selective layer simultaneously increases electron mobility, shifts its work function, changes precursor wetting, and produces a larger-grained, lower-trap perovskite film. The resulting planar cells show much less J-V hysteresis. Design a falsifiable experiment that determines whether hysteresis suppression is dominated by (i) electron-hole extraction-flux matching, (ii) reduced trap-assisted ionic polarization, or (iii) morphology-mediated recombination reduction. Specify the control matrix, perturbations, measurements, and the signature that would support each mechanism.

A modified SnO2 contact yields larger perovskite grains and better dark-storage and light-soaking stability, and the improvement is attributed mainly to reduced moisture penetration through grain boundaries. Before adopting the contact in a module, design a factorial aging study that tests whether grain size is sufficient to explain the stability gain or whether interfacial chelation, charge extraction, and contact chemistry are the dominant factors. State the stress matrix, decisive diagnostics, and module-design criteria that should follow.

A non-conductive cationic surfactant mixed with a phosphonic-acid hole-selective self-assembled monolayer improves substrate coverage and device voltage. Construct a control series that proves the benefit comes from suppressing monolayer aggregation and improving anchoring, rather than from a direct interfacial dipole, bromide passivation, residual surfactant acting as a separate interlayer, or a change in perovskite nucleation alone. State the measurements and the result pattern required for the anti-aggregation mechanism.

An oxygen-deficient TiO2 electron-selective layer exhibits persistent ultraviolet photoconductive gain, and complete perovskite cells show a photocurrent rise after light soaking. Design a time- and spectrum-resolved protocol that proves the reported stabilized photovoltaic improvement is true steady-state carrier extraction rather than trap-charging displacement current, capacitive memory, TiO2-only photocurrent, or J-V scan-history artefact. State the decisive observables and expected outcomes.

Deep traps in a TiO2 contact can increase photoconductivity and suppress photocatalytic oxidation, but an outdoor module experiences variable UV dose, oxygen and humidity, temperature cycling, and nightly dark periods. Propose a defect-engineering and qualification strategy that retains the beneficial mechanism without making performance dependent on uncontrolled light soaking. Explain the defect-density trade-off, the coupled-stress tests, and the acceptance criteria.

A nanocrystalline oxynitride evolves H2 or O2 efficiently in sacrificial-reagent tests and can participate in a redox-mediated Z-scheme. Define the material, reactor, and validation changes required to translate this result into durable solar overall-water-splitting operation. Explain why high sacrificial half-reaction rates are insufficient, and include charge selectivity, back-reaction control, gas stoichiometry, photocorrosion, cocatalyst durability, and scale-up constraints.

A quasi-two-dimensional perovskite film is modified with a crystallization additive. After treatment, its steady-state photoluminescence is dominated by the lowest-energy emission, the high-energy transient-absorption bleach decays more rapidly, the apparent photoluminescence lifetime increases, and the device open-circuit voltage improves. A researcher concludes that the film now has a homogeneous quantum-well energy landscape. Explain why this conclusion is not uniquely supported: the same observations could arise from faster carrier funneling into a small population of low-bandgap domains while substantial phase heterogeneity remains. Design an orthogonal diagnostic workflow that distinguishes genuine narrowing of the n-value/energy distribution from accelerated funneling through a still-disordered landscape. Your workflow must address phase census and depth distribution, transfer kinetics, minority-carrier transport, and nonradiative voltage loss, and it must state the combined outcome pattern required to accept the homogeneous-landscape interpretation.

A spacer/additive formulation produces a narrow quantum-well distribution in spin-coated quasi-two-dimensional perovskite cells. The same ink is transferred to slot-die coating over a 10 cm scale. Dynamic light scattering still shows no large precursor colloids, yet the dried film develops edge-to-centre photoluminescence shifts, spatially varying open-circuit voltage, and a stronger vertical phase gradient. Develop a scale-up strategy that preserves a homogeneous energy landscape without sacrificing the moisture and thermal advantages of low-n phases. Explain why a colloid-free ink is necessary but insufficient, identify the process variables that must be controlled, specify in-line and end-point acceptance measurements, and define accelerated tests that would reveal phase redistribution or spacer segregation after fabrication.

A chloride-containing crystalline intermediate is used to slow formation of an iodide perovskite during small-area spin coating. You must transfer the chemistry to a wide blade-coated film in which the edges, centre, and upstream/downstream regions experience different solvent evaporation and volatile-salt removal. Propose a staged drying and annealing strategy that uses the self-regulating precursor mechanism rather than simply eliminating chloride as fast as possible. Specify how gas flow, volatile-salt partial pressure, temperature, wet thickness, and residence time should be managed; identify in-line endpoint measurements and large-area mapping needed for process control; and explain the defects expected from both excessively rapid and excessively slow MACl removal. State what evidence would justify claiming that the transferred process improves film and device quality rather than only changing the conversion time.

A vertically oriented Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite solar cell loses photocurrent and fill factor as the absorber is made thicker. The loss becomes stronger at low internal field and low temperature, while average crystal orientation changes little. Two explanations remain plausible: carriers cross many distributed barriers inside the quantum-well stack, or a single extraction barrier at one selective contact dominates the device. Design a diagnostic matrix that localizes the dominant barrier. Your answer must combine absorber-thickness scaling, selective-contact/work-function perturbations, temperature and illumination dependence, transient or spatially resolved transport measurements, and device modelling. State the mutually exclusive result patterns expected for a distributed bulk-barrier mechanism and a contact-limited mechanism.

A physically large hybrid lead-halide perovskite quantum dot shows a low measured g²(0) and a biexciton lifetime shorter than that of an inorganic-cation control. These observations are compatible with phonon-driven wavefunction localization that selectively accelerates biexciton Auger-Meitner quenching, but static surface traps, intermittent charging/trions, or simple photobleaching could also suppress multiphoton emission. Explain the mechanistic distinctions and design a single-particle perturbation study that separates benign dynamic localization from these parasitic quenching mechanisms. Include lattice-dynamics perturbations, size and surface controls, heralded exciton/biexciton observables, and the correlated outcome pattern required to accept the phonon-localization mechanism.

A thickness series of lead-iodide perovskite films shows the following correlation: thicker films are more strain-relaxed, have higher electron mobility, but have lower apparent electron concentration, lower conductivity, higher series resistance, and poorer fill factor. Because thickness also changes crystallization history, buried interfaces, and measurement geometry, this correlation does not prove that strain controls carrier concentration. Design an intervention-based study that establishes or falsifies the causal chain strain → electron concentration → conductivity → fill factor. Include a reversible same-sample strain perturbation, independent methods for separating mobility from carrier density in an ionically mobile semiconductor, local co-mapping of strain and electrical properties, matched structural/compositional controls, and a device-level rescue criterion.

A sequential deposition method can retain beneficial compressive strain in a micrometre-thick perovskite by creating intermediate quasi-substrate interfaces, thereby improving carrier concentration, conductivity, and fill factor. You must scale this idea to a large-area thick absorber or module. Design a strain-management process and qualification plan that targets an optimum strain distribution rather than maximum compression. Address layer sequence and interface density, substrate/annealing/cooling mechanics, large-area in-line mapping, electrical acceptance metrics, and combined light-humidity-thermal-mechanical testing. Explain how you would detect the point at which beneficial electronic strain becomes harmful residual stress that promotes cracking, delamination, ion migration, or long-term voltage loss.

A bifunctional spacer gives an attractive inorganic bond angle and bandgap in an n=1 single crystal, but an n=4 blade-coated solar-cell film shows lower fill factor than expected despite retaining the local structural trend. Develop a go/no-go transfer program that determines whether the spacer chemistry is intrinsically useful but defeated by phase distribution, orientation, or interfacial transport. Your program must also identify when stronger terminal-group association becomes counterproductive for processing or long-term stability.

Two green perovskite LEDs have the same emission peak and similar hole mobility. Device H contains a small grain-boundary low-dimensional phase and shows longer PL lifetime, lower trap density, negligible initial current/luminance overshoot, weak scan-rate hysteresis, and much slower voltage drift under constant current. Device P is a conventional 3D polycrystalline emitter. Determine whether the overshoot suppression in H can be explained by trap passivation alone or requires reduced ion migration. Design a minimal orthogonal experiment set and state the outcome pattern that separates recombination, ionic redistribution, and ordinary electronic RC transients.

A mixed-halide perovskite host-guest film contains approximately 8 nm emissive domains in a crystallographically related wide-gap matrix. Its PL is stable for hours at moderate illumination but begins to red-shift at high excitation intensity and at lower temperature for Br-rich compositions. A pure film with approximately 35 nm domains segregates rapidly. Design a mechanistic test that distinguishes a finite-size/interface-energy nucleation barrier from lower defect density, reduced halide diffusivity, or simple optical dilution by the matrix. State the dependence on domain size, composition, temperature, and excitation that would support each explanation.

You must translate a photostable mixed-halide nanocrystal-in-matrix film into either an electrically driven LED or a tandem-solar-cell absorber. The guest domains must remain below the segregation-critical size, yet the device needs continuous carrier transport through the film. Propose a host-guest architecture and validation sequence that balances confinement, band alignment, percolation, injection/extraction, and manufacturability. Define explicit no-go outcomes that would reveal that optical photostability was purchased at the cost of unusable electrical transport.

A narrow-bandgap tin perovskite displays nanosecond-scale hot-emission signatures under strong optical excitation, but it is disordered and prone to Sn-vacancy self-p-doping and oxidation. Design a go/no-go program for converting this material into a hot-carrier photovoltaic absorber. Your answer must couple defect/doping control to an energy-selective contact architecture and specify measurements that prove useful hot-carrier extraction under near-solar steady-state conditions rather than only hot PL after a pulse.

A 3D tin-halide perovskite FET yields a very high saturation mobility from a fast forward gate sweep, but it also has high off-state current, a threshold voltage that shifts with sweep rate and dwell time, drain-current decay during constant gate bias, and a substantially lower mobility in a four-terminal measurement. Diagnose the contributions of true channel transport, tin-vacancy self-p-doping, mobile ions, gate leakage/capacitance error, and contact resistance. Specify a measurement matrix and the pattern that would justify reporting an intrinsic field-effect mobility.

A low-temperature back-end-of-line process needs a p-channel perovskite FET with high mobility, on/off ratio above 10^7, small bias-stress threshold shift, and operation in air. Compare two design routes: a fully 2D tin-perovskite channel and a 3D tin-perovskite channel protected by an ultrathin 2D or molecular cap. Develop a staged materials/device program that balances vacancy self-doping, oxidation, ion migration, contact resistance, dielectric compatibility, patterning, and channel scaling. Define the evidence that would select one route for integration.

A solvent treatment makes a MAPbI3 field-effect transistor appear better at first glance: the room-temperature transfer curve has a steeper turn-on and a higher extracted mobility. However, the result depends strongly on scan rate, the threshold voltage drifts during bias, temperature-dependent Kelvin-probe mapping reveals a new fast low-activation-energy surface-potential redistribution, and prolonged exposure to the same solvent produces PbI2 and pinholes. Diagnose why the mobility increase does not establish improved intrinsic electronic transport. Give an ordered evidence chain that separates removal of pre-existing ionic screening, creation of new mobile vacancies, contact artefacts, and genuine channel passivation.

A manufacturer wants to transfer a sequential clean-heal-clean surface treatment from small MAPbI3 test transistors to a large-area perovskite FET backplane before dielectric deposition. The process must remove ionic surface complexes and fill halide/organic vacancies, but both under-cleaning and over-cleaning cause failure. Design a process-control and qualification plan that defines the controllable window, distinguishes chemical healing from residual-salt contamination, and sets release criteria for long-term electrical stability.

An inverted perovskite solar cell becomes nearly hysteresis-free after introducing a PCBM electron-contact layer. Two explanations are proposed: PCBM passivates interfacial electronic traps, or mobile iodide enters PCBM and dynamically dopes the contact during operation. Design a mechanism-discriminating experiment. State the controls, time/temperature/bias signatures and orthogonal measurements that would allow one explanation, both explanations, or neither to be supported.

A low-bandgap perovskite absorber intended for a commercial module has a carrier diffusion length of only about 100 nm, while the optical thickness needed for strong absorption is several hundred nanometres. A mesoscopic scaffold can shorten the collection distance, but it increases interfacial area and process complexity. Decide how planar and mesoscopic architectures should be down-selected, and specify what evidence would justify switching to a planar design after the absorber is improved.

A tandem-cell team wants to remove the organic hole-transport layer from a new Sn-Pb rear subcell and rely on a direct conductive-oxide/perovskite junction for hole selectivity. The new absorber has a different Sn:Pb ratio and the transparent oxide has a different work function from ITO. Construct a go/no-go validation plan. Why can the contact concept not be transferred by stack analogy alone, and which stability tests must be coupled to the band-alignment study?

A noncovalent molecular bilayer is engineered to match a covalently interconnected bilayer in initial work function, wetting, perovskite photoluminescence yield and fresh-device efficiency. After thermal cycling, however, the noncovalent contact loses molecular coverage, transfers phosphorus-containing fragments to the perovskite fracture surface and develops interfacial voids, whereas the covalent network remains comparatively uniform and adherent. Explain why the initial equivalence does not falsify the role of covalent networking. Construct a causal interpretation that separates electronic alignment, molecular retention and mechanical adhesion.

A close-space annealing process shows a non-monotonic dependence on preheating. With very short preheating, films contain large crystallites but also pinholes, high dark leakage and poor device output. At an intermediate preheat, grains merge, carrier lifetime increases and the Urbach tail narrows. With excessive preheating, the film again resembles conventionally annealed small-grain material. Diagnose all three regimes using the balance between residual coordinating solvent, grain-boundary dissolution and solvent escape. What measurements and counter-controls would make the diagnosis causal rather than morphological speculation?

Translate film-side-down close-space annealing to a continuous roll-to-roll process for a monolithic all-perovskite tandem. Propose a manufacturable equivalent of the confined cover, explain how the low-bandgap and wide-bandgap subcells should be given separate solvent-release windows, and define the in-line controls and module-level go/no-go criteria needed before calling the method universal or scalable.

Two otherwise identical inverted perovskite cells use fullerene electron-transport layers with the same mean frontier-orbital energy and similar surface morphology. The more ordered layer has a Gaussian energetic-disorder width of about 90 meV rather than 135 meV, raises Voc by roughly 90 mV, and leaves Jsc, FF, and the transient-photovoltage recombination lifetime unchanged at matched carrier density. Charge-extraction measurements show that the disordered device must store more photogenerated charge to reach the same Voc. Explain the voltage gain in quasi-Fermi-level terms. Predict the corresponding chemical-capacitance and carrier-density-versus-Voc signatures, and state what observations would falsify energetic disorder as the dominant explanation?

A team must select an electron contact for a scalable wide-bandgap perovskite top cell. Candidate A has a favorable mean LUMO but broad energetic disorder; candidate B has a slightly less favorable mean LUMO but a narrow DOS; candidate C has a narrow DOS but low mobility. Design a screening and accelerated-aging workflow that ranks the contacts by retained voltage rather than by fresh-device Voc alone. How should the workflow separate mean energy alignment, energetic disorder, interfacial recombination, transport resistance, and aging-induced ionic or structural changes?

A mixed Sn-Pb perovskite has a strongly Sn-rich surface. A diamine treatment lowers the surface Sn:Pb ratio, creates a spatially uniform resistive chelate layer, suppresses Sn4+ formation, and raises QFLS. These correlations do not establish whether the benefit comes mainly from selective stoichiometric correction, chemical defect passivation, or a diffusion/oxidation barrier. What is the smallest control matrix that can determine which functions are necessary and which are sufficient, while also detecting over-etching or an extraction penalty?

An encapsulated, chelate-treated all-perovskite tandem shows long internal MPP stability, but an independently certified sample displays declining stabilized output during a short post-shipment test. What reliability protocol, including paired controls, subcell-resolved diagnostics, and decision criteria, can distinguish intrinsic failure of the Sn-Pb chelate interface from encapsulation leakage, transport/recombination-junction damage, or top-cell/bottom-cell current mismatch introduced during shipment and measurement?

In a p-i-n perovskite cell, replacing a conventional cathode buffer with dense SnO2 and then adding an ITO layer shifts catastrophic reverse-breakdown to much larger negative voltage. Adding an ultrathin LiF layer does not shift that breakdown threshold further, yet it strongly lowers sub-breakdown dark current and greatly extends lifetime during prolonged moderate reverse bias. Why are these observations not contradictory, and what time-resolved electrical and chemical signatures would distinguish an injection-limited degradation rate from an ion/metal-filament breakdown threshold?

A vertically graded perovskite-fullerene junction produces stronger steady-state photoluminescence quenching and a faster absorber-side transient photoluminescence decay than a sharp planar junction. In complete devices, however, transient photovoltage shows a longer recombination lifetime, while open-circuit voltage and fill factor both improve. Explain why these observations are not inherently contradictory. What additional measurements and controls are required to distinguish genuinely faster electron extraction from fullerene-induced non-radiative quenching or morphology damage?

A composition that is nearly free of planar defects in a single-iodide MA/FA perovskite is proposed as the wide-bandgap top absorber of a mixed-halide tandem. Explain why the original structural optimum cannot be assumed to transfer. Construct a screening workflow that determines whether the new composition remains defect-tolerant during fabrication and under illumination, and specify decision criteria that would reject a nominally high-efficiency formulation before module scale-up.

A new additive pair is credited with excellent operational stability, but the stressed devices also replace the standard electron-contact buffer with a more stable metal-oxide layer, whereas the headline efficiency devices use the original buffer. Design the smallest rigorous experiment that quantifies the additive contribution, the contact-stack contribution, and any interaction between them. Explain how encapsulation, initial efficiency, stress protocol, and degradation signatures must be handled before assigning a 2,000-hour retention claim to the additive chemistry.

You must build a model from a heterogeneous literature database to predict operational T80 for a new laboratory and device architecture. Most records lack complete stress conditions, many devices are still above 80% performance when reporting ends, and several rows come from the same paper. Define the prediction target, curation rules, data split, evaluation metrics, and deployment test needed for credible cross-laboratory transfer. Explain why a high random-row cross-validation score could be scientifically misleading.

An ambient-aged perovskite precursor produces a film whose final XRD pattern appears nearly normal. A strong post-deposition surface passivation restores the surface-sensitive lifetime, yet absolute PLQY, quasi-Fermi-level splitting and device fill factor remain substantially below those of a nitrogen-processed control. Design a split-sample forensic experiment that distinguishes three possible origins: precursor iodide oxidation and organic-cation deprotonation that create inherited bulk defects, an altered intermediate-phase crystallization pathway, and recombination introduced only at the completed device interfaces. Specify when the stabilizer or passivant should be added, the measurements required at the solution, wet-film, final-film and device stages, and the diagnostic result pattern for each origin.

Two perovskite films have matched composition, crystallographic orientation, surface trap density and average grain size, but one has concave grain bottoms that form nanoscale gaps against a flat electron-transport layer, whereas the other has nearly conformal grain bottoms. Design a causal experiment that partitions the performance difference into electrical-contact, thermal-transfer and mechanical-adhesion contributions. Include a geometry-only perturbation or rescue, local measurements, stress tests and the distinct signatures expected for each contribution.

A surfactant-based strategy that suppresses buried grain-bottom concavities is transferred from spin coating to slot-die coating of minimodules. The coated film has acceptable top-surface roughness, but module yield varies with web speed and the failures cluster near laser scribes after thermal cycling. Develop a process-transfer and qualification protocol that measures the buried geometry directly, identifies the coating variables controlling it, and separates absorber nanogap failure from scribe, electrode and encapsulation failure.

A temperature-dependent degradation study produces a kink in the Arrhenius plot near 105-110 °C. The same devices show a small PL redshift below the kink and a large PL blueshift above it, but series resistance also rises at high temperature. Design an experiment that determines whether the kink represents a true switch from cation segregation to volatile-cation loss, rather than a contact-resistance artifact or a change in the rate-limiting step of the same mechanism. Include capping-layer, operating-point, mass-balance and structural controls, and state the result pattern required for a pathway switch.

You must qualify a new p-dopant for spiro-OMeTAD that matches or exceeds LiTFSI conductivity but may contain a different mobile counterion or leave volatile reaction products. Design a screening funnel that separates initial doping efficiency from long-term chemical cleanliness and cycling stability. Include residue and ion-mobility measurements, transport controls, cycling protocols and failure criteria.

A mixed set of short-, medium- and long-chain alkylammonium chlorides in an ethanol/Lewis-base precursor yields better coverage, larger grains and lower recombination than any single additive. Design a mechanistic experiment that determines whether the mixture works through time-separated molecular roles—rapid alpha-phase nucleation, intermediate-phase-controlled growth and wetting/pinhole suppression—or merely through its total chloride concentration and ionic strength. Specify composition-matched controls, in situ measurements and the result pattern required to demonstrate non-additive synergy.

A bulky-ammonium treatment creates both a quasi-2D cap and a wider-bandgap near-surface region in a mixed-halide perovskite. The treated film shows a much longer photoluminescence lifetime and a much smaller fitted effective bimolecular recombination coefficient. Design a falsifiable diagnostic strategy to determine whether the lifetime gain is dominated by field-induced spatial separation of electrons and holes rather than by a true reduction in microscopic defect-capture probability. State the expected signatures for front-versus-back excitation, increasing carrier density or forward bias, and a chemistry-matched sample in which the compositional gradient is flattened.

A molecular additive gives a perovskite film a longer lifetime when deposited without PCBM, but the complete perovskite/PCBM-plus-additive half-stack shows much faster PL and transient-absorption decay than a perovskite/PCBM control. Explain why these observations are not contradictory. Then design a stack-decomposition experiment that separately establishes (a) perovskite defect passivation, (b) electron extraction through the PCBM layer, and (c) suppression of PCBM packing disorder and photodimerization. State what combination of results would be required for a causal claim.

An additive organizes PCBM into a more vertical, spatially uniform electron-selective layer and accumulates near the perovskite/PCBM interface. Propose a transfer protocol for slot- or blade-coating this chemistry in a monolithic module. Identify the process variables most likely to destroy interfacial enrichment or molecular orientation, the spatial acceptance measurements required before device completion, and the matched controls and ageing analysis needed to show that a module-level gain comes from the intended molecular mechanism rather than from coating or laser-scribing artifacts.

A wet treatment of commercial ITO simultaneously increases surface hydroxyl density, removes a weak amorphous surface layer, and creates oxygen-vacancy/uncoordinated-indium sites. A phosphonic-acid SAM subsequently becomes denser and more resistant to polar-solvent rinsing. Design a factorial experiment that determines whether robust anchoring is controlled mainly by hydroxyl density, removal of the weak surface layer, or coordination to vacancy-associated indium sites. Specify the substrate groups, the measurements needed before and after SAM deposition, and the result pattern that would falsify each proposed mechanism.

A polymer electron-transporting material forms face-on crystallites and has much higher out-of-plane than in-plane conductivity. Devices show a higher fill factor than controls. Design a causality test that determines whether the fill-factor gain is produced by vertical molecular packing rather than merely by more favorable energy alignment or stronger interfacial passivation. Specify matched materials or processing perturbations, the transport and interfacial measurements, and the result pattern required to assign a dominant role to orientation.

A hydrophobic, thermally robust non-fullerene polymer ETM gives a longer operational lifetime than PCBM, but a separate heat test also changes the buffer layer from an organic interlayer to ALD-SnOx. Design a protocol-normalized reliability matrix that determines whether the polymer itself provides an intrinsic stability advantage rather than benefiting from buffer-layer choice or encapsulation. Include the factorial controls, stress conditions, degradation observables and the criterion for distinguishing an ETM main effect from a stack-specific interaction.

Two micrometre-scale regions in a 600-nm polycrystalline halide-perovskite film have nearly identical steady-state photoluminescence intensity and bulk PL lifetime, yet a depth-sensitive transient-PL assay gives vertical redistribution times that differ by more than an order of magnitude. Construct the diagnostic argument required before assigning this contrast to genuine vertical-transport heterogeneity. Address why lifetime and intensity are insufficient, which optical and excitation-density controls are necessary, which model or boundary assumptions must be tested, and the most plausible microstructural origin of the contrast.

An AC-biased lead-halide perovskite contracts along the electric-field direction with strain proportional to E squared, oscillates predominantly at twice the drive frequency, follows the field below roughly 10 Hz but becomes negligible in the kilohertz regime, and shows an ionic activation energy that decreases at high field and rapidly recovers when the field is lowered. What mechanism is most consistent with this combined evidence? Give a diagnostic strategy that separates it from both conventional nearly instantaneous electrostriction and mere long-range ionic accumulation at the electrodes.

A thiol-rich n-type metal-organic-framework interlayer deposited on a perovskite produces very strong steady-state and time-resolved PL quenching, while complete devices show higher fill factor and open-circuit voltage. Explain why PL quenching alone cannot establish beneficial electron extraction, and specify the minimum evidence set needed to distinguish selective extraction from creation of a new nonradiative interface sink.

Design a cathode-side interlayer for a large-area inverted perovskite module that must simultaneously extract electrons, block holes and moisture, maintain a low-resistance metal contact, and immobilize Pb after catastrophic water ingress. Explain the principal design trade-offs and the validation protocol required before claiming both operational stability and lead containment.

Replacing a conventional polycrystalline TiO2 nanoparticle electron-transport layer with single-crystalline, facet-exposed nanoparticles simultaneously changes electron mobility, oxygen-vacancy density, surface chemistry, particle packing and the morphology of the perovskite deposited above it. Design a causal deconvolution study that determines whether a fill-factor gain is dominated by bulk ETL transport or by reduced interfacial nonradiative recombination.

A high-fill-factor TiO2 formulation performs well in 0.1 cm2 perovskite cells. Define a go/no-go framework for transferring it to a laser-scribed approximately 25 cm2 mini-module without mistaking a small-cell material benefit for a module-scale processing artifact.

A two-dimensional perovskite solar cell shows a light-soaking increase in open-circuit voltage and fill factor with little change in short-circuit current. Operando diffraction simultaneously shows out-of-plane lattice contraction, and electron-only measurements show increased mobility. Construct an experiment that distinguishes a causal contraction-induced lowering of interwell transport barriers from photodoping or trap filling that merely correlates with the lattice change.

You must screen A-site substitutions for a lead-halide perovskite that should retain a useful bandgap and an average cubic phase while exhibiting high carrier mobility and little ferroelastic instability. Propose a local-structure-based screening workflow and define the descriptors and pass/fail criteria you would use. Explain why average space group, mean tilt angle and a single room-temperature PL spectrum are insufficient for this design decision.

A methylammonium tin-halide solar cell has the correct absorption edge and an external-quantum-efficiency spectrum consistent with its short-circuit current, but it shows low open-circuit voltage, low fill factor, high dark current and a rapid loss of current and fill factor even during nominally inert storage. Construct a diagnostic hierarchy that separates (i) Sn(II) oxidation and self-doping, (ii) incomplete film coverage or shunting, and (iii) unfavorable contact energetics. For each mechanism, state at least one decisive measurement and the device signature expected if it dominates.

Design a manufacturing and qualification strategy for a lead-free tin-halide perovskite photovoltaic in which encapsulation alone is not allowed to mask intrinsic instability. Prioritize interventions at the precursor, deposition, film-morphology and selective-contact levels, and define a measurement matrix that would demonstrate that an apparent stability improvement results from suppressed oxidation and leakage rather than from reduced initial performance.

A perovskite-polymer bulk-heterostructure LED has high low-fluence PL quantum yield and efficient emission at low current, but its EQE rolls off sharply as current density rises and the electroluminescence decay becomes faster. Develop a diagnostic strategy that distinguishes Auger recombination, charge-injection imbalance or interfacial quenching, and Joule-heating/ion-migration effects. State the current-, fluence-, time- and temperature-dependent signatures expected for each mechanism.

A thick zero-bias perovskite single-crystal X-ray detector has high calculated X-ray absorption but unexpectedly low shunt resistance, drifting dark current and poor signal-to-noise ratio. Its performance improves substantially after prolonged dry inert conditioning, while the crystal thickness and optical absorption remain unchanged. Diagnose whether the dominant defect is residual solvate at the buried selective-contact interface, bulk trapping, or an insufficient built-in field. Specify the control experiments and the distinct electrical, spectroscopic and spatial signatures expected for each hypothesis.

A zero-bias single-crystal perovskite X-ray imager optimized for soft X-rays must be redesigned for 60-100 keV photons and a pixel pitch below 20 micrometres. Explain why simply increasing crystal thickness and shrinking the pixel pitch may fail. Propose an architecture and validation strategy that balances absorption efficiency, carrier transport, charge-cloud spreading, built-in-field collection, electronic noise and bias-induced instability.

An MA-free mixed-cation lead-halide single crystal is alloyed with a small fraction of an oversized A-site cation. Its photoluminescence lifetime increases and its trap-density signature decreases, yet its rocking curve broadens, microstrain rises, and the dark current becomes less stable. Adding a trace, isovalent, radius-matched B-site dopant reverses the structural and electrical penalties without a systematic bandgap shift or new diffraction phase. Construct the defect-chemical mechanism that reconciles all observations. Then state the minimum orthogonal measurements and counterfactual controls needed to distinguish halide-vacancy suppression plus strain-relieving Pb-vacancy formation from ordinary shallow doping or second-phase formation.

A dual-site, MA-free perovskite composition gives excellent low-field X-ray response in millimetre-scale single crystals, but it must be transferred to centimetre-scale, thick pixel arrays. Larger boules develop radial composition gradients, local mosaicity, and pixel-to-pixel dark-current drift; electrode processing may also passivate the surface independently of the bulk composition. Design a composition-growth-device optimization programme that preserves the defect/strain synergy at scale. Specify the controlled variables, spatially resolved acceptance metrics, controls that separate bulk strain engineering from contact effects, and an accelerated stress matrix with quantitative go/no-go logic.

A perovskite solar cell develops a reversible loss of open-circuit voltage and a redistributed surface-potential profile during minutes of illuminated forward bias; most of the signal recovers after dark rest. After much longer stress, depth profiling shows halide and electrode-metal accumulation at opposite interfaces and the voltage no longer fully recovers. Replacing one transport layer nearly eliminates scan-rate hysteresis but does not stop maximum-power-point degradation.
