Build a mechanistic diagnosis that separates reversible ionic polarization from irreversible interfacial chemistry, and explain why reduced hysteresis does not prove that bulk ion migration has been suppressed. Specify decisive perturbations and observables.

Design an ion-migration mitigation strategy for a mixed-halide perovskite module that must retain high electronic mobility and charge extraction. The absorber contains vacancy-mediated bulk transport, fast grain-boundary paths, and interfaces that act as ionic sinks; field hot spots arise near interconnects. Propose a coupled materials, interface, architecture, and operating strategy. For each intervention, identify the trade-off it could introduce, and define an accelerated validation matrix that distinguishes reduced mobile-ion density, increased migration barrier, blocked interfacial reaction, and merely hidden electrical symptoms.

Two surface passivators produce the same initial increase in perovskite-film PLQY and quasi-Fermi-level splitting. Passivator A is a small monodentate Lewis base with very strong binding to under-coordinated Pb; passivator B is a bulkier zwitterionic, multidentate molecule with moderate individual bond strength. Under heat and operating bias, A-treated cells develop hysteresis, voltage loss, and passivator redistribution, whereas B-treated cells retain performance but show a small fill-factor penalty. Explain why the initial optical metrics are insufficient to rank the molecules, diagnose the distinct failure mechanisms, and define measurements that separate chemical passivation, interfacial dipoles, ion blocking, molecular mobility, and transport resistance.

Develop a down-selection workflow for a passivator intended for a scalable inverted perovskite module. The molecule must passivate both surface and grain-boundary defects, survive coating and subsequent layer deposition, suppress ion-mediated degradation, and avoid an insulating interlayer or harmful dipole. Define the molecular descriptor set, sequential screening experiments, scale-up process controls, and device stress gates. Explain how the workflow would reject a molecule that gives record small-area efficiency but fails the broader design objective.

A monolithic two-terminal perovskite tandem underperforms the sum of its independently measured top and bottom cells, whereas a mechanically stacked four-terminal version using the same absorbers performs close to that sum. In the two-terminal device, the limiting current changes with spectrum and temperature, fill factor drops under high illumination, and the wide-bandgap top cell shows light-induced spectral instability. Construct a diagnostic sequence that separates current mismatch and parasitic optical loss from recombination-interconnect resistance and subcell instability. State the measurements and counterfactual signatures required before assigning the dominant loss.

A two-terminal perovskite tandem has record standard-test efficiency but lower annual energy yield than expected because outdoor spectra and temperature continually change the current-limiting subcell; the wide-bandgap junction also segregates under intense light, and partial shading occasionally drives reverse bias. Propose an energy-yield-oriented redesign rather than another standard-test optimization. Compare architectural, bandgap, optical, interconnect, control-electronics and stability options, and define the outdoor or accelerated data needed to decide whether a monolithic two-terminal, four-terminal, or partially decoupled architecture is preferable.

Two nominally identical black-phase iodide-perovskite films have the same initial diffraction pattern and bandgap. Under simultaneous illumination and humid air, film A develops yellow-phase nuclei at grain boundaries after an induction period, whereas film B remains black after a strain-relieving treatment that does not measurably change composition. Explain why these observations do not by themselves prove that the treatment made the black phase thermodynamically stable. Then propose a diagnostic strategy that can distinguish a reduced thermodynamic driving force from a raised kinetic barrier to phase conversion.

A laboratory black-phase perovskite remains phase-pure in small cells after simultaneous A-site mixing, partial halide substitution and formation of a thin 2D-rich surface layer. When transferred to a large-area module, the bandgap becomes spatially non-uniform and local phase conversion appears near interconnects under bias and light. Design a minimal, mechanism-resolving development plan that identifies which stabilization lever should be retained, modified or removed before scale-up. Your plan must separate bulk phase thermodynamics, kinetic suppression and electrically driven interfacial degradation.

A new organic A-cation produces three simultaneous changes relative to a formamidinium-rich control: stronger octahedral tilting, a longer photoluminescence lifetime and faster degradation in humid air. The new cation is slightly larger, has a larger molecular dipole and is more hydrophilic. Construct a causal interpretation that does not attribute all three observations to a single descriptor, and specify a set of comparison materials or measurements that would disentangle steric, electrostatic/dynamic and moisture-uptake effects.

A bulky ammonium salt improves moisture resistance and open-circuit voltage when added to a three-dimensional perovskite ink, but it is unclear whether the cation is incorporated into the 3D A-site, forms a quasi-2D surface phase, or remains as an amorphous interfacial residue. Propose a design-and-validation workflow that determines the actual structural role of the cation and uses that result to choose a scalable composition profile without sacrificing vertical charge transport.

Two halide perovskites have the same nominal composition and average crystal symmetry at room temperature. Sample X has a broader instantaneous metal-halide-metal bond-angle distribution, a blue-shifted absorption edge and lower mobility than sample Y, but their conventional Bragg diffraction patterns are nearly indistinguishable. Give a mechanistic explanation in terms of octahedral units and design a characterization sequence that can determine whether the difference arises mainly from static local distortions, dynamic octahedral motion or reduced octahedral connectivity.

You must design a wide-bandgap mixed-halide absorber that resists illumination-induced halide segregation while retaining efficient three-dimensional carrier transport. Using octahedral units as the design basis, propose two complementary material interventions and an experiment that would reveal whether improved stability comes from a stiffer/more coherent octahedral network rather than from merely slowing carriers or blocking interfaces.

Two semiconductor films contain comparable total point-defect densities by a structural assay. Film A nevertheless has a much longer carrier lifetime and a smaller voltage loss than film B. Explain why this comparison is insufficient to label A 'defect-tolerant', and formulate a minimum mechanistic test set that separates defect formation, electronic harmfulness, carrier capture, dynamic screening and surface effects.

A newly synthesized pnictogen chalcohalide has promising absorption and mobility, but its defect physics is unknown. Build a staged go/no-go workflow for deciding whether it is defect-resistant, defect-tolerant, self-healing or merely passivatable. The workflow must connect theory to controlled damage experiments and must prevent a favourable result for one defect or one measurement condition from being generalized to the entire material.

A two-terminal perovskite-organic tandem has apparently matched top- and bottom-subcell currents when each EQE spectrum is integrated under a reference spectrum, yet the complete device shows an S-shaped J-V curve, a depressed fill factor and a photocurrent that changes when selective bias light is applied to either subcell. Construct a diagnostic workflow that distinguishes: (i) a genuine spectral or optical current mismatch, (ii) charge accumulation or a transport barrier at the recombination contact, and (iii) excess non-radiative recombination in one subcell. State the decisive measurement signatures for each mechanism.

During scale-up of a two-terminal perovskite-organic tandem, the organic rear subcell becomes current-limiting. Simply increasing its thickness restores simulated absorption but lowers fill factor and accelerates light-induced burn-in because exciton transport and blend morphology deteriorate. Propose a design-transfer strategy that recovers tandem energy yield without relying on absorber thickening alone. Rank the interventions and define the measurements that would justify a go/no-go decision.

A self-assembled-monolayer hole contact that performs reproducibly on smooth ITO small cells gives lower voltage and large device-to-device variance when transferred to a monolithic perovskite-silicon tandem with a strongly textured bottom cell. Formulate a transfer strategy that preserves selectivity on the enlarged, rough surface without creating an insulating multilayer. Include molecular, deposition, stack-integration and qualification criteria.

A molecular interface modifier increases open-circuit voltage and fill factor, shifts the contact work function, changes perovskite grain size and reduces interfacial recombination. Design an orthogonal experiment that determines whether the dominant cause of the device improvement is (i) a molecular dipole and energy-level shift, (ii) chemical defect passivation, or (iii) altered nucleation and film morphology. Specify the control molecules, processing controls and diagnostic signatures required for causal attribution.

A monolithic two-terminal perovskite-silicon tandem operated at maximum power under light and heat shows a fast, partially reversible voltage loss and a slower, irreversible fill-factor loss. After dark rest, the perovskite top-cell photoluminescence spectrum and part of the voltage recover; the silicon-subcell EQE is unchanged, but the tandem's interfacial resistance remains elevated. Build a subcell-resolved diagnosis that separates reversible halide segregation or ionic redistribution, recombination-junction chemical degradation, and new shunting. State the decisive tests and expected signatures.

A thermally robust, ion-blocking inorganic hole-contact layer substantially extends the lifetime of a single-junction perovskite device. Before transferring it into a monolithic perovskite-silicon tandem, define a go/no-go framework that determines whether the same layer improves tandem reliability or merely introduces a new optical, electrical or process-limited failure mode.

Under otherwise identical illumination and temperature, a perovskite solar cell degrades faster at open circuit than at maximum power point, is comparatively stable at short circuit, and shows substantial but incomplete recovery after a dark rest. Explain how carrier density, internal electric field, mobile-ion redistribution and interfacial chemistry can produce this stress-state ranking. Then design a diagnostic protocol that separates reversible electrostatic or ionic effects from irreversible chemical degradation.

A self-limiting 3D-to-quasi-2D surface conversion gives reproducible devices by spin coating, but slot-die coating on a moving web produces a cross-web gradient from an unconverted region to a thick low-n surface layer. Propose a scale-up strategy that preserves a thin, vertically transport-compatible converted layer without sacrificing the moisture barrier. Your answer must identify the process variables to control, an inline endpoint signal, and acceptance criteria that distinguish true dimensionality control from merely depositing an organic salt overlayer.

A perovskite diode has high photovoltaic efficiency and high absolute photoluminescence quantum yield near open circuit, yet its electroluminescence external quantum efficiency is poor under forward bias. Develop a diagnostic sequence that separates three possible limits: imbalanced carrier injection or contact barriers, poor photon outcoupling, and current-induced creation of non-radiative defects. State the expected signature of each mechanism and why high open-circuit PLQY alone cannot identify the cause.

A phase-pure single-n film can be produced by spin coating, but scalable meniscus coating creates a vertical and down-web n-value gradient because solvent evaporation, complexation, and crystallization occur on similar time scales. Propose a process-control strategy that preserves phase purity and useful out-of-plane transport over a large area. Include the variables to control, an inline detection scheme, and a decision rule for rejecting a film that looks phase-pure by one ensemble measurement.

An inverted 3D perovskite solar cell is modified with an ultrathin reduced-dimensional surface layer. The treatment raises the initial open-circuit voltage and improves dark damp-heat shelf stability. However, during maximum-power-point operation at 85 °C, the fill factor progressively falls, hysteresis increases, and the absorber photoluminescence lifetime remains high. Construct a diagnostic argument that distinguishes (i) preserved trap passivation combined with an electronically blocking low-dimensional cap from (ii) failure of the cap to suppress field-driven ionic redistribution. Specify at least three paired measurements, the stress or bias condition under which each should be made, and the opposite signatures expected for the two hypotheses.

A perovskite mini-module degrades first at laser-scribed edges and then along grain boundaries during combined damp heat and reverse-bias hot-spot stress. A continuous 2D surface cap slows moisture ingress but lowers photocurrent and does not stop edge-to-interior propagation. Propose a dimensionality-engineering redesign that assigns different functions to the exposed surface, grain boundaries, and scribe-edge regions. Explain the intended phase placement or dimensional gradient, how vertical electronic transport would be preserved, and a module-scale validation matrix with explicit go/no-go criteria.

An MA-free FA/Cs mixed-iodide/bromide perovskite with a bandgap near 1.75 eV develops a reversible red photoluminescence shoulder under continuous illumination. Conventional X-ray diffraction shows no new peak. The red feature is strongest at open circuit, much weaker at short circuit, and disappears after a dark rest. Design a decisive measurement sequence to determine whether this is nanoscale light-induced halide segregation rather than trap filling, carrier heating, or simple lattice heating. State the expected time, spatial, bias, and temperature signatures for each interpretation.

An MA-free wide-bandgap top cell retains its quasi-Fermi-level splitting and an unchanged PL spectrum during standalone light-and-heat testing. After integration into a monolithic two-terminal tandem, however, fill factor and stabilized power decline during 85 °C maximum-power-point operation, while the top-cell bandgap remains constant. Build a failure-isolation matrix that can distinguish degradation of the wide-bandgap absorber, its charge-selective contacts, the recombination junction or current matching, and processing damage to the bottom cell. Specify the minimum witness structures, subcell-resolved measurements, and go/no-go criteria required before module scale-up.

A small zwitterionic molecule placed at a buried hole-contact/Pb–Sn perovskite interface improves quasi-Fermi-level splitting, fill factor, and hole extraction. Design the minimum crossed molecular-control experiment needed to determine how much of the benefit comes from chemical trap passivation and how much comes from an oriented interfacial dipole. Specify the control functionalities, the measurements that separately report chemical passivation and electrostatic alignment, and the result pattern that would demonstrate genuine synergy rather than a single dominant mechanism.

A dipolar passivator optimized for a PEDOT:PSS/Pb–Sn buried interface is to be transferred to a narrow-bandgap subcell that instead uses NiOx or a carbazole self-assembled monolayer as the hole contact. Because the new surface can change molecular anchoring, protonation, and dipole orientation, propose a staged transfer-and-qualification protocol for 85 °C maximum-power operation. State the interface-specific molecular design rules, the operando or post-stress diagnostics, and the failure criteria that would make the transfer a no-go even if the initial efficiency increases.

An approximately 5 nm amorphous TCO/phosphonic-acid SAM recombination junction is to be scaled from small textured silicon cells to full pseudo-square wafers. Spin coating produces different SAM coverage on pyramid tips, facets, valleys, and wafer edges. Define a manufacturing qualification plan and process window that preserve TCO continuity, SAM coverage, useful lateral shunt isolation, and low vertical contact resistance. Include spatial metrology, electrical and optical tests, accelerated stress, and quantitative-style go/no-go criteria.

A mixed-connectivity perovskitoid cap exhibits much less organic-spacer migration under heat and humidity than a conventional corner-sharing 2D perovskite cap. Design a matched causal experiment that can show whether the suppression is caused by the corner/edge/face-sharing inorganic topology rather than simply by greater hydrophobicity, stronger adsorption of the organic spacer, or a thicker surface layer. Specify the material controls, stress protocol, migration and structural measurements, and the outcome pattern required to assign causality to connectivity.

A wide-bandgap p-i-n perovskite receives an approximately nanometre-thick insulating salt layer A, followed by a diammonium iodide treatment B, before C60 deposition. On the perovskite before C60, A+B produces only a modest lifetime increase. After C60 is added, however, A+B gives a much larger increase in absolute PLQY and lifetime, higher device Voc and pseudo-fill factor, and no measurable loss of short-circuit current. Reversing the order to B then A, or making A several nanometres thick, can keep the PL signal high but produces an S-shaped J-V curve and a severe fill-factor loss. Construct a mechanistic diagnosis that separates chemical defect passivation, energy-level/electrostatic modification, and nanoscale electron-transport connectivity. Specify the minimum control set and measurement sequence needed to distinguish a genuinely selective, locally contacted interface from a uniformly blocking interlayer, and predict the decisive signature of each mechanism.

A bilayer-passivated perovskite/C60 contact that performs well on 1 cm2 tandems is transferred to a 10 × 10 cm textured monolithic tandem process. Initial median efficiency remains high, but edge regions show a growing fill-factor deficit and the devices develop a slow Voc decay during maximum-power-point operation. Propose a staged qualification and failure-localization plan that determines whether the loss originates from (i) nonuniform insulating-layer percolation, (ii) loss of chemical passivation, (iii) bias-driven ionic redistribution or interfacial reaction, or (iv) texture-dependent coating and C60 damage. Define the matched controls, spatially registered measurements, stress conditions and go/no-go criteria required before the interface can be considered scalable.

A low-dose imidazolium tetrafluoroborate ionic-liquid additive causes no measurable perovskite XRD peak shift, but increases PL intensity and lifetime, lowers the work function, and strongly suppresses spatial PL redistribution during an in-plane bias test. Surface XPS detects the imidazolium cation near the top surface, whereas depth profiling finds the tetrafluoroborate anion enriched mainly near the buried hole-contact interface and the cation distributed through the film. Construct a mechanistic model that reconciles these observations. Then design a decisive experiment set that distinguishes four possibilities: reduced mobile-ion concentration, increased migration barrier or ion trapping, electrostatic field screening, and improved contact energetics. Explain why the biased-PL result alone cannot identify which mechanism dominates.

During accelerated ageing of an ionic-liquid-containing p-i-n perovskite module, the peak reverse-scan J-V efficiency remains nearly unchanged, but stabilized maximum-power output declines, hysteresis and overshoot grow, and some performance recovers after dark rest. Design a stability protocol and decision framework that distinguishes reversible ionic redistribution or burn-in, irreversible absorber decomposition, selective-contact/electrode corrosion, and measurement artefacts. Include a route-control that separates additive effects distributed through the absorber from effects confined to the buried contact, and define when lifetime extrapolation is scientifically defensible.

After C60 evaporation onto a square-centimetre wide-bandgap perovskite, an ultrathin organic-cation-derived 2D layer makes the PL map both brighter and more spatially uniform. That observation has two competing interpretations: the layer may have passivated a previously heterogeneous interface, or it may simply have made electron extraction uniformly poor. Construct a joint diagnostic framework that proves a contact is simultaneously homogenized, passivating and electron-extractive. Compare the expected signatures of (a) a passivating but blocking layer, (b) an extractive but defect-sensitive contact, and (c) a mixed tailored layer that combines surface passivation with favorable out-of-plane electronic coupling. Include the most informative component and sequence controls.

A mixed-cation 2D contact layer improves 1 cm2 spin-coated wide-bandgap cells, but a blade-coated module pilot shows a broad yield distribution. Devise a factorial scale-up study that determines whether the lower tail is caused by absorber-film nonuniformity, failure of the mixed 2D phase to co-assemble, or spatially nonuniform C60 deposition. Your plan must use spatially registered metrology, separate material and process variables, include a credible control for sequential versus premixed chemistry, and define quantitative acceptance criteria that predict tandem rather than only single-junction performance.

An ultrawide-bandgap top cell gains about 60-70 mV in Voc and shows slower ion-related degradation after pseudohalide substitution, yet the completed monolithic perovskite/perovskite/silicon triple-junction gains only modest power. Build a quantitative loss-localization strategy that determines why the isolated top-cell benefit does or does not translate through the three-junction stack. Your strategy must separate top-cell voltage preservation, optical/current mismatch, recombination-junction loss, processing damage to underlying subcells, area nonuniformity and luminescent coupling. Extend the plan to attribute degradation during damp-heat and light/heat tests to the correct subcell or interconnection.

You must replace an aspartate-based multifunctional additive with a new single molecular salt for a different Sn-Pb narrow-bandgap composition and a different hole-contact polymer. Propose a screening funnel that preserves the useful design logic without assuming that the strongest-binding molecule will be best. Define the molecular functions, computational and solution-chemistry filters, crystallization and redox tests, interface/bulk diagnostics, ion-migration and stability tests, and the decision rules for translation into a monolithic all-perovskite tandem. Include at least four failure modes that stronger coordination or higher additive loading could create.

A volatile alkylammonium chloride additive produces a smoother, more strongly textured alpha-FAPbI3 film and accelerates the delta-to-alpha conversion, yet little of the additive or chloride remains after the final anneal. Design a time- and depth-resolved experiment that distinguishes three possible mechanisms: permanent bulk doping, transient Pb-Cl coordination in the wet or intermediate film, and antisolvent-driven surface templating by the organic cation. State the decisive observations for each mechanism and the controls needed to avoid confusing faster phase conversion with better crystallization.

A spin-coated alpha-FAPbI3 process relies on a discrete antisolvent drip, a short room-temperature aging step, a volatile alkylammonium chloride, and a subsequent anneal. Translate this chemistry to slot-die or blade coating, where a discrete antisolvent drip is impractical. Define a process window and an in-line qualification plan that preserve transient additive-assisted crystallization while preventing residual additive, roughness, pinholes, and spatially nonuniform phase conversion. Include the expected signatures of under-extraction, over-extraction, and over-retention of the additive.

A passivated zero-bias perovskite detector has a dark-count density of 2 counts s^-1 mm^-2 in a small test pixel. A scintillator instrument requires roughly 100 mm2 of photosensitive area. Explain why simply fabricating one large pixel can erase the photon-counting advantage even if the material quality is unchanged. Propose an array architecture and qualification protocol that preserve weak-signal detection, energy resolution, and long-term stability after scale-up.

A formamidinium lead iodide film made with an amidinium additive ends with strong (100) texture and no detectable yellow or intermediate phase. Design an operando experiment that proves the texture originates at the nucleation event because the additive lowers the free energy of a specific facet, rather than arising later from selective grain growth, dissolution-reprecipitation, or annealing. State the time-resolved signatures and perturbation controls that distinguish these mechanisms.

An additive that promotes direct, oriented black-phase FAPbI3 nucleation in spin-coated films is transferred to a 30-cm-wide slot-die process with a much longer wet-film lifetime. Explain why both insufficient and excessive nucleation delay can destroy module uniformity. Propose a closed-loop scale-up strategy that preserves phase-selective orientation across the web and define the inline and accelerated-stability criteria required before accepting the process.

A flexible graded single-crystal perovskite device loses fill factor after combined cyclic bending and 1-sun operation, while conventional XRD still shows a highly crystalline absorber. Construct a failure-analysis protocol that separates four mechanisms: mechanical cracking, electronically defective transfer/re-adhesion interfaces, transport-layer or contact degradation, and instability of the axial Pb-Sn gradient. Give the discriminating signatures and the minimum control structures.

A wider-bandgap perovskite LED prototype is reported to turn on at only about 70% of its optical bandgap voltage, but its operational lifetime is poor. Explain why a low turn-on voltage alone does not prove reduced Joule heating or improved stability. Propose a redesign and a matched-luminance qualification protocol that determine whether the low-voltage strategy is a genuine stability advantage rather than a consequence of leakage, current crowding, or unbalanced carrier injection.

An interlayer at a perovskite/transport-layer interface increases both Young's modulus and interfacial fracture strength, and devices survive thermal cycling better. Explain why increased stiffness alone is not sufficient evidence for improved thermal-cycle reliability. Construct a diagnostic framework that separates the roles of elastic stiffness, adhesion/fracture toughness, and moisture-induced chemical weakening.

A tightly packed heterochiral interlayer is optimal for rigid glass devices under damp heat and thermal cycling, but the target product is a flexible perovskite module that must survive repeated bending. Propose how you would decide between a stiff heterochiral layer, a softer homochiral layer, or a graded/mixed interlayer. State the failure metrics and the evidence needed to avoid sacrificing electronic quality for mechanical compliance.

Thermally accelerated light-dark cycling of a perovskite module yields an apparently linear Arrhenius plot and a single activation energy. Explain why this does not uniquely prove that bulk iodide migration is the rate-limiting degradation process. Design a perturbation matrix that can distinguish reversible ionic redistribution, irreversible iodine transfer into the electron contact, and contact-independent thermal decomposition.

A surface-reconstructed perovskite module has a projected multi-year T80 from accelerated light-dark cycling and performs well during a short hot-humid outdoor trial. Define a validation program for claiming durability in a different climate with strong UV, seasonal freezing, and frequent partial shading. Explain which parts of the original lifetime projection can and cannot be transferred directly.

A buried-interface treatment raises the perovskite half-stack photoluminescence quantum yield and quasi-Fermi-level splitting, but both fall substantially after the electron-contact layer is deposited. Explain how to determine whether the full-device voltage is now limited by the top contact, residual bulk recombination, or damage introduced during contact deposition. Give the expected signature of each case.

An amphiphilic hole-selective underlayer works because an anchored monolayer remains on the electrode while an excess wetting layer dissolves during perovskite coating. Develop a manufacturing process window for this two-population system on a large substrate. What inline or near-line measurements would detect too little anchored material, too much residual excess, and nonuniform dissolution before those defects become module shunts or long-term instability?

During two-step conversion of an FA-rich lead-halide perovskite, adding a multiiodide reagent to the organic-halide conversion solution leaves film thickness and grain morphology essentially unchanged, but reduces residual PbI2, eliminates one deep electronic trap, lowers a second trap population, increases PLQY and carrier lifetime, and raises Voc. Three explanations remain plausible: (H1) iodide-stoichiometry repair of a deficient precursor intermediate during conversion, (H2) persistent iodine/triiodide redox doping or surface passivation after crystallization, and (H3) selective chemical modification of the TiO2/perovskite interface. Construct the smallest decisive control matrix and time/depth-resolved measurement sequence that can distinguish these hypotheses. State the result pattern that would support H1 and at least two observations that would falsify it.

A multiiodide additive gives a narrow optimum when used during two-step perovskite conversion, and the active stock solution is created by thermally aging iodine in an alcohol. The process must now be transferred from spin-coated small cells to continuous slot-die coating of large-area modules. Design a process-control and reliability workflow that determines whether the additive provides robust stoichiometric defect repair rather than batch-dependent transient doping or harmful iodine excess. Which stock-solution, wet-film, final-film, module, and aging measurements define the process window, and what outcomes constitute a go/no-go decision?

An unencapsulated additive-treated wide-bandgap Sn-perovskite cell retains more efficiency than a control during nitrogen storage, short maximum-power tracking, and moderate-humidity exposure, but it still loses nearly half of its initial output after several days in humid air. Construct an early-stage and late-stage failure sequence that includes Sn oxidation, moisture ingress, ion migration, film stress, and contact/interface degradation. Then specify a stress matrix that can identify which process limits the remaining lifetime improvement.

An unencapsulated three-cell antimony-halide minimodule is highly stable in dark ambient storage, but under one-sun maximum-power-point operation at moderate humidity it loses 30% of its power within 300 h. During the first 100 h, total open-circuit voltage remains close to three times the single-cell value and the absorber optical spectrum is unchanged, whereas module fill factor falls, series resistance rises, and electroluminescence reveals one weak stripe coincident with a P2 interconnect. Later, the current also declines. Determine the most likely sequence of failure. Design a minimum experiment set that separates absorber photochemical degradation, transport-layer/electrode degradation, P2 contact failure, and current mismatch among the series cells.

Redesign an all-perovskite tandem interconnecting layer for a flexible module that must be fabricated below 100 °C, survive 10,000 bending cycles, block the solvent used for the upper perovskite, transmit near-infrared light to the lower narrow-bandgap subcell, and avoid mobile noble metals. The original rigid-cell interconnect is fullerene/ALD-SnO2/sputtered ITO/PEDOT:PSS. Propose a replacement stack and process sequence. Explain how the new design supplies vertical recombination, solvent isolation, low lateral shunting, mechanical compliance, and scalable patterning. Define the qualification tests and failure criteria.

An unencapsulated all-inorganic perovskite device containing a dynamic defect-buffering framework retains high efficiency during isothermal storage but loses Voc and then fill factor during repeated thermal cycling between room temperature and 100 °C in humid nitrogen. Post-mortem XRD shows only a small amount of yellow phase, while KPFM reveals increasingly heterogeneous surface potential and the dark current rises strongly. Develop the most plausible failure sequence. Explain why little bulk yellow phase does not rule out vacancy-driven degradation, and specify the measurements that would distinguish framework fatigue, interfacial ion accumulation, and moisture-assisted chemical decomposition.

A coordinating tin-salt additive deepens both band edges of a 1.4 eV all-tin perovskite by roughly 0.1 eV and passivates vacancies. You want to transfer the concept to a 1.20-1.25 eV Sn-Pb bottom cell in an all-perovskite tandem, where current matching and the recombination junction are fixed. Explain when the same band-edge shift would improve versus reduce tandem performance. Propose a transfer strategy that preserves defect passivation while re-optimizing contact energetics, and define the minimum optical, electrical, and chemical acceptance criteria before claiming successful transfer.

An inverted solar cell uses a roughly 20 µm thick, methylammonium-free FA/Cs single-crystal absorber and already exhibits a long carrier lifetime and broad near-infrared response. You are asked to reduce the absorber thickness below 10 µm to improve carrier collection and reduce material use without sacrificing phase purity or photocurrent. Propose a growth-and-device redesign. Explain the governing tradeoffs among absorption length, diffusion length, surface recombination, contact damage, series resistance, and optical trapping, and define evidence that would show the thinner crystal is genuinely superior rather than merely giving a higher fill factor at lower current.

A strongly coordinating Lewis-base additive widens the coating-temperature window by stabilizing an intermediate phase. Explain the stability risk if a small fraction of the additive or intermediate remains after annealing. Under heat, illumination, humidity, and electrical bias, describe how residual coordination could either suppress or accelerate degradation. Design a stress matrix and diagnostic set that determines whether the kinetic buffer leaves a chemically benign final film.

An ammonium-iodide surface treatment raises stabilized output during a short MPP measurement. Explain why this does not establish long-term stability and identify degradation pathways specific to a 2D/3D ammonium-salt interface under heat, light, humidity, and bias. Construct a failure-analysis program that determines whether the passivator delays degradation, merely changes the initial burn-in, or creates a new transport-limited aging mode.

A wide-bandgap mixed-halide cell is operated for 1000 h under simultaneous one-sun illumination and elevated temperature. During the first tens of hours, Jsc decreases while Voc and FF remain nearly constant, the PL peak shifts under light but substantially recovers in the dark, and the low-frequency ionic response grows. At later times, PL recovery becomes incomplete, iodide accumulates near a transport layer, and Voc and FF collapse. Explain the most likely staged failure sequence and why increasing the ion-migration barrier may delay, but not necessarily eliminate, the terminal failure.

A dopant-free polymer HTM and doped Spiro-OMeTAD both show little decay during dry dark storage. Under humid air, the Spiro device loses Voc rapidly, whereas under dry continuous illumination at 40 °C the polymer device first retains efficiency but later develops rising series resistance and a vertical composition gradient in the polymer layer. Explain the different degradation pathways, the likely electrical signatures, and why neither dark storage nor a single light-soaking test is sufficient to establish operational stability.

A salt-passivated n-i-p perovskite device initially has high PLQY, favorable surface work function, and improved VOC. During light-and-heat aging, PLQY remains relatively high but the surface potential drifts, then develops the opposite sign in some regions. FF falls, an S-shaped J-V curve appears, and XPS shows increasing iodine loss and metallic Pb signatures. The passivator signal itself remains detectable. Explain how a defect-mediated interfacial dipole can create this failure even when chemical coverage and trap passivation persist. Propose a quasi-operando validation plan and design changes that would make the interface robust to an evolving defect population.

The same ammonium salt raises the surface work function of an iodine-vacancy-rich n-type perovskite by roughly 0.5 eV but lowers the work function of a lead-vacancy-rich p-type perovskite. In both cases, PL indicates fewer traps. You must decide whether to use this salt at the perovskite/hole-contact interface of an n-i-p cell and at the perovskite/C60 electron-contact interface of a p-i-n cell. Predict when the treatment will improve or damage VOC and FF in each architecture. Then define an architecture-aware screening workflow that prevents trap passivation from being mistaken for favorable energy-level alignment.

A 2D-capped 3D perovskite solar cell loses efficiency during combined heat, illumination, and bias. Operando absorption develops features assigned to higher-n quasi-2D phases, but this correlation does not prove that A-site or spacer-cation migration caused the device decay. Construct a causal failure analysis that distinguishes cation-driven 2D/3D reconstruction from halide exchange, spacer desorption, and purely electronic contact degradation. Specify the stress controls, species-resolved measurements, temporal sequence, and reversibility tests required for a defensible assignment.

Two otherwise identical perovskite cells are preconditioned for 30 s at opposite biases and then switched to the same maximum-power-point voltage. Cell A shows a transient current overshoot accompanied by suppressed photoluminescence; Cell B shows a current undershoot accompanied by enhanced photoluminescence. Both converge to the same steady state over seconds, and the convergence accelerates strongly with temperature. Explain how opposite ionic profiles can produce these signatures, and state the evidence needed to rule out electronic trap occupancy or a simple RC transient.

The concept of fluoride-mediated bifunctional passivation is to be transferred from a regular TiO2/perovskite interface to an inverted NiOx/perovskite interface. Direct acid soaking is prohibited, and excessive fluoride can form an insulating nickel-fluoride-rich layer or shift the NiOx work function in the wrong direction. Propose a self-limiting interfacial chemistry and validation plan that preserves simultaneous NiOx-side and perovskite-side passivation without creating a hole-extraction barrier.

A team wants a self-formed perovskite-related coherent interlayer at SnO2/FAPbI3 because such layers can combine passivation and structural compatibility. In preliminary trials, a narrow precursor-composition window gives high voltage, but a small excess of the interlayer-forming species produces parasitic low-dimensional crystallites, reduced current, and large spatial nonuniformity during slot-die coating. Design a self-limiting chemistry and process-control strategy that makes the interlayer robust enough for module fabrication, and specify the evidence required to prove that it is coherent, electronically benign, and stable.

A manufacturer proposes coating a metastable CsPbI2Br precursor film at one site, storing and transporting the unconverted film for 24-48 h, and performing the high-temperature crystallization at a second site. Assess whether this “deferred crystallization” concept is scientifically defensible. Design the intermediate-state specification, packaging, conversion, and quality-control workflow, and identify failure modes that would make centralized later annealing unacceptable.

After 5,000 fold cycles of a laser-scribed flexible perovskite module, the summed open-circuit voltage remains close to its initial value but fill factor collapses. Infrared imaging under load shows hot spots near intersections between metal-mesh lines and P2/P3 scribes, while average transparent-electrode sheet resistance rises only modestly. Diagnose the likely failure sequence and propose measurements that separate current crowding, local ITO cracking, mesh delamination, scribe damage, and absorber degradation. Then identify the most direct mechanical redesigns.

A fluorinated bulky spacer improves an n = 4 FA-based quasi-2D perovskite. Predict how the same spacer strategy should be re-optimized for nominal n = 3 and n = 6 absorbers rather than transferred at fixed spacer concentration. Discuss phase distribution, quantum/organic barriers, vertical transport, defect passivation, and stability, and define a screening workflow that can select different optima for the two n values.

A carbazole-ammonium monolayer is effective when placed between an FAPbI3 absorber and a hole-transport material, where it provides moisture resistance and defect passivation. You now want to use an inverted p-i-n architecture in which the treated perovskite surface will contact C60 instead. Analyze the selectivity and transport risks of transferring the same molecule unchanged, and propose a molecular or architectural redesign that preserves waterproofing without blocking electron extraction.

An FA-assisted SnO2 buried interface greatly improves device retention during 85 °C aging. Develop an experiment that determines whether the benefit arises mainly from stronger mechanical adhesion and lower residual tensile stress, from suppression of ion migration/interfacial redox, or from both. Your answer must distinguish primary failure suppression from a merely slower manifestation of the same failure.

A flexible perovskite absorber contains a graphene-oxide scaffold grafted with Pb-binding polyacid chains. Increasing additive content first improves grain size, residual strain, carrier lifetime, and fill factor, but excess additive lowers device efficiency. Develop a mechanistic model for this nonmonotonic response that distinguishes beneficial heat spreading and precursor coordination from two possible high-loading penalties: formation of electronically resistive grain-boundary regions and formation of a conductive percolation path. Specify the measurements and contrasting signatures needed to identify which penalty dominates.

A PEAI-only treatment raises the open-circuit voltage of a wide-bandgap p-i-n perovskite cell but slightly reduces fill factor, whereas a combined MASCN+PEAI treatment raises both voltage and fill factor. Construct a mechanism that distinguishes three contributions: defect passivation, an electronically resistive low-dimensional surface layer, and grain-regrowth-mediated changes in vertical transport. Then specify a minimum experiment set that can assign the fill-factor difference to one or more of these contributions.

A neutral 1D Pb-I coordination network localizes at perovskite grain boundaries. At 2 mol% loading, trap density decreases, carrier lifetime increases, and device efficiency improves; at 4 mol%, trap-related and photovoltaic metrics worsen. Construct a quantitative microstructural model for this nonmonotonic behavior and design experiments that distinguish incomplete passivation at low loading, optimal boundary coverage, and excessive electronically blocking coverage at high loading.

A pseudo-module study uses oxide-exposed scribes as silane-bonded mechanical anchors, but a commercial monolithic module contains electrically distinct P1, P2, and P3 scribes. Determine which interconnect regions can be filled or modified safely, and design an anchor topology that increases fracture resistance without shorting subcells, raising series resistance, or compromising laser isolation. Include electrical, mechanical, and environmental validation.

The same ammonium ligand improves Voc and stability when used as a top-surface treatment in an n-i-p perovskite solar cell, but reduces fill factor when introduced at the buried interface of an otherwise similar p-i-n cell. Both films show higher PLQY than their untreated controls. Build an architecture-dependent mechanism that reconciles these results. Your explanation must account for where the low-dimensional phase forms, its n-value/orientation, interfacial dipoles, and the direction of majority-carrier extraction.

A PCBM/metal cathode interlayer is formed by blending an ion-blocking, metal-coordinating molecule with a conductive polymer. Increasing the polymer fraction lowers contact resistance and raises initial fill factor, but accelerated ageing shows faster iodide arrival at the metal. Develop a composition-and-thickness optimization strategy that preserves the anti-corrosion function without sacrificing electron extraction. State the expected signatures in TLM/EIS, transient extraction, ToF-SIMS, and metal-corrosion measurements at under-, optimally, and over-conductive compositions.

A crystallization-control strategy for a lead-based quasi-2D perovskite is transferred to a tin-based analogue. The transferred recipe produces excellent vertical orientation but poor Voc and rapid degradation even in dry nitrogen. Construct a revised process-structure-property framework that incorporates Sn2+ oxidation kinetics in addition to phase orientation. Which process variables and diagnostics should be added, and why can the most vertically oriented film still be electronically inferior?

Perovskite cells made with a highly reproducible robot-coated absorber are aged under continuous illumination in nitrogen at 60-65 °C. After roughly 1000 h, the dominant loss is fill factor, Voc decreases only slightly, Jsc is nearly unchanged, and ex situ absorption, XRD, and spatial PL maps of companion absorber films remain stable. Construct the most defensible failure diagnosis. Explain why absorber reproducibility does not by itself identify the failing component, and specify a post-mortem sequence that can distinguish transport-layer deterioration, contact resistance or electrode reactions, ion redistribution, and latent absorber damage.

In a 1.80/1.27 eV monolithic all-perovskite tandem, the high-gap subcell is examined by subcell-selective luminescence. Its PLQY rises strongly with excitation density at low injection and then approaches a plateau. Replacing PTAA with a phosphonic-acid self-assembled monolayer shifts the whole PLQY curve upward; adding a thin LiF layer gives its largest benefit at low injection; adding an amine grain modifier reduces pixel-to-pixel PLQY variation. Nevertheless, the EL-derived quasi-Fermi-level splitting remains below the PL-derived value in both the tandem and an otherwise matched high-gap single-junction device. Diagnose the distinct loss mechanisms addressed by the three interventions, explain the residual PL–EL discrepancy, and specify the minimum evidence needed to avoid attributing all improvements to generic “passivation.”

The same fluorinated COF is proposed for a narrow-bandgap Pb–Sn perovskite in which Sn2+ oxidation, rapid crystallization, and electron-transport losses are dominant. Determine which elements of the original multi-site design are likely to transfer, which may fail or become harmful, and how the COF chemistry and process should be redesigned. Include experiments that distinguish useful crystallization control from Sn oxidation, over-retardation, and formation of an electronically blocking grain-boundary network.

Molecule B has a larger calculated gas-phase dipole moment than molecule A, but both produce nearly the same UPS vacuum-level shift at low coverage. At higher dose, B gives a larger XPS passivation signature yet a lower fill factor and higher contact resistance. Explain why molecular dipole moment alone does not determine the interfacial potential step or device benefit. Formulate the relevant interfacial variables and design measurements that separate dipole orientation/coverage, chemical passivation, and formation of a transport barrier.

A perovskite photovoltaic cell delivers 1.10 V open-circuit voltage, but a CO2 electrolyzer requires 1.65 V at the target current and gradually rises to 1.80 V as it ages. Compare direct electrical coupling using two identical PV cells in series with coupling through an MPPT/DC–DC stage. Select an architecture for a long-duration demonstrator and define the electrical, chemical, stability, and containment metrics needed to report a defensible solar-to-fuel result.

The fluoroarene-hydrazine treatment is transferred from an iodide-rich Pb perovskite to a 1.25 eV Pb–Sn absorber. Voc initially improves, but dark conductivity falls and the Sn4+/Sn2+ ratio increases after processing. Redesign the treatment and establish whether the original anchoring, dipole, and ion-immobilization functions can be retained without accelerating Sn oxidation or creating an electron-extraction barrier. Include composition-specific controls and stability tests.

A thin Dion–Jacobson cap is proposed for a 1.75 eV bromide-rich perovskite top cell. The cap should suppress interfacial recombination and halide migration, but low-n phases may impede electron extraction and solvent reconstruction may redistribute Br. Define the target phase/depth profile, processing window, and stress-validation plan that could preserve current matching in a monolithic tandem while reducing light-induced segregation.

Apply a stack-resolved transient-PL framework to a monolithic two-terminal perovskite tandem. Selective excitation of the high-gap subcell can also produce low-gap emission through luminescent coupling, while the recombination interconnect and external electrodes store charge. Design a protocol that separates high-gap recombination, inter-subcell photon transfer, carrier transfer through the interconnect, and capacitive voltage redistribution. State the reference stacks, optical/electrical boundary conditions, and model-validation criteria.

A ferrocene interlayer causes stronger steady-state PL quenching and a shorter perovskite/HTL TRPL decay, but transient absorption shows a longer-lived spiro-OMeTAD hole-polaron signal, while device Voc and fill factor both increase. Explain why these observations are mutually consistent rather than contradictory. Design controls that distinguish faster forward hole transfer plus slower back recombination from a new non-radiative quenching channel introduced by ferrocene.

A comparison finds a planar perovskite mini-module cooler than a textured silicon mini-module, but the perovskite package uses TPU while the silicon package uses POE, and their TCOs differ. Design a matched experiment and modeling workflow that can determine how much of the temperature difference is caused by absorber bandgap/texture, encapsulant and TCO spectral absorption, and thermal boundary properties. Define the minimum module set, measurements, and criteria for making a technology-level claim.

A low-dose ethylammonium additive improves the initial efficiency and a 60 h unencapsulated MPP test of a 3D FA/Cs perovskite, but its long-term benefit under repeated light–dark and humidity cycles is unknown. Develop a failure map for this additive. Explain how ethylammonium could either suppress or accelerate ion migration, phase instability, and contact degradation, and design a stress matrix that identifies which mechanism controls lifetime.

A pyrazine-derived surface passivator increases neat-film PLQY and device Voc at low illumination, but after prolonged one-sun bias light the Voc gain largely disappears while the neat-film PLQY remains high. Diagnose the most likely separation between bulk/surface chemical passivation and device-interface energetic effects. What measurements would determine whether the lost gain is caused by passivator desorption, dipole reorientation, ionic screening, or a new extraction barrier at the perovskite/C60 contact?

A fluorinated sulfonate additive shifts the perovskite surface work function by about 0.3 eV, increases the built-in potential, and is described as producing a more n-type surface. Explain why these observations do not by themselves prove bulk electronic doping. Design measurements that distinguish bulk doping, a molecular surface dipole, fixed interfacial charge, and ion-redistribution-induced electrostatic screening.

Two near-intrinsic perovskite films have the same one-sun QFLS. Film A maintains high PLQY down to very low excitation, whereas Film B loses PLQY sharply at low excitation but approaches Film A at one sun. Using full SRH statistics, explain how the films can share the same one-sun QFLS yet contain different trap landscapes. Predict their relative performance under indoor light and under concentrated illumination, and state which measurements are needed to distinguish shallow traps, deep traps, and photodoping.

An all-inorganic mixed-I/Br perovskite is illuminated under four otherwise identical conditions: inert control, addition of a reversible electron scavenger, addition of a reversible hole scavenger, and simultaneous addition of both scavengers. The electron scavenger suppresses metallic Pb formation but increases oxidized iodine signatures; the hole scavenger produces the opposite trend. Predict how grain-boundary I-rich phase nucleation should change if coupled Pb2+/Pb0 and I-/polyiodide redox chemistry is causally required for segregation. Explain which observation would instead support a predominantly strain-, polaron-, or diffusion-driven mechanism.

A chemically defined plant-derived molecule improves spin-coated perovskite cells by slowing solvent evaporation and promoting a beneficial intermediate phase. When transferred unchanged to blade coating, the film develops an early nucleation front, lateral composition gradients, and lower module yield. Develop a scale-up strategy that preserves the molecular function under a different drying regime while maintaining a credible green-manufacturing claim.

During maximum-power aging of two otherwise identical inverted cells, the absorber XRD pattern, optical absorption, and top-surface contact angle remain nearly unchanged. In the weaker device, JSC is stable but VOC and fill factor decay together, hysteresis and low-frequency capacitance increase, and partial performance recovery occurs after dark rest. Diagnose the most likely buried-contact failure sequence. Distinguish reversible ionic redistribution from irreversible monolayer loss, NiOx redox chemistry, or creation of an extraction barrier, and specify the pre/post-aging controls needed to assign causality.

A precursor-added bridge molecule lowers the measured work function and produces more n-type character at the bottom surface of a wide-bandgap perovskite, even though that surface contacts a hole-selective self-assembled monolayer in a p-i-n device. The same treatment increases built-in potential, accelerates hole extraction, and improves VOC and fill factor. Reconcile this apparently counterintuitive result. Explain how a local interfacial dipole or defect-compensation layer can improve hole selectivity without beneficially n-doping the entire absorber, and define measurements that would distinguish local band bending from bulk doping or an unintended electron-leakage pathway.

FK209 doping raises the conductivity of a paracyclophane hole-transport film to approximately the same scale as doped spiro-MeOTAD and removes an s-shaped J-V curve, yet the resulting devices can still have lower VOC than tBP-containing recipes. Construct a loss analysis that separates bulk HTL conductivity from interfacial recombination and energetic mismatch. Explain how high doping efficiency can coexist with reduced hole mobility and voltage loss, and identify the measurements needed before concluding that the dopant recipe is device-optimal.

Four treatments deliver nominally similar formate exposure to a FAPbI3 device process: Pb(formate)2 on SnO2, Na formate on SnO2, Pb(formate)2 added directly to the perovskite precursor, and formic acid on SnO2. Build a mechanistic decision tree that determines whether the performance gain requires formate coordination to SnO2, a local Pb-containing precursor reservoir, or stabilization of a delayed perovskite intermediate. Specify the minimum orthogonal measurements and the expected pattern for each hypothesis.

The low-dimensional cap suppresses light-induced spectral red-shift in a mixed I/Br absorber. Design an experiment that determines whether the cap truly lowers halide-ion mobility, merely reduces the carrier-density gradients that drive segregation, or simply optically masks emission from segregated domains. Your answer must include bias and illumination controls, spatially resolved measurements, activation-energy analysis, and a falsifiable criterion for each mechanism.

As the concentration of a fluorinated polymer in a FAMA perovskite is increased, open-circuit voltage first improves and then plateaus, while fill factor and current decline beyond an intermediate dose. Build a mechanistic model for the transition from beneficial crystallization templating and grain-boundary passivation to an insulating polymer network. Predict the coordinated signatures expected in local conductivity, carrier mobility, luminescence, impedance, and temperature-dependent device operation.

Two TBAB-functionalized Ti3C2Tx cathode-buffer films have the same area-averaged UPS work function, yet one gives much higher fill factor and lower hysteresis. The films differ in flake orientation, termination distribution, and nanoscale dipole uniformity. Explain how these hidden variables can produce different device behavior despite identical average work function, and design the local measurements and device controls needed to identify the dominant cause.

A NiOx/polymer bilayer initially retains photovoltaic performance under 365 nm illumination, but during a longer mixed UV-heat-oxygen stress its open-circuit voltage and fill factor decline. Develop an action-spectrum-based failure protocol that separates simple UV filtering from NiOx surface-redox passivation, polymer photooxidation, perovskite photochemistry, and contact degradation. State the controls and the spectral, chemical, and electrical signatures expected for each mechanism.

An optimized hygroscopic ionic passivant reduces initial surface recombination but gives no clear improvement in ambient shelf stability. Develop a mechanistic explanation and a discriminating aging study. Separate water uptake by the passivant, passivant dissolution or redistribution, accelerated halide/guanidinium ion migration, interfacial dipole drift, and ordinary bulk perovskite degradation. State the signatures that would show whether initial passivation and long-term stability are governed by different rate-limiting processes.

An FPTMS-treated inverted cell remains stable under maximum-power-point illumination but later develops a rising series resistance with little initial loss of open-circuit voltage. Construct a time-resolved failure analysis under simultaneous light and heat in a device with PC61BM/BCP/Ag. Distinguish silane-layer reorganization, electron-contact degradation, silver-halide reaction, and renewed perovskite defect formation.

An initially ordered quasi-2D quantum-well gradient slowly flattens during heat and humidity aging, while the device first loses fill factor and only later loses open-circuit voltage. Explain the coupled thermodynamic, ionic, and interfacial failure sequence. Identify measurements that separate spacer migration, phase redistribution, contact-induced ion accumulation, and irreversible decomposition.

The dual-phase bromide nanowire interlayer is deposited on an iodide-rich perovskite absorber and then aged under light, heat, humidity, and operating bias. Construct a coupled failure pathway involving halide exchange, ligand loss, phase conversion, and ion migration. Predict which measurements change first and which failure could be hidden by an apparently stable initial PCE.

Predict the sequence of changes when pristine UHV-grown CsSnBr3 is exposed separately to dry O2, water vapor, and then humid air. Explain how Br vacancies, Br adatoms, metallic Sn0 at the Au interface, and Sn2+ participate. State which spatially resolved and chemical measurements would distinguish independent O2/H2O pathways from cooperative oxidation.

A wide-bandgap top cell containing residual PbI2 is placed in a two-terminal tandem and experiences partial shading that drives local reverse bias. Predict how reverse bias changes the mutual-destabilization loop relative to open-circuit illumination. Identify polarity-dependent spatial signatures and the measurements needed to distinguish electrical breakdown from iodine-mediated chemical propagation.

Two hole-transport underlayers are processed at the same chamber humidity and show similar water contact angles. Underlayer A contains little total water but releases a sharp pulse of weakly bound water during antisolvent exposure and early annealing; underlayer B contains more water by mass, but most of it is strongly bound and desorbs only above the perovskite annealing temperature. Predict how the two underlayers can produce different quasi-2D phase distributions and emission colors. Explain why equilibrium hygroscopicity, contact angle, or a single TGA mass-loss value is insufficient to predict the result.

As CNT loading increases in a MAPbI3/CNT absorber, electrical conductivity and attenuation constant rise, while MAPbI3 diffraction weakens, defect-sensitive Raman intensity increases, and PL is quenched without a peak shift. Explain why these trends do not imply that the highest CNT loading must give the strongest microwave absorption. Build a mechanism that includes percolation, polarization loss, impedance matching, and the possibility that excessive structural disruption removes useful dielectric response.

GIWAXS indicates that a guanidinium-modified quasi-2D emissive layer retains a preferentially in-plane orientation, which should impede vertical transport, yet the optimized LED has lower turn-on voltage and much higher EQE. Reconcile these observations without claiming that orientation is irrelevant. Explain how grain size, low-n/high-n energy transfer, spacer length, interfacial work function, defect density, and film thickness can collectively overcome—but not eliminate—the orientation penalty.

An orientation-engineered 1.77 eV top cell remains stable when tested alone, but the corresponding monolithic all-perovskite tandem loses current matching and fill factor under maximum-power operation. Analyze tandem-specific failure modes that would not be revealed by isolated top-cell retention. Propose a diagnostic sequence that distinguishes optical, electrical, ionic, and recombination-junction origins.

A polymer-soft-encapsulated perovskite module passes short water-leakage tests but gradually loses fill factor during combined heat, humidity, and maximum-power bias. Develop a failure model involving polymer hydrolysis, softening, migration, and interfacial accumulation. Explain which signatures would distinguish these polymer-mediated failures from ordinary perovskite decomposition.

A module containing a nominally stable RP-passivated interface operates at an average temperature of 65 °C, below the temperature at which uniform laboratory films reconstruct rapidly. Nevertheless, localized fill-factor loss appears near interconnects. Explain how bias and local Joule heating can trigger reconstruction below the measured average threshold, and design a protocol to prove the local causal sequence.

A monolithic two-terminal tandem combines a wide-bandgap perovskite front cell with a near-infrared organic rear cell. A new rear absorber increases the rear single-junction Jsc by 15%, but has lower mobility and requires a thicker film. The tandem is current-matched under the standard spectrum, yet under red-rich illumination and elevated temperature its fill factor decreases and the rear subcell develops a larger voltage-dependent collection loss. Develop a transfer decision for adopting the new absorber. Your answer must connect series-current constraints, optical thickness, transport and recombination, spectral/thermal variability, and long-term stability, and must define decisive subcell-resolved acceptance tests.

Design a quasi-2D perovskite absorber for a nominal 1.8 eV top cell in a monolithic tandem. The device must retain efficient vertical extraction while tolerating sustained illumination and 85 °C operation. Explain how you would choose between RP and DJ structural families, set the n-value distribution, select the spacer, control orientation, and passivate interfaces. Identify the failure modes that would invalidate an apparently high initial Voc, and define a validation sequence that separates true structural stability from encapsulation-only protection.

A redox-active ionic additive containing a ferrocenium-like cation and PF6− is introduced into Li-TFSI-doped spiro-OMeTAD. To separate its functions, three matched controls are prepared: neutral ferrocene, an inert-cation PF6 salt, and ferrocenium paired with TFSI−. Predict which parts of the following response each control should reproduce: rapid spiro oxidation, higher HTL conductivity, Li+ immobilization, Pb/iodide surface stabilization, suppressed Li/iodide migration, and improved Voc/FF. Give the decisive measurements and explain why no single control should reproduce the full device response.

Increasing the concentration of a selective sulfate-based additive in a Sn-Pb perovskite keeps the final Sn/Pb depth profile uniform and suppresses Sn4+, but beyond an optimum the device develops lower FF, stronger hysteresis, and a gradual rise in series resistance during heat-light aging. Diagnose the likely over-treatment failure modes and formulate a transferable dose-selection rule for absorbers with different Sn fractions and drying rates. The rule must not rely on a fixed mass concentration.

A sulfate-containing hydrazinium additive produces a more uniform Sn/Pb depth profile, sharper PL, longer front- and back-side TRPL lifetimes, lower Sn4+ content, and higher Voc and FF in a mixed Sn-Pb perovskite. Two mechanisms are proposed: selective slowing of Sn-rich crystallization and direct chemical stabilization of Sn2+. Design the smallest decisive control set that quantifies the contribution of each mechanism. State the expected signatures for hydrazinium without sulfate, sulfate without hydrazinium, addition only after crystallization, and the full molecule.

During FAI-assisted antisolvent purification of CsPbI3 quantum dots, the PL peak and XRD reflections shift monotonically with increasing FAI, while zeta potential moves from negative toward neutral and then positive. Film mobility, orientational order, and device PCE peak at an intermediate FA fraction and then collapse; high-FA films show Pb0 and a large Stokes shift. Explain the mechanistic sequence that produces these apparently conflicting trends. Which measurements distinguish beneficial vacancy-assisted A-site exchange from particle growth, ligand-shell loss, and defect-mediated energy transfer?

A multifunctional bridge optimized for a perovskite/PCBM interface must be transferred to a non-fullerene polymeric electron-transport layer that lacks PCBM’s aromatic fullerene surface and is processed from a different solvent. Propose a modular molecular redesign and qualification plan. The new bridge must preserve defect passivation and favorable band bending, promote adhesion and electron transfer to the new ETL, avoid acid-induced perovskite damage, and remain stable during coating and long-term operation.

A fluorinated dopant-free polymer HTM and doped spiro-OMeTAD give nearly identical Jsc and similar pristine-film hole mobility, but the polymer produces a deeper HOMO, higher Voc and FF, lower trap density, higher electroluminescence efficiency, an ideality factor closer to one, and a smoother perovskite/HTM interface. Diagnose which photovoltaic loss terms are reduced. Explain how to distinguish beneficial energy alignment and defect passivation from a hole-extraction barrier caused by an excessively deep HOMO.

A sparsely pyridine-functionalized PTAA-like HTM is transferred from an iodide-rich perovskite to a 1.8 eV mixed-halide buried interface. Under continuous illumination, the new device initially has high Voc but develops a low-energy PL shoulder and spatially nonuniform voltage. Explain how pyridine coordination, wetting-controlled crystallization, interfacial strain, and halide migration could interact. Propose an optimization and falsification plan that determines whether the polymer suppresses or accelerates light-induced segregation while preserving its interfacial benefits.

A Cs3ErCl6-based reactive treatment developed for an iodide-rich 1.55 eV absorber is proposed for a 1.75-1.80 eV mixed I/Br top-cell perovskite. Assess the transfer. Explain how Cs, Cl, and Er incorporation could alter crystallization, strain, bandgap, halide segregation, and defect chemistry. Propose a minimum screening program and state the conditions under which the original quantum dot, a composition-modified analog, or a non-rare-earth treatment should be selected.

A hole-transport-layer-free carbon perovskite cell is modified at the rear interface. Absolute photoluminescence indicates that the absorber quasi-Fermi-level splitting rises by 90 mV, but the measured open-circuit voltage rises by only 55 mV; short-circuit current is unchanged and fill factor improves. Construct a quantitative voltage-loss diagnosis. Explain where the missing 35 mV can reside and define the measurement set that separates absorber recombination, rear-contact selectivity, transport resistance, and lateral carbon-electrode nonuniformity.

In a molecularly implanted Spiro-OMeTAD film, increasing the F4TCNQ dose raises the oxidized-host absorption and shifts the HOMO deeper, but conductivity reaches a maximum and then declines. Develop a mechanistic explanation that separates carrier-density gain from mobility loss. Specify how energetic disorder, ionized-dopant Coulomb fields, aggregation, and vertical concentration gradients would be identified, and define the optimum doping criterion for a photovoltaic HTL.

A redox-active polyphenolic modifier on PEDOT:PSS increases the layer's conductivity, decreases its surface hydrophilicity, and reduces the hole-extraction barrier to a Sn-Pb perovskite. Explain why these three changes are not automatically mutually consistent. Design a mechanism-deconvolution study that distinguishes PEDOT:PSS phase rearrangement, acid neutralization, secondary doping/dedoping, and formation of an interfacial dipole, while testing whether the conductivity gain preserves hole selectivity.

A bifunctional salt suppresses ion migration and Ag corrosion during normal MPP operation, but a large-area series-connected module must also survive partial shading and reverse bias. Develop a reverse-bias qualification and redesign strategy. Address field-driven cation/anion redistribution, secondary-phase breakdown, local heating, electrode choice, bypass protection, and the possibility that a passivating surface layer becomes a high-field extraction barrier.

A dopant-free hydrophobic polymer hole contact works well with ANI pretreatment and a two-step SnI2/FAI deposition, but it must be transferred to a one-step, antisolvent-free, blade-coated tin-perovskite process. Explain why copying the ANI dose and polymer thickness is not a valid transfer. Define a functional process window that controls polymer swelling, surface energy, precursor residence time, nucleation, interfacial chemistry, and large-area electronic uniformity.

A CsPbI3−xBrx device using a LiTFSI-doped Spiro-OMeTAD contact and a bifunctional amine additive performs well in dark storage and in 65 °C nitrogen. Under combined one-sun illumination, humid air, and maximum-power-point bias, however, the fill factor begins to decline before a major loss of short-circuit current, and a yellow nonperovskite phase later appears. Construct the most plausible coupled failure sequence if Li+ coordination is beneficial but incomplete. Link water uptake, Li and halide redistribution, field screening, interfacial recombination, and black-to-yellow phase transformation. Identify the time-resolved measurements that would distinguish this sequence from simple electrode corrosion or purely optical phase degradation, and explain why dark storage plus inert-atmosphere thermal aging cannot establish operational durability.

A NiOx/MAPbI3 p-i-n device uses an alkyl phosphonic-acid monolayer whose useful coverage window is narrow. Predict two distinct degradation trajectories during heat and electrical operation: one for persistent undercoverage and one for local overcoverage. Your answer must connect NiOx dangling bonds or Ni3+-related sites, MAI interaction, perovskite nucleation, local current distribution, and possible AgI formation. State how time-resolved PL/EL imaging, impedance, capacitance, and post-mortem chemical mapping would distinguish the two trajectories.

Two FASnI3 devices have similar initial efficiency in a nitrogen glovebox. During repeated small oxygen excursions, one rapidly loses voltage and diffusion length, while the other contains a modest quasi-2D or bulky-cation component and degrades more slowly but develops a growing series resistance. Explain the competing failure mechanisms. Trace how oxygen exposure drives Sn2+ oxidation, Sn-vacancy-related self-doping, recombination, and film/interface deterioration in the 3D device. Then explain why the low-dimensional component can suppress some failures yet introduce transport and phase-distribution penalties. State the measurements needed to separate chemical oxidation, excessive background doping, and insulating-spacer transport loss.

An IPL-processed perovskite made with a sacrificial sulfoxide additive shows a higher apparent ion-migration barrier and better 500 h MPP retention. Consider two latent manufacturing defects: incomplete additive removal in cooler regions and excessive local IPL heating in hotter regions. Develop the distinct degradation sequence expected from each defect under light and bias. Relate residual coordination or decomposition fragments, halide transport, buried-interface voids, band alignment, and nonradiative recombination to the evolution of Voc, FF, hysteresis, and structural/chemical signatures.

In an all-air processed SnO2/perovskite device, the buried interface contains metal-coordinate defects and is exposed to oxygen- and moisture-assisted iodide redox chemistry. Construct a coupled degradation pathway from iodide oxidation to I2 release, iodide-vacancy formation, Pb0 generation, interfacial recombination, and further ion migration. Explain how a multisite antioxidant/chelating modifier can interrupt several links at once, and identify the endpoint failure mode that would remain if the modifier eventually becomes chemically consumed or its binding sites saturate. Use humidity, thermal, and MPP diagnostics to distinguish the stages.

The highest-efficiency device uses LiTFSI-doped Spiro-OMeTAD, but long-term stability is evaluated with a nondoped PBDB-T hole contact. What stability conclusions are transferable from the PBDB-T stack to the champion stack, and what conclusions are not? Develop the additional failure pathways introduced by returning to Spiro-OMeTAD/LiTFSI, including moisture uptake, Li migration, interaction with vertically segregated PVDF:DH fragments, residual PbI2 photolysis, and contact resistance. Propose a matched stability matrix that isolates absorber/additive durability from hole-contact-specific degradation.

Design a high-radiance NIR-II tin-perovskite LED rather than a low-brightness proof of concept. The narrow bandgap needed for 900-1700 nm emission increases intrinsic carrier density, p-type self-doping, Auger loss, and thermal load. Propose a material-and-device architecture that addresses these coupled penalties while preserving spectral purity. Identify the main tradeoffs and the measurements that would determine whether the design is viable.

You want to transfer cyano-Sn coordination from FASnI3 to a wider-bandgap tin-bromide or mixed Sn-Ge photodetector. Develop an additive-selection strategy that balances coordination strength, oxidation suppression, vacancy formation, crystallization kinetics, band alignment, and ion mobility. Explain how an additive can bind Sn too strongly and become harmful, and define the control series needed before claiming transferability.

A SnO2/MXene composite electron contact initially gives high conductivity and low interfacial recombination. During 85 °C maximum-power-point operation, the device retains nearly the same open-circuit voltage but gradually loses fill factor and short-circuit current. The MXene Ti core level shifts toward a more oxidized state, sheet resistance increases, and mobile halide is detected closer to the electron contact. Construct a ranked failure mechanism and an experiment that separates MXene oxidation, loss of electrical percolation, halide-induced interfacial reaction, and ordinary perovskite bulk degradation. State which observations would make the composite intrinsically less stable than pristine SnO2 despite its higher initial efficiency.

A dual-interface n-i-p design uses a Cl-terminated two-dimensional carbide at the SnO2/perovskite buried interface and a pi-conjugated carbon-rich two-dimensional material at the perovskite/hole-contact surface. You must transfer the concept to an inverted p-i-n stack with a phosphonic-acid hole contact below the perovskite and C60 above it. Decide which original modifier, if either, should be retained at each interface.
