Explain how carrier selectivity, chemical compatibility, solvent sequence, and band bending change the design logic, and propose a minimal experiment matrix that can distinguish successful transfer from simple defect passivation with a new extraction barrier.

A stability data package for a buried-interface modifier contains two complications: the high-efficiency device uses Spiro-OMeTAD, but the accelerated 60 °C/60% RH test substitutes P3HT; additionally, the text reports 91% retention after 1000 h whereas the figure caption states 500 h. As an expert benchmark evaluator, reconstruct the strongest defensible stability claim, identify which causal conclusions are invalid, and design the minimum repeat experiment needed to determine whether the modifier stabilizes the original device architecture under combined environmental and operational stress.

A fluorinated pyrrole-core small-molecule HTM combines good film formation, high hole mobility, a relatively deep HOMO, and Lewis-base interaction with Pb defects in a lead-halide perovskite. Evaluate its transfer to a tin-based perovskite, where Sn2+ oxidation, a shallower valence band, high p-type self-doping, and rapid surface chemistry dominate. Decide which molecular features should be retained, weakened, or redesigned, and propose a comparison that tests whether fluorination is still beneficial.

An n=1 Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite made with an insulating alkylammonium spacer shows a sharp, intense excitonic photoluminescence band, whereas analogous n=1 films made with two pi-conjugated spacers show much weaker and broader emission. In device-relevant n=5 films, however, the donor-acceptor conjugated spacer gives the longest carrier lifetime, the lowest trap density, and the best photovoltaic voltage and fill factor. Explain why these observations are not contradictory. Construct a mechanistic interpretation that distinguishes exciton dissociation and interlayer electronic coupling from nonradiative recombination, and identify the minimum measurements needed to avoid misreading weak PL as poor material quality.

A dopant-free phthalocyanine device retains most of its output during long maximum-power operation in nitrogen, whereas a conventional Li-TFSI/tBP-doped Spiro-OMeTAD control rapidly loses efficiency. Explain why this comparison does not by itself prove that the phthalocyanine's intramolecular electric field is the origin of the stability advantage. Build a matched failure-analysis experiment that separates intrinsic semiconductor stability, dopant-induced ionic failure, contact chemistry, and transport-layer morphology. State the signatures expected for each mechanism.

A new fluorinated asymmetric self-assembled monolayer has a larger molecular dipole, deeper substrate work function, denser packing, lower precursor contact angle, and stronger Pb coordination than a reference monolayer. A second-generation analogue increases the dipole and fluorine content further, yet devices show lower fill factor and a wider distribution of Voc despite complete film coverage. Diagnose why maximizing each apparently beneficial molecular property can produce a non-monotonic device response. Identify the competing interfacial mechanisms and the measurements that would locate the true optimum.

A bowl-shaped π-conjugated additive makes C60 sufficiently processable to form a smooth amorphous electron-transport layer. Solution NMR and fluorescence suggest association, but these observations do not establish whether the additive acts as a reversible molecular “chaperone” during drying, a permanent electronic dopant, or a residual plasticizer. Design a concentration-, temperature-, and process-dependent experiment that distinguishes these three mechanisms. State the decisive signatures expected in solution, during film formation, in the final solid, and in electron-transport measurements.

An ammonium–thiol passivator performs well under dry nitrogen but loses most of its voltage benefit during combined humidity, oxygen, heat, and illumination. XPS develops oxidized sulfur components, the surface potential drifts, and iodine-related degradation products increase. Build a chemical failure map for the passivator and redesign the molecule so that dual-site passivation and favorable orientation are retained without relying on an oxidation-sensitive free thiol. Define the validation sequence and rejection criteria.

A lattice-reinforced mixed-halide perovskite shows only moderate improvement under illumination alone or electrical bias alone, but a much larger advantage under simultaneous light and forward bias. Build a quantitative stress-response framework that can determine whether this nonlinearity arises from carrier–ion coupling and strain-assisted migration rather than simple Joule heating, different steady-state carrier densities, or contact-induced spectral artifacts. Specify matched controls and decisive observables.

An iodide-based one-dimensional ion-blocking layer is to be adapted to a bromide-rich wide-bandgap perovskite single crystal. Directly using the iodide layer may cause halide exchange, local bandgap narrowing, and an extraction barrier. Design a composition-matched low-dimensional interface, processing route, and validation plan that preserves ionic blocking without creating spectral or electronic heterogeneity.

Increasing surface Pb richness can increase the density of Pb–S–Mo bridges at a perovskite/MoS2 interface, but excessive Pb-richness may also create PbBr2-like residues, deep defects, or nonproductive recombination. Develop a mechanistic “volcano” model for photocatalytic activity versus surface stoichiometry and design a matched experiment that locates the optimum by separating interfacial bond density from surface-defect penalties.

A bifunctional additive optimized for a 50:50 Sn:Pb absorber is to be used in an 80% Sn or all-Sn perovskite. Explain how the HSAB balance, precursor aggregation, crystallization, and redox risk change as Pb content falls. Design a composition-dependent additive library and qualification matrix, and state when the original bifunctional architecture should be replaced by a Sn-selective strategy.

A layered hybrid perovskite undergoes, on heating, a transition from a low-symmetry multiaxial polar phase to an orthorhombic uniaxial polar phase and then to a centrosymmetric nonpolar phase. The optical absorption and dc conductivity change only gradually across this temperature range. Predict the temperature-dependent signatures expected in axis-resolved polarization-electric-field loops, ferroelastic domain imaging, and zero-bias open-circuit photovoltage. Explain which signatures would demonstrate that multidirectional self-driven photodetection is controlled by ferroic symmetry rather than merely by anisotropic transport.

During slot-die coating of a perovskite film, in situ GIWAXS shows disappearance of a solvent-intermediate peak followed by early growth of the perovskite Bragg peak. Simultaneous absorption reaches its final value, while photoluminescence rises sharply and then collapses before the film is fully dry. A stronger gas quench shifts crystallization earlier, increases the transient PL maximum, but produces a rougher final film with lower steady-state PL. Infer the likely sequence of nucleation, growth, solvent removal, and defect formation, and recommend how the process window should be adjusted.

A compositionally graded quasi-2D perovskite film is tuned to contain a larger fraction of low-n domains. As this fraction increases, its photoluminescence becomes spectrally narrower and the PeLED external quantum efficiency rises, but a solar cell made from the same film loses short-circuit current and fill factor despite reduced trap-assisted recombination. Explain the opposing trends using exciton binding, energy funneling, carrier density, vertical transport, and optical absorption.

A narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb perovskite film exhibits high terahertz mobility and a long low-fluence photoluminescence lifetime, yet its solar cell has a large open-circuit-voltage deficit. Temperature-dependent electroluminescence shows a broad sub-bandgap tail, and Voc continues to increase strongly as temperature is lowered before saturating. Explain how high mobility and lifetime can coexist with poor voltage, and diagnose the roles of energetic disorder, self-doping, and interface recombination.

Two perovskite solar cells contain the same amount and chemical identity of a bulky-spacer-derived 2D phase. In device A, the 2D phase forms an abrupt, largely parallel-to-substrate surface layer; in device B, its concentration is graded and the higher-n phases are preferentially oriented for vertical transport. Both show similar surface trap passivation, but B retains higher fill factor and better bias stability. Explain the difference using band offsets, phase orientation, carrier percolation, strain, and ion migration.

A halide perovskite shows increasing band-edge mobility as temperature falls from 300 K to 150 K, but below 100 K the dc mobility decreases, terahertz conductivity becomes strongly dispersive, and an excitonic absorption resonance strengthens. Construct a unified interpretation involving electron-phonon scattering, large polarons, disorder/localization, and the free-carrier-exciton equilibrium. Explain why no single mobility trend alone proves or disproves polaron formation.

A commercial recycler receives mixed perovskite photovoltaic waste with unknown absorber compositions, different transport layers, silver or gold electrodes, polymer encapsulants, and both intact and fire-damaged modules. Design an adaptive decommissioning line that can maximize safe reuse and high-value recovery without applying one destructive treatment to every module. Specify the incoming diagnostics, branching process logic, closed-loop controls, product qualification, and conditions under which repair, component reuse, material recycling, or downcycling should be selected.

Two perovskite cells have the same open-circuit voltage, one-sun quasi-Fermi-level splitting, and low-intensity photoluminescence lifetime, yet one loses much more power between open circuit and the maximum-power point. Develop a bias-resolved recombination diagnosis that determines whether the extra loss arises from interfacial recombination activated under carrier extraction, transport-induced carrier accumulation, field-dependent bulk trapping, or ordinary series resistance. State the measurements and mutually exclusive signatures.

A perovskite film appears strain-uniform in an ex situ room-temperature map, but under simultaneous illumination and heating it develops transient local strain hotspots that coincide with current-voltage hysteresis and disappear in the dark. Determine whether the hotspots arise from ordinary thermoelastic expansion, light-driven ionic or compositional redistribution, a reversible structural phase transition, or relaxation of mechanical constraint at interfaces. Design an operando experiment and state the discriminating time, bias, and spatial signatures.

A perovskite-nanocrystal supercrystal retains the absorption edge and composition of its individual nanocrystals after humidity and heat cycling, but its narrow polarized emission and fast collective radiative component disappear. Construct a failure mechanism in which the nanocrystal cores remain intact while the supercrystal loses collective behavior. Design measurements that distinguish ligand swelling or desorption, spacing disorder, rotational disorder, domain cracking, and a simple change in optical-cavity conditions, and define a credible recovery test.

A strongly confined blue-emitting lead-halide perovskite quantum-dot sample shows three low-temperature features: a weak red-shifted long-lived emission band, a prompt narrow band with polarization fine structure, and intermittent dark periods in single-dot traces. Construct an experiment that distinguishes a dark-exciton fine-structure state, a charged trion undergoing Auger recombination, and a surface-trapped exciton. State the temperature-, magnetic-field-, excitation-density-, and photon-statistics signatures that would support or falsify each assignment.

Design a modular perovskite-nanocrystal platform that uses a common emissive core for both aqueous biological imaging and X-ray scintillation, while allowing application-specific outer layers. Resolve the conflicts among water/ion isolation, biocompatibility, high nanocrystal loading, optical transparency, radiolysis resistance, and charge or energy transport. Define separate qualification criteria for the imaging probe and the scintillator.

Photovoltaic-style defect passivation improves a perovskite memristor's retention and endurance but nearly eliminates analog conductance updates. Design a spatially graded material/device architecture that preserves a controlled mobile-ion reservoir for learning while suppressing parasitic reactions and long-term drift. Explain how the programming protocol and algorithm should be co-designed with the physical gradient, and define the device-level criteria for success.

A thin single-crystal perovskite photovoltaic absorber has a long bulk lifetime and high mobility-lifetime product, yet its complete device shows lower open-circuit voltage and fill factor than a high-quality polycrystalline control of the same bandgap. Build a diagnostic hierarchy that distinguishes surface recombination, damaged crystal preparation, contact injection barriers, and bulk transport limitations. Explain how internal quasi-Fermi-level splitting should be reconciled with the external device voltage.

Red and near-infrared tin-halide perovskite LEDs are substantially more mature than blue devices. Propose a blue-emitter strategy based on wide-bandgap composition, strong or quasi-2D confinement, and interface engineering. Explain how the design should avoid Sn2+ oxidation, deep defects, mixed-halide segregation, inefficient energy funneling, and insulating-ligand transport barriers, and define a staged qualification plan.

Selective excitation of a perovskite/organic-semiconductor heterojunction produces rapid decay of the perovskite bleach and growth of a new broad transient feature in the organic layer. Determine whether the interface undergoes charge transfer, Förster-type energy transfer, or a field-induced electroabsorption response. Design spectral-basis, spacer-thickness, excitation-wavelength, bias, and device-output controls and state the decisive kinetic signatures.

A volatile carbonyl additive improves residual strain, film photoluminescence, and flexible-device voltage. Design a factorial experiment across substrates with different thermal-expansion coefficients and across controlled cooling rates to determine how much of the electrical benefit is causally mediated by stress release rather than by crystallization or chemical passivation. State the interaction patterns and measurements expected for each mechanism.

A vapor-deposited bulky-ammonium treatment is applied to an inverted 3D perovskite in a dose series. At low dose, open-circuit voltage and absolute photoluminescence quantum yield rise, but fill factor changes little. At an intermediate dose, voltage remains high while fill factor, cross-plane current, and contacted-stack carrier extraction all improve. At high dose, low-angle layered-perovskite diffraction and an excitonic absorption feature become obvious, while short-circuit current and fill factor collapse. Construct a process-structure-property interpretation of this non-monotonic response. Specify the measurements needed to distinguish useful surface passivation and vertically compatible transport from Br alloying, bulk low-dimensional conversion, incomplete coverage, or formation of a continuous transport barrier.

Develop an accelerated-lifetime framework for a sealed iodide-perovskite device whose catastrophic failure involves four coupled processes: stochastic lesion nucleation, iodine-assisted lateral propagation, volatile escape or capture, and top-electrode rupture after pressure buildup. Explain why a single Arrhenius extrapolation of T80 is not physically defensible. Define the minimum factorial stress program, observables, model structure, and field-extrapolation criteria.

A dual-interface Sn-Pb perovskite device uses a top post-treatment and a buried-interface precursor additive. It retains more than 80% of initial efficiency for a limited maximum-power-point test in nitrogen, but longer operation produces VOC loss near the top contact and fill-factor loss beginning at the acidic polymer bottom contact. Build a degradation-attribution protocol that determines whether the two modifiers remain protective or merely delay Sn oxidation, ion migration, and contact deterioration. Specify the control ladder, stress separation, depth-resolved diagnostics, and redesign logic.

A dopant-free polymer HTL device remains stable in dark humidity storage but loses fill factor rapidly during 85 °C one-sun maximum-power-point operation. VOC and absorber QFLS initially remain high. Construct a failure-analysis program that distinguishes polymer morphological relaxation, loss of interfacial selectivity, Au migration, perovskite ion redistribution, polymer photo-oxidation, and residual-solvent effects. Explain which observations would show that dopant-free humidity stability does not translate into operational stability.

A wide-bandgap device with a surface 2D/3D heterostructure shows excellent nitrogen shelf stability and outdoor module retention, yet its one-sun maximum-power-point T80 remains only a few hundred hours. Build an operando failure tree that separates bulk mixed-halide phase segregation, reconstruction or dissolution of the ultrathin 2D layer, buried-SAM degradation, electron-contact reactions, and Ag/halide chemistry. Define the layer-ablation controls, spatial probes, and mechanism-specific acceptance criteria.

A semi-transparent photovoltaic window is optimized at normal incidence and has acceptable PCE, 30% photopic AVT, and near-neutral CIE coordinates. When installed on a façade, observers report strong color changes at oblique viewing angles even though normal-incidence AVT remains unchanged. Explain why this can occur in multilayer polymer or perovskite cells. Develop an angle-resolved optical and device-design strategy that preserves daylight color while retaining near-infrared harvesting and electrical output.

A buried-interface coordinator produces vertically oriented, lower-strain perovskite grains and improves initial light stability. During combined illumination and forward bias, however, a later-generation mixed-halide version develops a slow red-shifting PL shoulder while XRD orientation remains unchanged. Construct a failure diagnosis that explains how an interface that improves crystallographic order can still permit halide redistribution. Specify tests that distinguish bulk phase segregation, field-driven interfacial ion accumulation, and chemical decomposition of residual PbI2.

During maximum-power-point operation at elevated temperature, an inverted perovskite cell first loses Voc within tens of minutes while the quasi-Fermi-level splitting of an absorber recovered after contact removal remains unchanged. Hours later, fill factor decreases, hysteresis becomes strong, and part of the loss recovers after dark rest. XRD shows no new bulk phase. Develop a sequential failure model that distinguishes newly generated interface recombination, reversible ionic field screening, and irreversible contact or electrode degradation. Specify the stress perturbations and operando or post-mortem signatures that would establish the order of events rather than merely correlate them.

A PACl-modified inverted CsPbI3 device remains stable during inert light soaking but degrades during combined humidity and thermal cycling. The bulk gamma-CsPbI3 diffraction pattern remains largely unchanged, while surface Cl and organic-N signals decrease, contact resistance rises, and Voc loss precedes fill-factor loss. Construct a failure tree that distinguishes loss or redistribution of the surface treatment, renewed CsPbI3/PCBM energy mismatch, PCBM/BCP/Ag degradation, and incipient bulk phase instability. State the decisive measurements and recovery or replacement tests for each branch.

An unencapsulated inverted MAPbI3 cell initially stores better than a doped-hole-conductor normal cell, but under humid illumination it later loses Voc and fill factor. Develop a side-specific failure analysis that distinguishes hygroscopic or acidic PEDOT:PSS damage, MAPbI3 volatile-component loss, PCBM oxidation or delamination, and Au/halide interdiffusion. Specify material-substitution controls, ingress localization, and recovery tests that establish which layer provided the early benefit and which layer limits long-term operation.

During light and bias aging of a quasi-2D perovskite device, the initially productive high-current domains gradually disappear and Jsc and fill factor decline, while average XRD and whole-film PLQY remain nearly constant. Construct a spatial failure model that distinguishes loss of percolation connectivity, strain relaxation and reorganization of n phases, halide or cation redistribution, local non-radiative hot spots, and contact delamination. State the same-location measurements and reversibility tests needed to explain why average optical and structural metrics remain insensitive.

A large-area two-step perovskite process deliberately leaves a small amount of PbI2 near the electron-selective contact because this can passivate the buried interface. Two modules show the same total residual-PbI2 signal by bulk XRD, yet one remains stable while the other develops voltage loss and shunts during 85 °C humidity-biased operation. Formulate a process-control and qualification strategy that distinguishes beneficial, spatially confined PbI2 from random or excess PbI2. Include precursor-aging controls, spatial/depth-resolved acceptance metrics, and a go/no-go rule for module production.

A coherent PbS–FAPbI3 heterostructure uses moderate compressive strain to stabilize the photoactive black phase at room temperature. During repeated −20 to 85 °C cycling, diffraction shows reversible lattice expansion at first, then irreversible relaxation, while the device develops hysteresis and microcracks near the heterointerface. Explain the coupled failure sequence and propose a redesign that preserves phase stabilization without accumulating damaging stress. State the measurements needed to choose among a lattice-matched substrate, a compliant buffer, and a van der Waals template.

A high-throughput computational screen ranks a lead-free A2B'B''X6 double perovskite as an excellent photovoltaic absorber because it has a calculated 1.40 eV fundamental band gap, low decomposition energy, and no deep intrinsic defects in the ideal crystal. Experimentally, dense films show weak absorption near 1.40 eV, strong absorption only above 2 eV, low external quantum efficiency, and low current despite long photoluminescence lifetime. Explain why the computational ranking can fail. Propose a revised down-selection workflow that tests optical selection rules, excitons, transport connectivity, defect chemistry, oxidation-state stability, morphology, and interfaces.

In a zero-bias perovskite–BiVO4 artificial leaf, replacing the Cu–In cathode catalyst with a catalyst that has twice the partial current for CO at −0.4 V versus RHE produces almost no increase in the tandem operating current or solar-to-fuel rate. The photovoltaic subcell, photoanode, and electrolyte are nominally unchanged. Explain why the catalyst improvement may not translate to the integrated device. Design a diagnostic sequence based on component polarization curves, series resistance, mass transport, local pH, and product faradaic efficiency.

A plasma-sprayed MAPbI3 film has a fracture energy about an order of magnitude above a spin-coated control because of its bimodal grain structure. Flexible modules made from the same process nevertheless fail rapidly during damp-heat bending tests. Explain why high fracture energy does not establish operational durability. Design a coupled mechanical-environmental qualification program that determines whether the bimodal microstructure is beneficial, neutral, or harmful under realistic service conditions.

A grain-boundary treatment decreases trap-assisted recombination, raises photoluminescence quantum yield, and improves initial Voc. Unexpectedly, infrared thermography shows that the treated device operates several degrees hotter at maximum power, even though recombination heat should be lower. Construct a multi-physics diagnosis that distinguishes reduced thermal conductivity, increased parasitic absorption, altered current density or contact resistance, and a measurement artifact. Explain how the hotter operating state could change the long-term interpretation of the passivation benefit.

A sulfurized ABS3 film has an ellipsometric “direct gap” of 2.0 eV and a PL peak at 1.9 eV, giving a small Stokes shift. The film is textured and contains 5-10 at.% oxygen. Design an optical and transport diagnosis that determines whether the 2.0 eV edge is a true fundamental band-to-band transition and whether the small Stokes shift genuinely indicates a useful absorber rather than oxide contamination, excitonic emission, or defect-selective luminescence.

A vapour-deposited perovskite film shows Drude-like terahertz photoconductivity and an apparent bimolecular recombination coefficient about five orders of magnitude below the Langevin value inferred from its mobility. Design a study that distinguishes intrinsically non-Langevin electron-hole recombination from three alternative causes: spatial electron-hole separation, rapid trapping into THz-invisible states, and bias from a nonuniform excitation-depth profile. Predict the key signatures for each explanation.

A research program can fund only one major next experiment for an all-perovskite tandem platform: a six-month pilot-line yield campaign, a two-year outdoor reliability campaign, a redesign replacing an expensive evaporated contact, or a 1.5 percentage-point efficiency program. Develop a value-of-information framework that selects the experiment most likely to reduce commercial LCOE risk. Specify the model inputs, decision thresholds, and conditions under which each option would be preferred. Do not assume that the largest nominal LCOE sensitivity automatically identifies the best experiment.

During light soaking, a reference perovskite device shows a gradual work-function drift across an internal perovskite/perovskite homojunction, followed by increased interfacial roughness, local PbI2 enrichment, and eventual fill-factor loss. A modified device suppresses all four changes. Construct a mechanistic sequence that explains how an initially electrical discontinuity can evolve into mechanical and chemical failure. Then define experiments that establish the direction of causality rather than treating work-function drift, roughening, and PbI2 as interchangeable degradation markers.

Transfer the bifunctional-ligand concept from an FAPbI3/SnO2 n-i-p cell to a narrow-bandgap mixed Sn-Pb perovskite used in an inverted tandem. The new buried contact is a hole-selective self-assembled monolayer rather than SnO2, and Sn2+ oxidation is a dominant risk. Define how the ligand's two functional ends, segregation behavior, and processing window should be redesigned. Specify the controls needed to show that orientation control and buried-interface passivation remain beneficial rather than accelerating oxidation, creating a transport barrier, or disrupting tandem current matching.

A dopant-free polymer hole contact is stable in short inert-storage tests but will be used in a flexible nanocrystal module exposed to 85 °C thermal cycling. Identify the coupled failure modes involving the polymer, the ligand-stripped CsPbI3 nanocrystal solid, and the MoO3/metal contact. Propose a stress-and-diagnostics sequence that distinguishes chemical depassivation, thermomechanical cracking, and contact-energy drift.

A two-terminal perovskite/silicon tandem is intentionally bottom-cell current limited by about 0.5 mA cm−2 under standard test conditions. The top cell uses a passivating precursor additive and sparse dielectric nanoparticles that improve voltage and fill factor but also change film thickness and parasitic optics. Determine whether the same current-mismatch setting maximizes annual energy yield under variable spectra and temperature. Design the modeling and experimental workflow, and define the metric that should replace champion PCE as the optimization target.

CsPbI2Br devices with a compact TiO2 electron contact still lose performance under ultraviolet exposure. Determine whether the dominant UV failure originates from TiO2 photocatalysis, direct perovskite photochemistry, or UV-accelerated ion migration at the interface. Propose a minimal contact-and-spectrum matrix and specify the signatures that distinguish the three pathways.

A shallow iodine interstitial is proposed to catalyze α-to-δ phase nucleation even though it introduces little immediate deep-gap recombination. Predict how this failure mechanism should appear under electrical bias in the dark and under illumination. Design an operando experiment that separates defect-driven structural nucleation from ordinary reversible halide migration and from PbI2-forming decomposition.

An all-quantum-dot CsPbI3 solar cell retains its black phase and initial efficiency for months in dry dark storage. Under one-sun operation at elevated temperature, however, the device first develops a broadened and red-shifted PL spectrum, increasing hysteresis, and slower extraction; only later do XRD and microscopy show larger crystallites and nonperovskite domains. Construct a coupled failure mechanism involving ligand dynamics, interdot coupling, ion redistribution, and quantum-dot coarsening. Which time-resolved measurements would distinguish reversible electronic disorder from irreversible sintering or phase conversion, and why is dark shelf stability an insufficient qualification metric?

A slot-die-coated perovskite module has uniform average XRD, thickness, and initial efficiency, yet damp-heat aging produces narrow low-PL bands aligned with regions that dried last. Chemical analysis of failed bands finds residual coordinating solvent and a higher density of deep traps, while the module average composition remains nominal. Construct the failure sequence from heterogeneous intermediate conversion to moisture-assisted device decay. Explain why average in-line metrics can miss the relevant risk, and define the process and diagnostic changes needed to eliminate the low-conversion tail rather than merely improve the mean film quality.

A peroxide-passivated perovskite initially shows high PLQY and low nonradiative recombination, but the benefit decays during 85 °C storage without a large immediate change in bulk XRD. Construct three distinguishable failure hypotheses: reversible loss or reduction of passivating Pb–O species, latent overoxidation that creates new defects, and thermally activated redistribution of the oxidized surface layer. Specify the recovery tests, isotope/chemical measurements, and optical or electrical signatures that would identify each pathway.

An APTES-protected, tBP-degassed n-i-p device retains most of its efficiency during 1000 h at 85 °C in dark nitrogen, yet the remaining decay is dominated by fill-factor loss with a smaller Voc loss. Construct a postulated failure tree that begins after the interfacial radical-cation recombination center has been suppressed. Include LiTFSI redistribution, HTL morphology or conductivity changes, silane condensation/desorption, contact resistance, and metal-electrode reactions. Which time-resolved and post-mortem measurements would rank these branches and show whether APTES delays failure or merely changes its dominant mode?

A tripodal monolayer device survives brief 120–130 °C heat pulses and retains high output during a 100 h inert-atmosphere MPP test. During longer light-bias operation, however, Voc and fill factor decay while average monolayer loading and bulk perovskite XRD remain nearly constant. Construct a plausible buried-interface failure sequence involving monolayer reorientation or patch formation, charge accumulation, ion migration, and TCO/perovskite reactions. Explain why short heat tests and average loading cannot exclude this pathway, and specify the spatial and operando evidence needed to prove or falsify it.

A planar-core HTM device retains 94% of its efficiency after 1000 h of 1-sun MPP operation at 65 °C in nitrogen. When transferred to humid air with the same temperature and bias, the device instead shows an early fill-factor decline, followed by Voc loss and later PbI2 growth. Construct the additional failure sequence introduced by oxygen and water, considering HTM oxidation or crystallization, interfacial wetting, ion migration, and Cu-electrode reactions. Define the controls needed to determine whether planarity remains protective or becomes a morphology-driven liability outside inert conditions.

A humid-air-stressed FA-rich perovskite film can be partially restored by supplying formamidinium iodide vapor at mild temperature, but only when the stress is stopped early. Films stressed longer retain iodate-rich surface residues, voids, and nonperovskite Cs- and FA-rich phases even after replenishment. Explain the reversible-to-irreversible transition and design a materials strategy that delays the tipping point. Your answer must distinguish stoichiometric depletion, phase segregation, framework loss, and interfacial transport damage, and must define an accelerated test that proves the intervention interrupts the degradation loop rather than merely re-blackening the film.

A cation-size-engineered all-iodide perovskitoid is stable under continuous light at room temperature, but accelerated thermal cycling causes gradual peak splitting, increased PL heterogeneity, and a loss of fill factor without a large change in the average optical gap. Propose a failure mechanism and a transferable composition-processing strategy for widening the phase-stability window. Address unequal cation mobility, local connectivity changes, face-sharing/corner-sharing interconversion, strain, and the possibility that average diffraction and bandgap measurements hide nanoscale phase separation. Define the experiments and acceptance criteria needed before extending the design rule to a new spacer-cation family.

Across an n=3 layered lead-iodide series, replacing an allyl spacer with an iodine-functionalized spacer simultaneously increases octahedral distortion, increases interlayer separation and polarizability, accelerates band-edge depletion, and strengthens broad sub-bandgap emission. Design a causal strategy to determine whether the deep emissive state is controlled primarily by inorganic-lattice distortion or by dielectric/interlayer effects of the organic spacer. Your answer should use matched spacer analogues, hydrostatic or uniaxial pressure, temperature, polarization-resolved spectroscopy, and structural calculations, and should specify the result pattern expected for each mechanism.

A perovskite device under steady forward bias exhibits a superlinear degradation rate: modest hole accumulation initially shortens the carrier lifetime, then ion redistribution accelerates, and the rising nonradiative loss requires still higher injection to maintain the same light output. Build a coupled kinetic feedback model for this behavior and identify experimentally accessible early-warning observables. Then propose an operating and materials strategy that breaks the feedback without relying solely on a thicker transport layer or a lower average current density.

A two-dimensional perovskite heterostructure is required to preserve an atomically sharp Br/I junction under operating bias, but ion migration is observed to initiate at sheet edges and junction corners. Propose an edge-engineering strategy that suppresses the fast ionic channel while preserving lateral electronic transport and optical access. Compare chemical edge passivation, physical edge encapsulation, increased layer number, and junction-geometry redesign. Define experiments that determine whether a higher migration threshold represents genuine suppression or merely delayed field concentration and catastrophic degradation.

An unencapsulated perovskite/silicon tandem built on an optimized TOPCon bottom cell shows an early burn-in followed by slower decay under one-sun operation in nitrogen. Develop a failure-analysis protocol that distinguishes perovskite ion migration and selective-contact degradation from loss of hydrogen passivation or oxide/contact evolution in the silicon bottom cell. State the stress splits, reversible signatures, and layer-resolved measurements required before blaming the new TOPCon process.

A retained polymer-perovskite grain-boundary bridge improves moisture, heat, and light stability in a rigid small-area cell. Predict the new failure modes that may appear when the same composite is used in a flexible module subjected to repeated bending, damp-heat exposure, and thermal cycling. Develop a qualification matrix that determines whether the polymer acts as a mechanically beneficial bridge, a water-plasticized ionic pathway, or a brittle constraint that transfers stress into the perovskite.

During maximum-power operation, a dual host-guest interface slowly loses voltage but recovers after dark storage. Develop a failure diagnosis that distinguishes reversible host/guest redistribution or decomplexation from irreversible molecular decomposition, loss of surface passivation, and transport-layer degradation. Include the bias, temperature, and compositional signatures expected for each case.

After 500 h of operation, a particle-decorated fully textured tandem loses performance while cross-sections remain largely conformal. Residual PbI2 is suspected. Develop a spatial failure hypothesis linking particle-assisted nucleation to local stoichiometric or phase reservoirs, and design a postmortem study that determines whether PbI2 is protective, electrically harmful, or a degradation product. Propose process changes that preserve conformality.

A mixed Sn–Pb low-bandgap perovskite is treated with a surface diammonium iodide that raises PLQY and quasi-Fermi-level splitting, but stronger treatment also increases scan-rate-dependent hysteresis. A second bulk additive contains a hydrogen-bonding cation and chloride. After adding it, electronic trap density falls only modestly, yet the ion-migration activation energy rises by more than an order of magnitude and forward/reverse scans nearly coincide. Construct a kinetic explanation that separates electronic passivation from ionic immobilization. Predict the signatures expected in (i) bias-pulse current relaxation, (ii) temperature-dependent hysteresis, (iii) light-versus-dark preconditioning, and (iv) depth-resolved ion profiles if the interpretation is correct.

After a strain-relief treatment, a perovskite film shows the following apparently conflicting changes: the average TRPL lifetime of a perovskite/HTL stack becomes much shorter, the transient photocurrent extraction time becomes shorter, the transient photovoltage lifetime becomes longer, and the device ideality factor approaches unity. Reconcile all four observations without invoking measurement error. Explain what each experiment probes, what boundary condition changes between them, and why a single statement such as “longer lifetime means better material” is inadequate.

A bifunctional molecule is blended into a semicrystalline polymer hole-transport layer. One end coordinates under-coordinated lead at the perovskite surface and the other interacts with the polymer backbone. A separately deposited molecular interlayer improves the device, but the blend performs substantially better and exhibits an optimum at intermediate molecular concentration. Build a thermodynamic and kinetic explanation for this hierarchy. Predict what happens to interfacial coverage, polymer ordering, vertical composition, conductivity and recombination below and above the optimum.

A planar n–i–p perovskite cell shows decreasing hysteresis as the electron mobility of its SnO2-based contact is raised toward the effective hole-extraction mobility of the opposite contact. Explain why hysteresis should depend on carrier-flux balance rather than on maximizing electron mobility without limit. Predict the non-monotonic failure modes expected if electron mobility, contact work function or interfacial selectivity is pushed too far, and identify the impedance and scan-rate signatures that distinguish flux balancing from simple trap passivation.

Two quasi-two-dimensional perovskite films contain the same total fractions of low-n and high-n phases, have similar out-of-plane crystal orientation, and show nearly identical steady-state PL and average TRPL lifetime. Their only deliberate difference is the vertical phase order in an n-i-p device: Film A places more low-n, wide-gap material near the hole-selective top contact and more high-n, narrow-gap material near the electron-selective bottom contact, whereas Film B reverses this gradient. Explain why the two films can nevertheless show different short-circuit current, fill factor, and non-radiative voltage loss. Predict the most diagnostic changes under front-side versus back-side excitation and after swapping the selective-contact polarity.

A size series of hybrid FAPbBr3 quantum dots grows from 8 to 18 nm edge length, yet simulations and spectroscopy suggest that the thermally localized electron-hole wavefunction remains confined to roughly a nanometre-scale region at room temperature. A size-matched CsPbBr3 control instead shows electronic extent that grows with physical dot size. Predict how biexciton lifetime, g2(0), exciton brightness, and their temperature dependence should scale with dot size if phonon-driven dynamic localization, rather than ordinary geometric confinement, controls single-photon purity.

A new spacer gives a high charge-separation descriptor, a large in-plane Pb-I-Pb angle, and high in-plane hole mobility in an n=1 single crystal. In an n=4 thin film, however, out-of-plane mobility is unchanged and the solar-cell fill factor improves only slightly. Explain how both results can be scientifically consistent. Propose an additional descriptor and a transfer-validation workflow that determine when the charge-separation descriptor is useful for a vertically operating photovoltaic device and when it is insufficient.

Two endotaxial mixed-halide nanocrystal composites have the same guest-domain radius, composition, matrix structure, and interface density. Composite L has a 70 ns photoluminescence lifetime and fewer non-radiative traps; Composite S has a 20 ns lifetime. Under the same absorbed optical power, L develops a segregation-related red-shift sooner than S. Explain why this result would not necessarily contradict the confinement mechanism. Analyse the competition between trap passivation, steady-state carrier density, carrier-induced demixing free energy, and nucleation, and design measurements at matched carrier density rather than matched incident power.

The excitation-density-dependent PL blue shift of FASnI3 is about twice as large at 24 K as at 293 K. Explain why this does not automatically mean that hot carriers cool more slowly at 24 K. Use band filling, carrier-density calibration, effective mass, Fermi-Dirac broadening, disorder, and time resolution to state what would and would not be inferred from the larger steady-state spectral shift.

A candidate perovskite module combines Cs-substituted FA perovskite, a grain-boundary treatment, hydrophobic charge-selective contacts, and edge encapsulation. It survives 1,000 hours of open-circuit light soaking but fails rapidly during damp heat under load and develops local hysteresis before visible delamination. Construct a stress-and-diagnostics programme that identifies whether the first limiting process is absorber phase instability, grain-boundary ion transport, buried-interface chemistry, contact degradation, or encapsulation leakage. Explain why the open-circuit result cannot be used as a universal lifetime claim.

Two inverted perovskite devices have the same fresh efficiency. During repeated -40 °C to 85 °C cycling, one first develops intermittent fill-factor loss and local electroluminescence dark spots that partly disappear at room temperature; later it shows permanent voids and delamination. Develop a time-resolved failure model that separates reversible molecular disorder, irreversible molecular desorption, thermomechanical crack initiation, buried-interface recombination, and bulk absorber degradation. Which hold tests and interrupted-cycle measurements establish the sequence?

An all-perovskite tandem made from close-space-annealed subcells operates well initially. During prolonged maximum-power tracking, tandem current slowly falls while total Voc remains nearly constant; spatially averaged PL shows no clear peak splitting. Develop a subcell-resolved failure analysis that distinguishes delayed residual-solvent damage, Sn-Pb bottom-cell oxidation, wide-bandgap halide segregation confined to small regions, recombination-junction degradation, and simple current mismatch. State the measurements needed to identify the first failing layer.

A chelate-treated Sn-Pb cell is stable during continuous warm maximum-power operation but degrades during combined humidity and thermal cycling. Early maps show isolated low-QFLS spots; later, Sn4+ rises near those spots and the C60 contact resistance increases. Develop a failure sequence that distinguishes chelate desorption or dissolution, mechanical cracking of the low-dimensional barrier, oxygen/water penetration, renewed Sn-rich surface exposure, and a direct chelate-C60 reaction. Which interrupted-stress controls determine the initiating event?

A reinforced perovskite minimodule survives a single prolonged partial-shading test, but repeated short shading transients over months produce gradually increasing leakage without catastrophic breakdown. Some leakage relaxes overnight, while a persistent component co-localizes with hot spots near interconnect edges. Construct a failure model that separates reversible ionic polarization, cumulative iodine-Cu chemistry, local Joule heating, interconnect or scribe damage, and incipient filament formation. Define the waveform and diagnostics needed for an accelerated but mechanism-faithful test.

A graded electron-acceptor junction is to be rebuilt with a non-fullerene molecular acceptor that has a deeper electron affinity, stronger visible absorption, lower molecular diffusivity, and less isotropic electron transport than PCBM. Define the desired vertical concentration and orientation profile, the principal failure modes, and a screening workflow that determines whether the new acceptor can shorten collection distance without increasing optical loss, hole leakage, energetic trapping, or crystallization damage.

A strongly out-of-plane-oriented perovskite film is proposed for a flexible device. The texture reduces electronic disorder, but anisotropic thermal expansion and coherent vertical grain boundaries may concentrate stress during bending and thermal cycling. Develop a qualification and redesign strategy that determines whether the same orientation that improves charge transport also creates a mechanical reliability penalty. Include texture controls, substrate choices, operando measurements, and a decision rule.

The same paired-ion stabilizer is proposed for an air-processed 1.80 eV mixed-halide perovskite. It may suppress iodine oxidation but also change Br/I precursor speciation, introduce a mobile A-site cation, or alter the driving force for light-induced halide segregation. Develop a composition-specific transfer plan that separates initial manufacturing benefit from long-term mixed-halide instability. Include dose selection, chemical and structural diagnostics, and operational rejection criteria.

A near-surface wider-bandgap gradient that repels electrons is beneficial when it lies next to a hole-selective contact in an n-i-p perovskite cell. You must transfer the concept to an inverted p-i-n architecture, where the treated top surface is adjacent to an electron-selective contact. Explain why copying the same gradient may reduce rather than improve performance, and propose two physically distinct redesigns that preserve low interfacial recombination while maintaining electron collection. Define the measurements that would distinguish successful selectivity engineering from passivation that merely lengthens film photoluminescence lifetime.

A vacancy-rich FA-Cs perovskite device degrades strongly during open-circuit light soaking, while a sub-percent A-site iodide excess suppresses the failure. Predict how the defect and ion-migration signatures could differ under open circuit, maximum-power-point operation, and short circuit when photon dose and temperature are matched. Then design a protocol that identifies whether the excess salt prevents a universal absorber defect cycle or only a bias-specific failure of hole extraction.

A 1.3 eV tin-iodide perovskite is being developed as the bottom absorber of an all-perovskite tandem. Bulk bromide alloying raises voltage and fill factor but also widens the bandgap and sacrifices near-infrared current. Propose a device and materials strategy that increases the bottom-cell voltage without relying on substantial bulk bromide incorporation. Explain how you would allocate improvements among defect chemistry, interfaces, optical thickness and contact selectivity, and define the measurements that show voltage was gained without losing the low-bandgap function.

A zero-bias perovskite single-crystal imager is limited by approximately 100 micrometres of lateral charge-cloud spreading. You want to strengthen carrier drift and reduce spreading without applying an external high field that would trigger ionic instability. Propose a built-in-field engineering strategy using contacts, doping or junction geometry. Explain the trade-offs with injection noise, depletion width, recombination and chemical stability, and define how to verify that resolution improves for the intended reason.

A team proposes adding a third junction to a high-performing perovskite/silicon tandem. Formulate a decision rule for when the extra junction increases real device efficiency and annual energy yield rather than merely raising the detailed-balance limit. Include bandgap allocation, spectral/current matching, added optical and interconnect losses, processing damage, area scaling and stability. Define the minimum simulation and experimental evidence required before committing to the three-junction architecture.

A wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskite for a tandem cell suffers light-induced halide segregation. A candidate cyclic amidinium A-cation is less volatile and more hydrophobic than MA, has a similar effective size to FA, and forms stronger directional hydrogen bonds, but complete substitution reduces solubility and produces low-dimensional inclusions. Design a composition and processing strategy that uses this cation without sacrificing three-dimensional transport. Explain how you would determine whether any stability improvement comes from modified lattice dynamics, reduced ion migration, or merely formation of a blocking surface phase.

Two perovskite films have the same composition, average crystal symmetry and mean metal-halide-metal bond angle. Total-scattering analysis nevertheless shows that film A contains long-range-correlated octahedral tilts, whereas film B has tilts of similar amplitude but random orientation beyond one or two unit cells. Film A exhibits anisotropic mobility and a sharper absorption edge; film B has nearly isotropic but lower mobility and a larger Urbach energy. Explain why the correlation of octahedral distortions, not only their mean amplitude, can produce these differences. Propose an evidence strategy that rules out texture, grain size and defect density as simpler explanations.

Two encapsulation schemes give similar water-vapour transmission rates, yet perovskite devices protected by scheme A develop reversible performance loss after humid ageing, whereas scheme B shows slower but irreversible decay. Design an isotope-enabled NMR workflow using labelled water or deuterium that distinguishes reversible hydration, proton/deuteron exchange, organic-cation loss and irreversible decomposition. Explain how the results would be converted into a module-level encapsulation acceptance rule rather than remaining a qualitative spectroscopy study.

Semiconductors A and B show the same room-temperature photoluminescence lifetime at low excitation. Under high injection and elevated temperature, A retains its lifetime and voltage, whereas B develops strong non-radiative loss. First-principles calculations predict that A has more numerous but shallow defects; B has fewer defects, including one deep level with a large lattice relaxation. Explain why the low-injection lifetime does not establish equal defect tolerance. Design a minimum experiment-and-theory set that distinguishes defect concentration, trap energetics, capture coefficients, charge-state transitions and dynamic screening.

A perovskite-organic tandem is initially current matched, but during outdoor ageing the organic subcell undergoes rapid burn-in and then stabilizes, while the perovskite subcell loses current slowly and continuously. The tandem power therefore declines nonlinearly even though neither subcell has failed catastrophically. Design an energy-yield-oriented architecture and qualification method that manages this moving current mismatch. Your proposal must address absorber selection, optical design, recombination contact, recoverable versus irreversible ageing, and why optimizing initial efficiency alone can select the wrong stack.

An inverted p-i-n perovskite cell uses NiOx as the hole contact. A stronger oxidative surface treatment increases the measured work function and improves wetting, but devices show lower open-circuit voltage, faster interfacial photoluminescence quenching and a growing PbI2-rich signal at the buried interface. A mild molecular passivation step recovers part of the voltage without restoring the original work function. Explain the most likely interfacial chemistry and why faster PL quenching is not sufficient evidence of better hole extraction. Design measurements that separate favorable energetic alignment from redox-induced recombination and perovskite damage.

Three interface molecules have the same anchoring group and nearly identical calculated isolated-molecule dipole moments, yet they produce different contact work functions, coverage uniformity and device voltages. Their only designed difference is the length and rigidity of the molecular spacer. Explain how collective monolayer packing can override the isolated-molecule dipole. Design a causal experiment that separates molecular orientation, surface density, depolarization, defect passivation and contact morphology, and identify which measurements would justify a structure-property rule transferable beyond the three molecules.

A monolithic perovskite-silicon tandem module is stable under uniform illumination but develops localized hot spots and permanent power loss during repeated partial shading. Infrared imaging shows heating near cell-string edges; after the event, the perovskite top-cell spectrum is locally red-shifted, the recombination-contact resistance is higher, and the silicon subcell shows no bulk lifetime loss. Explain how current mismatch and reverse-bias stress can couple ionic redistribution, halide segregation and recombination-junction damage. Design tests that distinguish these mechanisms from a pre-existing shunt.

A perovskite light-emitting solar cell is placed in an optical microcavity. The cavity increases forward-direction electroluminescence intensity and narrows the emission spectrum, but short-circuit current under sunlight decreases even though the absorber composition and electronic contacts are unchanged. Explain this trade-off using optical reciprocity, angular and spectral selectivity, photon recycling and parasitic absorption. What measurements would determine whether the apparent light-emission gain reflects improved external extraction or only redistribution of photons into the collection angle?

A nominal single-n layered perovskite film gives one clean family of low-angle X-ray diffraction peaks and a narrow absorption onset. Nevertheless, its emission linewidth broadens on cooling, diffuse scattering appears between Bragg peaks, and cross-sectional electron microscopy suggests occasional changes in inorganic-slab spacing. Determine whether the film should still be called phase-pure. Explain how coherent intergrowths, stacking faults or RP/DJ-like local registry changes can evade conventional phase assignment, and design a characterization hierarchy that distinguishes a true single-n crystal population from a structurally disordered single-composition film.

A silicon tandem designer must choose between two MA-free top cells. Composition H has a 1.75 eV bandgap and gives better current matching in the reference spectrum, but shows a larger voltage deficit, stronger temperature dependence and slow light-induced halide redistribution. Composition L has a 1.68 eV bandgap, smaller voltage deficit and better phase stability, but limits the tandem current under the same reference spectrum. Develop a decision framework for field deployment rather than selecting the cell with the highest initial standard-test efficiency.

After prolonged 85 °C operation, a dipolar-passivated Pb-Sn narrow-bandgap cell retains most of its open-circuit voltage but develops a gradual fill-factor loss. The buried-interface work-function shift becomes spatially non-uniform, sulfanilic-acid fragments appear deeper in the absorber, and the Sn4+/Sn2+ ratio increases near the hole contact. Construct a coupled degradation mechanism and redesign the passivator/interface for thermal operation without losing its initial dipole and trap-passivation functions.

A square-centimetre wide-bandgap perovskite film has a uniform PL map before C60 deposition but develops spatially heterogeneous PL after C60. A tailored two-component 2D surface layer reduces that heterogeneity and improves average device yield. Design a spatially registered causal analysis that proves the post-C60 heterogeneity predicts local voltage or fill-factor loss rather than merely reflecting optical thickness, collection efficiency or benign PL variation.

A 1.9 eV-class mixed-halide perovskite containing a low fraction of a bromide-sized pseudohalide shows a higher quasi-Fermi-level splitting and device Voc. Design a stack-by-stack voltage-loss experiment that proves the dominant improvement is in the absorber bulk rather than at the hole contact, electron contact, or through a small bandgap/optical change. State the decisive controls and loss signatures.

After accumulated gamma irradiation, a zero-bias perovskite photon-counting detector shows a tenfold rise in dark-count rate, while average dark current, room-temperature PL intensity and the readout baseline remain nearly unchanged. Construct a radiation-damage analysis that separates newly created shallow traps, contact or shunt damage, scintillator/coupling degradation and electronics artefacts, and define a recovery or redesign pathway.

Strong (100) texture can change which crystallographic pathways connect the two electrodes. Develop an orientation-dependent stability study that determines whether oriented FAPbI3 suppresses or accelerates halide migration, moisture ingress and interfacial reactions compared with phase-pure isotropic material. Include field direction, exposed-facet and device-contact controls.

A green perovskite LED uses thermally assisted sub-bandgap carrier injection, so its electroluminescence at fixed voltage changes strongly with ambient temperature. Design a drive and qualification strategy for a wearable display that must maintain luminance and colour from 0 to 60 degrees Celsius without sacrificing the low-heating lifetime advantage.

A freshly processed 1.75-eV Br-I mixed-halide perovskite has a Br-richer top region and a less-Br-rich interior. With excitation from the top, its transient-absorption bleach shifts to lower energy by about 0.1 eV over hundreds of picoseconds; with excitation through the substrate, the shift is absent. Explain how to determine whether this behavior is benign carrier funneling through a pre-existing vertical bandgap gradient or the onset of light-induced halide phase segregation. Your diagnosis must use directionality, timescale, illumination-history dependence, and at least two independent composition or emission measurements.

A terpyridine-induced 0D surface reconstruction suppresses iodide migration in FAPbI3. A tandem team proposes applying the same treatment to a 1.75-eV Br-I mixed-halide top cell. Develop a go/no-go evaluation that addresses whether the treatment suppresses or instead redistributes halide segregation, alters Br/I surface stoichiometry, creates a carrier-extraction barrier, and compromises tandem current matching at module scale.

A narrow optimum in multiiodide dose improves initial device voltage, but residual redox-active iodine could become harmful during long-term operation. Design an accelerated reliability study that distinguishes durable stoichiometric defect repair from latent I2/I3− redox cycling, halide migration, and contact corrosion. Include additive-dose controls, stress modes, operando observables, post-mortem depth profiling, and a go/no-go criterion.
